description: Product scope, integration design and setup instructions. Check the documented implementation status.
text:
# Browser sign-in and your Claude Code / Codex activity

Implementation in the Texas readiness worktree. Live Texas deployment and real
Nomen account sign-in remain unverified.

The dashboard uses the existing Nomen dashboard public client with authorization
code + S256 PKCE. The Rust gateway exchanges the code and introspects the access
token before opening the same account-owned devspace used by the collector.
Neither the browser nor RROFLOW needs a Claude or Codex provider credential.

## Configuration on Texas

Keep the existing `[nomen]` configuration and provision its API key through the
operator's secrets mechanism. Add this block to the configuration retained by
the installer (`/etc/rroflow/nomen.toml`):

```toml
[browser]
origin = "https://app.rroflow.ai"
client_id = "396821568908492804"
```

Register the exact callback `https://app.rroflow.ai/auth/callback` on that public
client, with token endpoint authentication `none` and PKCE enabled. It must also
appear in `nomen.clients`. The service refuses insecure origins, and browser
sign-in requires one configured Nomen project audience. Without `[browser]`,
the UI says account sign-in is unavailable and retains the key entry.

Use the canonical app hostname: cookies are host-only, so signing in there does
not sign a browser into the API hostname. Both can reach the same Rust service.
Do not log query strings on `/auth/callback` in the reverse proxy: they contain
short-lived authorization codes. Tokens and callback responses are never logged
by this implementation.

## Session behavior

- Login transactions expire after ten minutes and are bound to a random browser
  cookie. A callback is single-use. State and PKCE are independently random.
- Access tokens stay in server memory. The browser receives an opaque
  `__Host-` cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/ and SameSite=Lax.
- API requests still pass through Nomen introspection and the existing
  account-to-devspace mapping. Cookie writes require the exact configured Origin
  and the dashboard's custom header. Collector bearer credentials remain supported.
- Sessions last at most the access token lifetime or one hour, whichever is
  shorter. They are bounded in number and cleared by server restart. This version
  does not request a refresh token; sign in again after expiry. Multiple service
  instances require sticky routing or a separately designed shared session store.
- Sign out invalidates the local session and pending login, and clears displayed
  data. It does not sign the user out of every Shippin service.
- Responses have `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

## Populate the owner's dashboard

On the computer running Claude Code and Codex, install the collector release,
run `rroflow login`, then `rroflow whoami`. Use the **same Shippin account** as
the browser. An ingest-key environment override takes precedence over login;
inspect `whoami` before sending, and remove that override if it names a different
devspace. Run the existing ingest commands with explicit session-directory paths:

```powershell
rroflow ingest-claude "$HOME/.claude/projects"
rroflow ingest-codex "$HOME/.codex/sessions"
```

Use the actual configured session folders when different. These commands upload
metrics and signal results; content is omitted unless `--content` is explicitly
chosen. They are one-shot imports; ongoing capture hooks and automatic discovery
are separate work. Refresh the dashboard to see both agents' received records.
No record means **no captured activity**, not proof of a provider connection.

Existing key-owned data needs the operator's explicit `rroflow-ingest claim`
operation after checking the account subject. Never assign the `jesse` devspace
automatically to the first user who signs in. Existing ownership/claim safeguards
remain in force.

## Proof required before calling it live

Run Rust tests (including Postgres/Nomen tests), dashboard state tests, formatting,
clippy and deployment preflight. Then verify on Texas: trusted VM identity,
app DNS/TLS, configured Nomen key/client/callback, real account sign-in,
same-owner Claude and Codex captures, second-account isolation, and sign-out.
The local OAuth transport test uses a test credential and mock token endpoint;
it does not claim real Nomen or Texas authentication.

Protocol references: [Zitadel endpoints](https://zitadel.com/docs/apis/openidoauth/endpoints)
and [frontend/backend audience scopes](https://zitadel.com/docs/guides/solution-scenarios/frontend-calling-backend-API).

text:
# Canon alignment notes for the RROFLOW mechanism spec

Date: 2026-10-24. Basis: the four project docs named below, read in full. Purpose: fix the vocabulary, the existing types RROFLOW builds on, the types it still lacks, and where the spec lands in the decided build order, so the mechanism records cannot drift from canon.

Sources: `claude/compute-and-data-workload-classification.md` (WC), `claude/rrflow-capability-study.md` (CS), `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` (BO), `claude/rrflow-definitions-and-schema-audit.md` (DA). Canon rule (DA, decided 2026-10-17): the latest explicit statement wins.

## 1. Terms the spec must use (and never rename)

| Term | Canonical meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| RRFlow / RRD | Reason Ready Flow, the engine and platform; Reason Ready Daemon = `rrd-server` + embedded `RrdEngine`, the only writer (ADR-0001) | DA §2 |
| estate / rrflowDB | one project's database, served by one instance; an account owns many estates; a workspace is a set of estates grouped above the engine (Decision 1) | DA §2, BO |
| RRO | Reason Ready Object: a persisted, versioned unit of knowledge RRFlow reasons over (record, relation, claim, vector, reasoning node); the retired provisioning-role sense is gone (PR #5/#6) | DA §2, C9 |
| RROFLOW | the recursive self-improvement configuration in which RROs improve themselves; a plug-in configuration with no roadmap owner yet; needs its own record before Gate G | DA §2, BO |
| LFG | deterministic kernel of compiled rules (no model, golden-file proven) + configured extension on escalate: tier 2 encoder and per-node classifiers on CPU, tier 3 a small CPU model or a remote model, all endpoint-bound; every answer carries value, probability, confidence, tier, provenance; SWAG decides, LFG suggests (Decision 3) | DA Decision 3 |
| SWAG | the System One controller and model gateway: decides, selects, dispatches through configured endpoints; needs its own record before Gate G | DA §2 |
| Governance | verification checks, permission gate, proof pattern (`verification_requirement` on terminal reasoning nodes) | DA §2, C10 |
| memory | rrflowDB's records, relations and bi-temporal claims; no second database | DA §3.5 |
| flight | a prompt flight: strict lifecycle record + events in one runtime commit; `flight-launch/list/read`; exact replay by session+key; `observe` arm with fresh/pruned context at one read stamp (PR #17) | BO |
| prompt-flight use edge | `rrflow-prompt-flight-used`, identity `<flight-id>.<rank>`, carries rank, fused score, avenues; written in the flight's commit (PR #18) | BO, DA §8 |
| task | named task record `rrflow-task` (title, goal, status) + `rrflow-task-includes` edge from a flight; `task_id` on flights (PR #19, Decision 16) | BO |
| context packet | `ContextPacket` with read stamp, evidence, evidence digest, packet digest | CS §3 |
| endpoint binding / profile / hardware inventory | `rrd-contract/src/endpoint_binding.rs` (PR #7): eight closed workload classes; kinds local, self-hosted, subscription, API; credential = Infisical secret name, never a value; declared footprint and limits; revisioned, digest-bound profiles with ordered fallbacks | WC, BO |
| workload class 7 | learning: behaviour updates — traces → signals → issues → experiments → changes to prompts, skills, routines, configs; evidence canonical, classifiers derived; little GPU. Class 6 = weight updates. Raindrop is the named class-7 reference | WC |
| prompt graphs | lexicon, evidence, source, knowledge (= memory), governance, classification, reasoning, plan/task; the set is configurable | project memory, 2026-10-19 |

Collision watch: BO mentions "generated SDK/signal surfaces" — the repo may already use "signal" for a generated surface. Verify in `rrflow-development` before the spec adopts Raindrop's "signal" unqualified; if it collides, the spec's term is **behaviour signal**.

## 2. Existing types RROFLOW builds on (do not reinvent)

- `Claim` with `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `tx_time`, `Tier`, `PromotionState` (`rrd-core/src/claim.rs`) — the shape for memory consolidation; nothing runs it (DA §3.5, §7).
- Flight record + events + use edges + task edges (PRs #17–#19) — the evidence graph of what a prompt used; `flight-read` cost is the flight's own size.
- Events key family 0x1f; commit/changefeed stream; audit chain (two control-journal entries per audited op — retention item) (DA §3.5, BO).
- Reasoning tree contract (A-02): nodes, typed edges, recipe, cursor, decision evidence, `verification_requirement`; frozen fixture, no persisted execution (DA §5).
- `EstateConfiguration` revisions (install-time only; step 2 adds edit/validate/activate/rollback) and the config-home rule: master copy lives in the instance store as UI-edited, versioned revisions; TOML is import/export (WC).
- Gate I (unbuilt): triggers, durable routines, skills; I-07 "reacts to recurring failure signals"; exit condition: automation explicit, bounded, replayable, removable, subordinate to `RrdEngine` — every self-improvement lands as a versioned, authorized, reversible change, never an automatic hook (BO).
- Gate G (unbuilt): G-04 commits recipe selection and branch navigation with the tree state (BO).
- Schema rule: `schemars` on `rrd-contract` → JSON Schema → OpenAPI, digest-pinned, five generated SDKs; schema-driven UI forms (WC, DA §3.7).

## 3. Types RROFLOW needs that do not exist yet

| Needed | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Answer (Gate, Choice, Score, Extract, Compose; probability, confidence, tier, provenance) | missing (v3 §3) | required by LFG and SWAG; waits per Decision 5 |
| Address (stable `CategoryId` segments, revision, 64-bit key, alias table) | PROPOSED, not ratified (v3 §5) | no contract built on it yet |
| Journal record / rule source / promotion | missing | name collision with `Claim.PromotionState` (claim tiers) must be resolved by naming |
| Check / Evaluator / Verdict | partial (`verification_requirement` only) | Governance |
| PermissionScope | missing | depends on Decision 1 (done) |

Consequence: the spec's mechanism records are design-time records with explicit dependencies on these types; they do not pretend the types exist.

## 4. Where this lands in the decided order

- BO: "SWAG record and RROFLOW record: before Gate G" — deferrable, named stage. Current order: 1 recoverability (served path done; D-11 open) → 2 config revisions → 2a Parquet → 2b benchmark harness → 2c speed wins (E-01, E-02, catalogue direct read) → 3 ingestion (embedding backend first) → 4 answers via bound endpoints → 5 prototype UI **and its Raindrop wiring pointed at RRFlow's HTTP API**. Decision 14 inside that: per-prompt graph + tasks → E-01 → folder → vector DB → real provider flights.
- WC open item 3: "Deep study of Raindrop's loop for class 7 design." This spec is that item.
- DA §7 placements, already decided: memory consolidation = RROFLOW's first mechanism; per-node classical classifiers belong to LFG's extension after the journal exists; rule promotion from reasoning traces ("the slow path mints fast paths") = RROFLOW, needs Answer, Address and journal types first.
- WC mapping already on record: signals ≈ configurable metrics; experiments ≈ eval arms; traces ≈ evidence graph; issue definitions ≈ lexicon and reasoning graph content. Raindrop is already wired into the rrflow-hydradb prototype (real events + feedback, read-back verified, TEAM.md 2026-10-12).

## 4b. What the repo already defines (checked on `main` `94d0567`, 2026-10-24 — PR #116; the project docs above stop at PR #28)

Sparse checkout at `canon/rrflow-development` (docs + `rrd-contract` + `rrd-core`). These are canon and the spec builds under them:

- **RROFLOW is defined** (`docs/architecture/system-overview.md` terminology row): "committed reasoning outcomes, verdicts, and corrections propose better rules, exemplars, claims or model candidates; each promotion is an authorized, versioned, reversible engine change, never an automatic hook. Unimplemented." Bound to G-06 (candidate qualification) and I-03/I-07 (governed improvement).
- **Learning contract exists**: `docs/reference/inference/learning/controller-training.md` (sources reviewed 2026-10-20). Loop: Outcomes → Candidate (rules/examples/model) → versioned Eval → authorized Shadow → exact Promotion proposal → `RrdEngine` admission + receipt → Active → Outcomes. Five stages with required evidence: observe/baseline, supervised improvement, unsupervised discovery, recursive improvement, promote/monitor. Hard rules: consent for training is separate from telemetry ("No dataset exists merely because a prompt flight was recorded"); Python cannot own runtime state or promotion; no second event store ("reuse the existing task/flight and causal evidence boundaries"); clustering is hypothesis, never verdict; held-out sets are versioned and never reused for tuning; replay-for-inspection ≠ re-invoking models. Raindrop Workshop and Arize Phoenix are cited as informing H-05/H-06 projections.
- **LFG/SWAG contract exists**: `docs/reference/inference/lfg-swag.md`. LFG = optional CPU analysis producing versioned observations (complexity, language, modality, task category) with declared units and confidence only when calibrated; deterministic rules admissible, learned classifier optional with pinned manifest. SWAG = policy over authorized endpoint candidates (modality, capacity, locality, quality floor, price ceiling, deadline, health) → proposal → engine recheck → dispatch → receipt. User-selected effort budgets (quick/balanced/thorough/custom) are required runtime behaviour. Note: the system-overview LFG row still says "whether a model runs inside it is undecided", lagging Decision 3 — a doc correction, not a conflict.
- **Prompt graph families are canon (H-09)**: `docs/reference/data/rrflowdb-capability.md` — lexicon, classification (Answer nodes with value, probability, confidence, tier, provenance), reasoning, plan/task, evidence (flight-used edges live), source, knowledge (= memory), governance (checks, verdicts, permission decisions). Definitions live in the schema registry; activation per project in the estate configuration revision; **experiments** = two or more arms (activation revisions), assignment rule, rubric, minimum sample, threshold; each flight records assignment, exposure and outcome as separate events; promotion = authorized reversible configuration revision.
- **Gate I RROFLOW packages** (`docs/roadmap/rrflow-1.0/gate-i.md`): "I-07 learning candidates" (a repeated failure proposes a bounded rule/example/model experiment with source and consent identities; clustering never a correctness verdict) and "I-03 RROFLOW promotion" (race two promotions, accept one; kill/restart matrix; duplicate receipt cannot deploy twice; rollback = new compatible revision). I-01 canonical engine-event envelope; I-02 triggers; I-03 routines; I-04 host-event adapters (Claude/OpenAI adapters, no automatic hooks).
- **"Signal" is taken.** `docs/reference/protocol/signal-catalogue.md` is the generated H-05 telemetry catalogue (diagnostic levels off/normal/detailed/profile; bounded metric dimensions; cardinality limit 2,000). Raindrop's "signal" (a learned behaviour classifier) therefore needs its own term in the spec. **D0 resolved by fact: use "behaviour signal"** (or a better name Jesse picks) and never bare "signal".
- **Still absent in the repo**: Answer and Address types, verdict/correction/dataset record kinds, any classifier representation, the experiment record, the engine-event envelope (I-01). The spec's records name these as dependencies, not as existing.

Consequence for the spec: it is the mechanism-level fill beneath the learning contract — for each Raindrop mechanism, what canon already covers, the gap, the proposed record in which family, the owning gate/package, and the fact Raindrop supplies that canon lacks. It does not restate the contract.

## 5. Standing constraints every mechanism record must satisfy

1. Nothing hardcoded beyond overridable defaults; today's hardcoded RRF constants (k = 60; weights 2.0/1.0/1.0/0.5) are the pattern to avoid, not follow (DA §3.7).
2. Every model and classifier reached through an endpoint binding; local vs remote changes no behaviour (WC).
3. Every change lands as a versioned, validated, activatable, rollback-able revision (WC "UI-managed"); automation subordinate to `RrdEngine` (Gate I).
4. Real instead of synthetic: planned states are labelled, never simulated (Jesse, 2026-10-18).
5. Built for scale: millions of records/vectors per estate; cost must not grow with estate history (POAM-028 is the anti-pattern).
6. Schema first: new types in `rrd-contract` with `schemars`; no standalone schemas outside it.
7. One PR per step, CI green, one journal under `docs/evidence/change-journals/`.
8. An ADR is canon only when saved through the interactive component.

text:
# AI capability baseline: Raindrop, Sentry, PostHog and RROFLOW

Updated 2026-10-28. Owner: this capability map. The minimum product target is the
AI-relevant capabilities of all three products, followed by enterprise datasets
and governed supervised/unsupervised learning. This is an implementation backlog,
not a statement that RROFLOW already has parity. No row is complete because a menu
item exists. Newly discovered capabilities must get a row and an acceptance gate;
this inventory is a maintained baseline, not proof of exhaustive product parity.

**Status:** tested = implementation with test evidence, partial = useful subset,
designed = owned contract without the complete worker/service, missing = not yet
implemented. All statuses concern development source. Texas deployment and real
member onboarding remain unverified. Test fixtures do not establish provider
compatibility or production scale.

## Sources and changed assumptions

- **R0:** [Raindrop documentation inventory](https://www.raindrop.ai/docs/llms.txt), inspected 2026-10-28: capture/integrations, platform, organization, query/MCP and privacy families.
- **R1:** [Signals](https://www.raindrop.ai/docs/platform/signals/): drafting, presets, instrumented checks, refinement, backfills and evidence navigation.
- **R2:** [Datasets](https://www.raindrop.ai/docs/platform/datasets/): collections of events/traces/uploaded rows, annotations and export.
- **R3:** [Dashboards](https://www.raindrop.ai/docs/platform/dashboards/): saved query panels and filter-preserving drill-downs.
- **S1:** [Sentry agent dashboards](https://docs.sentry.io/product/agents/dashboards/): overview/model/tool views and AI/full-trace navigation. Retrieved directly from the official site when the browsing extractor could not read its Markdown response.
- **P1:** [PostHog AI Observability](https://posthog.com/docs/ai-observability): trace/session context, costs, tools, feedback, replay/error links and query access.
- **P2:** [PostHog evaluations](https://posthog.com/docs/ai-evals): code/model/sentiment evaluations, backfills, trace reviews, datasets and offline experiments.
- **P3:** [PostHog product analytics](https://posthog.com/docs/product-analytics): trends, funnels, retention, paths, cohorts/identity, dashboards and experiment/flag correlation.
- **U1:** owner direction, 2026-10-28: these capabilities are a minimum for AI; clean drill-down dashboards, every signal, enterprise datasets and actual supervised/unsupervised evolution are essential.
- **H1:** all eight dated [Raindrop research notes](../README.md#research), plus the [DevPulse ledger](../research/devpulse/devpulse-research-ledger.md). Historical observations remain preserved rather than rewritten as current competitor claims.

The old comparison is superseded: Raindrop now documents coding-agent setup,
positive presets, dataset collections and custom dashboards. PostHog has online
and offline evaluations and datasets. These are baseline requirements, not gaps
we can claim competitors lack. RROFLOW's intended distinction must be demonstrated
through reliable source capture, account ownership, truthful coverage and governed
improvements. SDK, browser, mobile, managed-agent and subscription access are
separate surfaces; owning a subscription does not expose all its history.

## Capability inventory and acceptance gates

The source column names a capability family, not a claim that the products have
identical semantics. Supporting enterprise/platform requirements are explicit
RROFLOW obligations even where a competitor's detailed implementation has not yet
been investigated. No unverified competitor security claim is inferred.

| ID | Required capability | Basis | RROFLOW status / owning implementation | Evidence needed to close the gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Account-linked, system-wide coding-agent capture | R0, U1 | partial: CLI sources/startup | Real member links each supported source; work across projects reaches the same account |
| C02 | Provider/framework SDK wrappers | R0, P1 | partial: JavaScript Claude/Codex/Grok adapters | Normalize SDK journals into shared turn/trace/signal views; real streaming, tool, cancellation and error compatibility per SDK/version |
| C03 | HTTP, OTLP and import interoperability | R0, S1, P1 | partial: events/turn HTTP APIs; no general OTLP receiver | Versioned mappings, identity and finished-span validation; round-trip fixtures and real imports |
| C04 | Browser/mobile/remote execution capture | R0, U1 | partial: source-side collector independent of dispatcher | Explicit coverage per app; remote execution identity, offline replay and phone-disconnect proof |
| C05 | Durable delivery, retry, health and loss visibility | U1, H1 | partial: queue, cooldown, startup, source reports | Disk-full/backpressure, bounded retention, sustained load and gap accounting |
| C06 | Nested traces, handoffs, tool catalog and timing | R0, S1, P1 | partial: turns/tools/subagents and SDK journal | Full correlated waterfall, available-tool schemas, causal links and clock uncertainty |
| C07 | Private content, scrubbed projections and diagnostics | R0, H1 | partial: opt-in text, redaction, doctor | Member-editable policies, versioned redaction, leakage tests across every capture surface |
| C08 | Activity search, sessions and projects | R0, S1, P1 | tested: filtered/paginated turns and inspector | Model/tool/user/release/property dimensions, saved views and scalable query indexes |
| C09 | Readable conversation/tool/evidence drill-down | R1, S1, P1 | partial: turn inspector and pinned reviews | Correlated multi-turn/multi-agent trace view with deep links, missing-span states and keyboard paths |
| C10 | Built-in, custom and historical signals together | R1, H1 | tested: signal library, scoped custom predicates, recorded-definition fallback | Versioning/edit/archive/import and access controls; no lost historical interpretations |
| C11 | Signal trends and agent/project drill-downs | R1, R3, S1 | tested in this increment: full-cohort stats API and evidence links | Broader model/tool/release facets and production-scale latency evidence |
| C12 | Signal drafting from natural language | R1, H1 | designed: tier-3 candidate mechanism | Sandboxed candidate generation, preview coverage, human review and held-out gates |
| C13 | Semantic/example-trained classifiers and positive/negative mood | R1, P2, H1 | partial: deterministic mood; semantic tier designed | Label provenance, uncertainty, per-version evals and measured precision/recall |
| C14 | Instrumented feedback and agent self-diagnostics | R0, R1, P1 | partial: native SDK event journal | Typed outcome/feedback events, provenance, explicit semantics; self-reports are not truth labels |
| C15 | Backfill and re-evaluation | R1, P2 | missing: new custom signals do not scan history | Durable bounded jobs, frozen policy/version/scope, coverage and restart/retry accounting |
| C16 | Issue grouping, triage, ownership and lifecycle | R0, S1, H1 | partial: findings, no issue lifecycle | Group fingerprints, assign/resolve/ignore/reopen, regression state and linked evidence |
| C17 | Alerts, thresholds, anomaly detection and notifications | R0, P3, H1 | missing | Versioned rules, deduplication, routing, delivery receipts, rate limits and permission checks |
| C18 | Overview, model, tool and performance dashboards | S1, R3, P1 | partial: overview and signal dashboard | Latency percentiles, first-token timing, model/tool health and evidence-preserving filters |
| C19 | Spend, cache usage and unknown-cost handling | R0, S1, P1, H1 | partial: raw optional token fields | Effective-dated price table, model census, cache semantics, cost coverage and corrections |
| C20 | Subscription windows and wasted-work accounting | U1, H1 | partial: usage-limit signal | Supported plan-window adapters; explicit attribution and unknowns; no subscription/API-billing conflation |
| C21 | Custom saved/shareable dashboards and visualizations | R3, P3 | missing | Persisted panel/query contracts, units, filter semantics, ownership/sharing and drill-down proof |
| C22 | Trends, funnels, retention, paths and cohorts for AI | P3, U1 | missing | AI task/outcome identity, comparable denominators, censoring and cohort definitions |
| C23 | Users/organizations and product-to-agent correlation | R0, P1, P3 | partial: account-owned devspaces | Scoped end-user identity, groups and traits with consent and deletion semantics |
| C24 | Session replay, exceptions, logs and external trace links | S1, P1, P3 | missing | Permission-checked correlation IDs, redaction, retention and useful cross-system navigation |
| C25 | Releases, flags, experiments and before/after comparison | R0, P2, P3 | missing | Exposure records, pinned variants/cohorts, uncertainty and reproducible comparisons |
| C26 | Investigation assistant, query API, MCP and safe A2UI | R0, P1, P2 | partial: REST queries and local allowlisted A2UI | Scoped read/write tools, query budgets, provenance and audited actions; no arbitrary UI execution |
| C27 | Scheduled briefs, change reports and root-cause/repair support | R0, H1 | partial: doctor repair text | Durable schedules, evidence-linked reports, controlled repo context and verified fix/revert loop |
| C28 | Shared curated datasets, uploads, annotation and export | R2, P2, U1 | designed: automatic-datasets-v0 | Real isolated collections, immutable snapshots, structured labels, safe import/export and lineage |
| C29 | Automatic dataset policies and durable build jobs | U1, H1 | designed: automatic-datasets-v0 | Purpose/consent revision, cutoff, leases, idempotency, staging validation and atomic publication |
| C30 | Enterprise dataset access, audit and collaboration | U1 | missing implementation | Project/team RBAC, approval/audit history, retention, deletion propagation and explicit sharing |
| C31 | Dataset revisions, quality, provenance and split hygiene | U1, P2, H1 | designed | Reproducible hashes, exclusions, frozen source revisions, deduplication and session/fork leakage tests |
| C32 | Online/offline code, model and sentiment evaluations | P2, R1, H1 | partial: deterministic detection and preview only | Versioned evaluator artifacts, budgets, typed results, coverage, backfill and experiment linkage |
| C33 | Review queues and outcome/correction labels | R1, R2, P2, H1 | partial: MATCH/NOT MATCH against exact snapshot | ACCEPTED/EDITED/REJECTED/ABANDONED with actual correction pairs, reviewer provenance and disagreement handling |
| C34 | Prompt/configuration versions and playground | P1, P2, H1 | missing | Replay-safe test inputs, pinned provider/configuration and comparable eval results |
| C35 | Supervised improvement | U1, H1 | designed | Consented journaled labels, bounded training jobs, holdout intervals, candidate evidence and monitored rollout |
| C36 | Unsupervised discovery | U1, H1 | designed | Eligible unlabelled data, reproducible embeddings/clusters, novelty review; clusters never become truth labels |
| C37 | Reversible promotion and recursive improvement | U1, H1 | designed: mechanism/RRFlow learning contract | Inactive candidates, independent held-out admission, versioned deployment, monitoring and revert receipts |
| C38 | Free/paid entitlements and quota behavior | R0, U1 | missing integration | Server-owned Shippin entitlement contract, downgrade/expiry handling, quota and retry semantics |
| C39 | Member source/key management and onboarding | R0, U1 | partial: auth, public entry, setup guide and milestones | Live signup, self-service source credentials/revoke, same-account readback and no manual operator key handoff |
| C40 | Organization/project RBAC, SSO and provisioning | R0, U1 | partial: isolated Nomen-owned devspaces | Shared platform identity contracts; roles, team/project permission tests and enterprise provisioning |
| C41 | Audit, retention, deletion, residency and export controls | R0, U1 | missing service controls | Owned policies, complete audit trail, deletion/revocation propagation and operational verification |
| C42 | Hosted scale, recovery and GitHub delivery | U1, H1 | partial: immutable artifacts/readiness/rollback fixtures | Verified Texas host, authenticated load/capacity, backup restore and real release/rollback receipt |
| C43 | Live debugging and real-time activity | R0, U1 | partial: polling and SDK event journal | Bounded streaming, reconnect cursors, partial-event presentation and completed-span authority |
| C44 | Human-friendly access on desktop/phone | U1, H1 | partial: responsive vector UI, modals, tooltips and guided paths | Real-user acceptance, assistive technology, keyboard drill-downs and measured performance budgets |

## Delivery sequence and proof

1. **Service foundation:** finish Texas identity/deployment and real member/source
   onboarding alongside server-enforced entitlements (C01, C05, C38-C42).
2. **Monitoring depth:** complete signal, issue, trace, spend and model/tool
   dashboards. Every count must open the same evidence cohort (C06-C20, C43-C44).
3. **Analytics and operations:** saved boards, cohorts/outcomes, correlation,
   alerting, experiments and scoped agent tools (C21-C27). These are real features,
   not visual imitation of PostHog or Sentry.
4. **Enterprise datasets:** implement collections first, then policy-driven builds,
   immutable revisions, review/correction workflows and enterprise governance
   (C28-C34). No training starts because a person labels a signal.
5. **Learning:** bounded supervised experiments and unsupervised candidate discovery;
   held-out evaluation, reversible promotion, regression monitoring and recurrence
   close the loop (C35-C37). External model fine-tuning is a separate supported
   provider capability, not assumed from a consumer subscription.

Monitoring may ship before learning, but dataset lineage and purpose/consent must
be designed into capture/review from the beginning. The dataset implementation
contract remains [automatic-datasets-v0](../spec/automatic-datasets-v0.md); learning
mechanisms remain [mechanism-spec-v0](../spec/mechanism-spec-v0.md). This map links
those owners and does not replace their schemas.

The current signal-dashboard increment is documented in
[signal drill-down](../ux/signal-drilldown.md). It closes a concrete monitoring gap;
it does not close the entire capability baseline or the enterprise learning gates.

text:
# Hosted server artifacts and managed activation

Status: implemented for review on `codex/hosted-release`, 2026-10-27. This is a
continuation of [Texas readiness](texas-readiness.md). It does not establish a
verified Texas VM, a public deployment, production recovery or account activation.

## Build and qualification

The `hosted-artifact` CI job depends on the Linux/Postgres validation job. It checks
out the exact PR head (or push) commit, builds `rroflow-ingest` in release mode on
Ubuntu 22.04, and packages an x86_64 GNU/Linux server. This targets glibc 2.35 or
newer; architecture and runtime compatibility must be checked on the actual VM.
The collector's four-platform release matrix does not establish server support
on those four platforms.

The server embeds its commit, Cargo target and SHA-256 fingerprint of the complete
ordered migration files at build time. `rroflow-ingest build-info` and the read-only
`GET /build-info` endpoint expose that identity without consulting the host's Git
checkout or runtime environment. Unstamped local builds say `development` and
cannot be packaged by the release script.

The archive contains only `rroflow-ingest`, `revision`, `target`, `migrations`,
`build-info.json` and their `SHA256SUMS`. The adjacent `.sha256` pins the archive.
Packaging rejects a binary whose embedded commit/target differs from the expected
release. The CI smoke test extracts that exact archive into a temporary directory,
starts it against disposable JSONL fixture data, and checks build identity,
readiness, unauthenticated rejection, account mapping, ingest/readback, dashboard
assets, authenticated research and graceful SIGTERM. Postgres behavior is tested
in the prerequisite validation job, not by this JSONL artifact smoke.

The artifact is retained by GitHub Actions for 30 days and is a review artifact.
An operator must select the reviewed commit and obtain its expected digest from
the corresponding trusted workflow result. This increment does not attach a
production server to a permanent GitHub Release or provide cryptographic build
attestation. Do not mistake an arbitrary checksum beside an untrusted download
for provenance. Promotion requires all applicable checks on the intended revision.

## Readiness versus liveness

`/healthz` remains process liveness. `/readyz` has a two-second deadline and checks
Postgres connectivity/table readability or the presence of the JSONL directory.
Failures return 503 without connection details. It does not certify free space,
write permissions, backup health or identity-provider availability. Activation
also performs authenticated `/v1/whoami` and `/v1/summary` checks against an expected
devspace, so liveness alone cannot make a rollout successful.

## Provisioning boundary

`deploy/tx-infra-prod/activate-release.sh` upgrades an already-provisioned dedicated
application VM. It never installs packages, creates a database or account, changes
credentials, rewrites runtime configuration, edits DNS/TLS or touches Gold. The old
`deploy.sh` source-build bootstrap is not the production upgrade path.

Before first activation, the operator must independently verify the SSH host and
VM inventory, architecture/runtime, capacity, firewall, Postgres ownership and a
backup restored to an isolated target. Provision root-owned non-writable release
directories `/opt/rroflow` and `/opt/rroflow/releases`, the `rroflow` service user,
external configuration at `/etc/rroflow/ingest.toml`, and the reviewed
`deploy/tx-infra-prod/rroflow-ingest.service` unit. The unit executes
`/opt/rroflow/current/rroflow-ingest` as `rroflow`; configuration and state remain
outside release directories. Do not start it until a release is installed.

The script requires a root-owned backup/restore receipt and a separate protected
smoke-account ingest key file. The presence of a receipt is an operational gate,
not machine proof that a restore succeeded. Keep those files on the host, outside
Git. Configure the expected smoke devspace explicitly. The key is passed to curl
through stdin, never a command-line argument or deployment receipt. Runtime
configuration must grant the service only the access it needs.

After those prerequisites and commit/checksum verification, the operator invokes:

```sh
EXPECTED_HOST=<verified-vm-name> \
RROFLOW_BACKUP_RECEIPT=<protected-restore-receipt-path> \
RROFLOW_SMOKE_KEY_FILE=<protected-smoke-key-path> \
RROFLOW_SMOKE_DEVSPACE=<expected-devspace> \
bash deploy/tx-infra-prod/activate-release.sh <archive> <trusted-sha256> <full-commit>
```

`LISTEN` defaults to loopback `127.0.0.1:8787` and must match the external config.
`RROFLOW_RELEASE_ROOT` and `RROFLOW_CONFIG` support explicitly provisioned layouts;
the systemd unit must use those exact paths. Credentials and live endpoint values
do not belong in this document.

## Activation, rollback and interruption

The read-only VM guard runs first and refuses a Proxmox host. The activator checks
root ownership, permissions and service execution identity, then takes a process
lock. It copies the archive into a protected staging directory and rechecks the
trusted digest, preventing a mutable download from changing between verification
and extraction. Archive membership, member digests and embedded binary identity
must agree. Existing release directories cannot be silently replaced.

Upgrades require the same migration fingerprint as the prior release. A migration
change is refused before activation and requires a separate reviewed migration
and restore procedure. Equal fingerprints are necessary for this rollback path;
they do not prove arbitrary future application/data changes backward compatible.
External config changes are a separate operation and are not rolled back here.

The activator records `activation.pending`, atomically swaps the `current` symlink,
restarts the managed service, and checks readiness, exact build identity and
authenticated reads. Success writes `last-deployment.receipt`. Failure restores
the prior symlink, restarts and verifies it, and writes `last-rollback.receipt`.
First-install failure stops the service and retains a pending receipt; it cannot
invent a prior release. Failed rollback also retains the pending receipt.

A kill/power failure can leave `activation.pending`. The next invocation refuses
to proceed. An operator must reconcile its recorded previous/candidate paths with
the actual symlink and running build, restore a verified prior release or stop the
service, and perform the same authenticated checks before archiving the pending
receipt. Automatic recovery after abrupt power loss is not implemented. Release
directories and database content are never garbage-collected by this script.

The Linux fixture suite exercises activation, upgrade, explicit rollback,
readiness/authentication-triggered rollback and refusal of checksum, migration,
locking, pending-receipt, unit, key-permission and immutable-release violations.
Systemd, HTTP and machine identity in that suite are fixtures. A real Texas
backup/restore and rollout rehearsal remains an acceptance requirement.

text:
# Identity and devspaces on rroflow.ai

Date: 2026-10-26. Decisions D-4 (hosted store: Postgres on tx-infra-prod) and D-6 (devspace owned by the Nomen account) in [rroflow-ai-plan.md](rroflow-ai-plan.md).

## Model

```
Nomen account (issuer, sub)  ──owns──▶  devspace  ──holds──▶  turns, signal hits, signal settings
                                            │
                                            └──attached to (optional)──▶  Shippin.cloud tenant
```

- **Nomen** is the identity provider shared by every Shippin service (a Zitadel fork). rroflow.ai does not keep its own accounts.
- **Devspace** is one person's space on rroflow.ai. Table `devspaces`: `id`, `owner_issuer`, `owner_subject`, `owner_org` (Nomen claim `urn:zitadel:iam:user:resourceowner:id`), `shippin_tenant_id`. One devspace per Nomen account (unique index on issuer + subject).
- **Growing into Shippin.cloud** sets `shippin_tenant_id`. Turns stay where they are, so nothing is copied and nothing can be lost in a move.
- **The credential decides the devspace.** A client never names a devspace; the server derives it from the key or token. Requests can only read and write their own devspace.

## Credentials

| Who | Today (built) | Next (Nomen) |
|---|---|---|
| Collector (`rroflow ingest-claude`, `ingest-codex`) | ingest key; server stores only its SHA-256 | `rroflow login` via the OAuth device flow, like `devagotchi-cli@shippin`; refresh token kept in the OS keychain |
| Dashboard | Nomen authorization code + PKCE when configured; ingest key fallback | account-owned devspace, server-held token and HttpOnly session cookie |
| Server check | key hash lookup, then Nomen (built) | opaque token introspection (RFC 7662) with private-key JWT client auth, answers cached 60 s; Nomen unreachable → 503 `issuer_unavailable`. Same pattern as the Devagotchi hub (`crates/hub/src/nomen.rs`). Required: issuer, `aud` = the rroflow project, `client_id` in the allowed list, `exp`, `sub` |

Keys stay supported after sign-in exists, for headless machines and CI, but are minted by a signed-in user for their own devspace.

## API (ingest)

| Method and path | Auth | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/turns` | devspace | upsert `rroflow.turn/v1` records by `event_id` |
| `GET /v1/turns?agent=&signal=&limit=` | devspace | newest first; filter by agent (`claude-code`, `codex`) and signal |
| `GET /v1/summary` | devspace | totals, per-agent signal counts, the catalogue, the devspace's settings |
| `GET /v1/signals` | public | catalogue `rroflow.signals/v1`: categories (Failure, Friction, Cost, Context), signals, options with defaults and ranges |
| `GET`/`PUT /v1/signals/settings` | devspace | which signals run and their thresholds; collectors read this before evaluating |
| `GET /v1/whoami` | devspace | which devspace the credential opens, and how (`key` or `nomen`, account ID, org) |
| `GET /healthz`, `GET /`, `GET /app` | public shell | health; public product page; member dashboard shell (data requires authentication) |

## Build steps

1. **Built:** Postgres store with migrations, signal catalogue grouped with options, per-devspace settings, dashboard with Claude Code and Codex side by side, deploy script with Postgres for tx-infra-prod.
2. **Built:** Nomen token introspection on the ingest (ported from the Devagotchi hub, same checks and caching); first sign-in creates the devspace for that `sub`; `rroflow-ingest claim` gives an existing key devspace to an account; Nomen down → 503 `issuer_unavailable`, keys keep working.
3. **Built:** `rroflow login` / `logout` / `whoami` (device flow ported from the Devagotchi CLI, refresh within 5 min of expiry, 7-day offline grace, tokens in `account.json` 0600). The collector sends as the signed-in account; `RROFLOW_INGEST_KEY` still wins for headless machines.
4. **Implemented, deployment unverified:** Dashboard sign-in (authorization code + PKCE), opaque browser session, account-owned Claude Code/Codex views. See [browser-sign-in.md](browser-sign-in.md). Key management in the page remains future work.
5. Public: `api.rroflow.ai` (API) and `app.rroflow.ai` (dashboard), both A records to 23.156.136.173, TLS at Caddy in front of `127.0.0.1:8787`. Both hosts reach the same service, so the dashboard's API calls are same-origin.
6. Attach a devspace to a Shippin tenant (`shippin_tenant_id`), started from the Shippin console.

## Nomen setup (created 2026-10-26, project `rroflow` in the Shippin Platform org)

| What | Value |
|---|---|
| Issuer | `https://id.shippin.cloud` (endpoints under `/oauth/v2/`) |
| Project id (the `aud`) | `396821566727389188` |
| `rroflow-ingest` API app, private-key JWT (introspection) | client id `396821567230771204`; key in Gold's `platform-core.sops.yaml` as `rroflow_ingest_jwt_key_b64` |
| `rroflow-cli` native app, device flow + refresh, no secret | client id `396821568421953540` |
| `rroflow-dashboard` web app, authorization code + PKCE + refresh, no secret | client id `396821568908492804`; redirect `https://app.rroflow.ai/auth/callback` |

DNS: `rroflow.ai` → 23.156.136.173 (Cloudflare proxy off). `api.rroflow.ai` and `app.rroflow.ai` to be added the same way.

## Turning on sign-in (tx-infra-prod)

1. Put the API application's key file at `/etc/rroflow/nomen-key.json`, owner `rroflow`, mode 0600.
2. Write `/etc/rroflow/nomen.toml` (kept across deploys):

   ```toml
   [nomen]
   issuer = "https://id.shippin.cloud"
   audiences = ["396821566727389188"]
   clients = ["396821568421953540", "396821568908492804"]
   key_file = "/etc/rroflow/nomen-key.json"
   ```
3. Re-run the deploy; it prints `nomen sign-in: on`.
4. Sign in once, read your account ID from `GET /v1/whoami`, then give your existing devspace to it:
   `rroflow-ingest claim --config /etc/rroflow/ingest.toml --devspace jesse --subject <sub>` (run as `rroflow`). An empty devspace made by that first sign-in gives way; one with turns does not.

title: rroflow.ai: plan v1

text:
# rroflow.ai: plan v1

Status: **proposal**. Decisions marked `D-n` are open until saved as ADRs.
Date: 2026-10-25 (v1: product split with rrflow.ai; powered by Shippin.cloud / shippin.ai; learning vision with status and sources).
Grounded in:
- the Raindrop absorption (live workspace capture, signal authoring, onboarding, settings)
- the DevPulse research ledger (6 repos, 8 Drive docs, 2026-03 → 2026-10)
- RROFLOW mechanism spec v0
- this repo's working ingest (Claude Code + Codex → Raindrop, `doctor`)

## 1. The split: two products, one stack

| | **rrflow.ai: RRFlow** | **rroflow.ai: RROFLOW** |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | The reasoning engine: rrflowDB/rrflowKV, rrflowQL, prompt graphs, LFG kernel, SWAG controller | **Sentry for AI**, plus the **learning layer**: it captures what AI agents do, detects behaviour signals, and learns (supervised, unsupervised, recursive) what works |
| Delivered by | Its own site and repo (`rrflow/rrflow-development`, `rrflow/site-development`), with Connectome as its UI | **Powered by Shippin.cloud / shippin.ai.** Accounts, subscriptions, hosting and the user's devspace come from Shippin, sharing the IdP/OIDC used by DevPulse and Shippin.cloud |
| Repo | `rrflow/rrflow-development`. Engine-side RROFLOW code (promotion contract, learning tables) stays here | `rrflow/rroflow-development` (lab + site), moving to `rrflow/rroflow` at alpha |
| Relationship | RRFlow is where a promoted improvement *lands*: a reversible engine change | RROFLOW produces the evidence and candidates. It monitors RRFlow-powered agents as one of its sources |

**rroflow.ai in one line:** Sentry for your AI. It captures every agent turn, catches failures and wasted spend, shows the evidence, and learns from your corrections. Every learned change is tested before it goes live and can be undone.

**For:** vibe coders first, people who build with AI agents and pay for subscriptions (DevPulse Tier 0: "highest economic exposure"). There is a drill-down for developers. What it protects: "the user's wallet and time" (DevPulse PHILOSOPHY, locked).

**Why Shippin.** A Shippin.cloud user already has an account, a subscription and a devspace. rroflow.ai becomes a capability of that subscription rather than another signup:
- the collector installs with the devspace;
- the hosted dashboard sits in the Shippin user panel;
- billing rides the shippin.ai plan.

The local-first collector still works without Shippin (D-2: both tracks).

### Why it beats Raindrop for this user

| Raindrop (observed live) | rroflow.ai |
|---|---|
| SDK integration; built for teams shipping AI products | Zero-code: reads the sessions your agents already write. Our ingest does this today |
| A label rewrites the classifier with no check. On our real data that gave precision 5/8 to 7/8 | A label becomes evidence for a *candidate*. It is promoted only after held-out evaluation, and every promotion is reversible |
| Cost is a lower bound on what the SDK reports | Cost is derived from raw tokens and a versioned price table. Unknown stays unknown, never $0 |
| No view of your subscriptions | Plan usage and limits per agent (Codex records rate-limit windows in every rollout) |
| PII guard masks product names, and the setting is plan-gated | Redaction rules are visible and editable from day one |
| Onboarding trace review uses a model | `doctor` runs the same checks deterministically, free and instant (shipped) |

## 2. What exists today (verified)

- `crates/rroflow-raindrop`. Its pieces:
  - `ingest-claude` and `ingest-codex`, validated on real transcripts. That includes forked Codex subagents, compaction, and only finished tool calls being sent.
  - `doctor`, with 7 deterministic checks, validated on three producers.
  - Redaction that is always on.
  - Raindrop as the first **sink**.
  - PRs #1 and #2, merged 2026-10-25.
- Live Raindrop findings that change the design:
  - Events upsert by `event_id`.
  - A span re-sent with a new status is listed twice.
  - Generated classifiers skip turns without tool payloads.
  - The Query API ignores `?project=`.
  - Unclaimed project slugs are hidden.
- The DevPulse designs to adopt (section 4).
- Local checkout: `D:\projects\rroflow.ai` (dabo), on `main`.

## 3. Product surfaces

1. **rroflow.ai, public web app.** A story site that explains Sentry for your AI with a live demo built from real captured data (source chip on every panel; no sample numbers), docs, and a waitlist. Learning is shown honestly as "being built", with the loop visible.
2. **`rroflow` CLI, the collector.** `connect`, `doctor`, `ingest-*`, and the Claude Code `Stop` hook / Codex hook. It runs on the user's machine. Sinks: a local store, Raindrop, and later rroflow cloud.
3. **App, the dashboard.** Signals, evidence cards, spend and limits, and labels. Local first. Hosted later, opt-in (see D-2).

## 4. Core model, adopted from DevPulse notes

- **Event.** Aligned to devpulselabs `AiEvent` and OTel GenAI:
  - `CallStarted{provider, model, origin}`
  - `CallFinished{tokens_in, cache_read, cache_write, tokens_out, cost_micros, duration_ms, outcome}`
  - `Disposition{kept}`
  - Per turn: `termination_reason ∈ {completed, tool_error, timeout, budget_exhausted, user_cancel, parent_cancel, model_refusal}`.
  - Every token count is optional. `None` means "provider did not say" and is never priced as zero.
- **Cost is derived, tokens are truth.** A versioned `pricing.v1` table with effective dates. Unknown models are flagged, and a census test fails when a model is seen but missing from the table.
  - Cache tokens stay separate. Today's ingest folds Claude's cache reads out of input, which undercounts (fixed in increment 2).
  - Usage counting per provider: Codex reports cumulative totals, and Claude reports per message.
- **Signals.** Per-domain enums with one stamped envelope `{domain, ms, type, …}` and a global `seq`. Signals fire after the write ("report truth, never intent"). A spec declares delivery, sinks and version: "a kind without a spec does not compile".
- **Content.** Prompt and response text live in an opt-in, scrubbed store joined by hash. Metrics never need content.

## 5. The vision rroflow.ai holds: recursive, supervised and unsupervised learning

Status key: **built** = in this repo and verified on real data; **designed** = written down with a source; **vision** = direction, no design yet.

### The loop

```
capture ─▶ signals ─▶ evidence ─▶ labels ─▶ candidates ─▶ held-out eval ─▶ promote (reversible) ─▶ monitor
   ▲                                                                                              │
   └──────────────────────────── recursion: the promoted change is captured again ◀───────────────┘
```

| Stage | What happens | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Capture | Every agent turn from Claude Code and Codex: prompt, tools, results, tokens; forked subagents; only finished spans | **built** | this repo (`ingest-*`, `doctor`) |
| Signals, tier 1 | Deterministic rules over the capture, with evidence spans | designed | DevPulse classification compiler (Drive 2026-09-24); Raindrop's code classifier = deterministic gate + judge (captured 2026-10-25) |
| Signals, tier 2 | Similarity: embeddings plus per-signal classifiers trained on labels. New categories are new exemplars, not a retrain | designed | LFG_NOTES_v3 §4 (2026-09-26) |
| Signals, tier 3 | Model judge for fuzzy cases only. It answers and mints a candidate tier-1 rule ("the slow path mints fast paths") | designed | LFG_NOTES_v3; Raindrop "Triage writes policy rules + classifier" |
| **Supervised** | Labels: MATCH / NOT MATCH on signal hits, plus outcome labels ACCEPTED / EDITED / REJECTED / ABANDONED. EDITED is the best data, because the edit is the correction | designed | DevPulse normalizer training spec; Raindrop MATCH/NOT MATCH review |
| **Unsupervised** | Cluster unexplained failures (tool-error streaks, aborts, correction spirals) into candidate signals for a person to name. Cluster members are candidates, never labels | designed | mechanism spec R5b; Raindrop "Issues" and "Stumbles" |
| Governed promotion | A candidate lands inactive. It is promoted only when the held-out interval supports the gain; the held-out set is rotated once used; a human revert is a verdict on one revision, not a ban on the category | designed | RRFlow learning contract; vibeguard lessons (live trace); DevPulse "nothing goes live on the model's say-so" |
| **Recursive** | Three nested loops: (1) RROFLOW improves the **agents** (rules, prompts, hooks); (2) RROFLOW improves **its own signals**, since signal precision is itself measured and labelled; (3) promoted rules land in **RRFlow** (LFG tier-1 snapshot), whose answers are captured again | vision (1, 2) / designed (3) | mechanism spec; LFG snapshot swap via ArcSwap; RRFlow learning contract |
| Monitor and roll back | Every promotion is watched against the signal it targeted. Regression triggers a revert proposal | designed | DevPulse incremental enforcement ladder (Drive 2026-09-18) |
| Fine-tuning | Not before thousands of journaled examples ("training first freezes guesses") | rule | v2.1 Addendum A11 |

### Concepts carried over, and where each came from

| Concept | From DevPulse notes | From Raindrop |
|---|---|---|
| Event model | `AiEvent`: tokens are truth, cost is derived, `None` is never zero, Live vs Backfilled | events + OTLP spans; upsert by `event_id` |
| Signals | per-domain signal doctrine; signals report truth, never intent; spec or it does not compile | signal types topic/regex/instrumented/code; presets on by default |
| Mood | bidirectional ebb-and-flow scale (owner correction: not only negatives) | Frustration / Churn Intent presets (negative only) |
| Failure taxonomy | CC-001…CC-014 (false completion ~30%, compaction loss, correction spirals) | Repeated Tool Call Failures, Capability Gaps |
| Onboarding | a checklist that ticks only on real signals; "every line on screen actually happened" | N-of-5 checklist; trace review with a copyable repair prompt |
| Honesty | a provider that declares "does not report usage" instead of showing zero | cost shown as a lower bound with unknowns counted |
| Spend and subscriptions | per-provider usage adapters; subscription-only, never hold a key; backfill from existing sessions | none; this is our gap to fill |
| Evaluation | fail-then-pass pairs are promotion evidence; proof by golden file | portable evaluator artifact (program + judge + pinned projection + hash) |

## 6. Signal set v0 (deterministic first)

| Signal | Evidence source | Why it matters to a vibe coder |
|---|---|---|
| Blocked handoff | denied tool or permission, then the agent asks the user to act | the agent stopped doing the work |
| False "done" | completion claim while tools failed or TODOs remain (CC-001 ~30%) | "it said done; it wasn't" |
| Correction spiral | 3+ user corrections or reverts in a session window | wasted time and tokens |
| Tool-error streak | N failing tool calls in a row (exit codes, error spans) | stuck agent |
| Usage-limit hit | Codex `rate_limits`, `UsageLimitExceeded`; Claude `rate_limit_event` | subscription friction |
| Wasted spend | cost of turns ending aborted, abandoned or reverted | wallet protection |
| Mood (both directions) | frustration and positive signals on one scale (owner correction: "not just negatives") | ebb and flow, not punishment |
| Context loss | compaction followed by repeated or forgotten work (CC-002/006) | silent quality drops |

## 7. Architecture

- **Rust-first.** Python only for ML training.
- **Collector:** this crate, split into `rroflow-core` (event model, pricing, redaction), `rroflow-collect` (Claude and Codex parsers) and sinks (`rroflow-raindrop`, local store).
- **Public site:** same pattern as the decided rrflow.ai site (Astro static + islands, plus a Rust gateway that is the only data client; source chip on every live panel; planned states labelled, never sample data). Explainers rendered with Remotion. Lives in `site/` in this repo (repo scope already decided: outward lab + site).
- **Hosted track runs on Shippin.cloud.** `api.rroflow.ai` ingest and the hosted dashboard are deployed as Shippin.cloud services. Accounts and plans come from shippin.ai, and auth from the shared IdP. Endpoints are configuration, nothing hardcoded.
- **Store:** hosted ingest on Postgres (D-4); the on-machine store is still open. Identity and devspaces: [identity-and-devspaces.md](identity-and-devspaces.md).

## 8. Build order (one PR each; each builds on the last)

0. **Repo ready.** #1 and #2 merged 2026-10-25; checkout at `D:\projects\rroflow.ai`; workspace layout from section 7; CI unchanged (fmt, clippy, tests).
1. **Positioning page.** `site/` skeleton on Astro with the hero "Sentry for your AI", how it works, the learning loop marked "being built", and a waitlist. Deployed to rroflow.ai.
2. **Event model + pricing.** `rroflow-core` with the AiEvent-aligned event, cache tokens split, `pricing.v1`, census test. Ingest moves onto it; the Raindrop sink stays byte-compatible.
3. **`connect` + hooks.** Claude Code `Stop` hook and the Codex equivalent; key reference in keychain or Infisical; project create/claim. Per-turn capture, so compaction no longer loses data.
4. **Signals v0** as deterministic rules with evidence spans, evaluated offline on real captured traffic, with precision reported per signal.
5. **Evidence card.** Label → candidate → held-out result with interval → promote or revert. First on Blocked Work Handoff.
6. **Spend and limits view.** Per agent, project and day; Codex plan windows.
7. **Unsupervised:** failure clustering that proposes candidate signals.
8. **Live demo on rroflow.ai** from the public demo dataset through the gateway.
Hosted track, in parallel from increment 2 on the same event model:
- **H1.** rroflow.ai on Shippin.cloud: Shippin accounts/IdP, project keys under the user's Shippin subscription; `api.rroflow.ai` ingest accepting the event model (OTLP + events), deduplicated by `event_id`, with the finished-span rule enforced server-side.
- **H2.** Hosted dashboard inside the Shippin user panel: signals, evidence cards, spend and limits. It reuses the local dashboard's components.
- **H3.** Sync: the local collector uploads opt-in, redacted projections; content stays local unless enabled.

## 9. Decisions (one per pass)

- **D-1 Positioning — answered 2026-10-25:** *RRFlow (rrflow.ai) is the reasoning engine; RROFLOW (rroflow.ai) is Sentry for AI and holds the learning vision, powered by Shippin.cloud / shippin.ai.* rroflow.ai leads with capture, signals, spend and learning, and links to rrflow.ai for the engine. This replaces the May 2026 "RRO sold to enterprise" headline. Not canon until saved as an ADR.
- **D-2 Order of surfaces — answered 2026-10-25: both in parallel.** The local-first collector and dashboard, and hosted rroflow.ai accounts with cloud ingest, are built as two tracks on one event model. Not canon until saved as an ADR. Consequence: the event model (increment 2) is the shared contract, and hosted ingest must honour the DevPulse laws: no provider keys held; content opt-in and scrubbed before upload.
- **D-3 Site — answered 2026-10-25:** `site/` in this repo, using Astro static with islands, a Rust gateway as the only data client, and Remotion explainers. This is the same pattern as the rrflow.ai site. Not canon until saved as an ADR.
- **D-4 Store — hosted answered 2026-10-26: Postgres on tx-infra-prod.** The rroflow.ai ingest keeps devspaces, turns, signal hits and signal settings in Postgres (schema in `crates/rroflow-ingest/migrations/`). The on-machine store stays open: Parquet + DataFusion (devpulselabs, 2026-08) vs Turso vs RRFlow when ready. Not canon until saved as an ADR.
- **D-5 Term.** "Behaviour signal" for the learned classifier, because "signal" is already H-05 telemetry in RRFlow.
- **D-6 Devspace identity — answered 2026-10-26:** a devspace is owned by the user's Nomen account (issuer + `sub`), the identity shared by all Shippin services. If the user grows into Shippin.cloud, the devspace is attached to their Shippin tenant; the data does not move. Not canon until saved as an ADR.

## 10. Sources

- Raindrop: `claude/raindrop-*` project docs; live captures 2026-10-24/25.
- DevPulse: project doc `claude/devpulse-research-ledger.md`. It covers platform_devpulse, devpulselabs, devpulse-telemetry, devpulse_alpha and devpulse-template, plus the Drive LFG_NOTES_v3, the RRFlow Classification Compiler notes, adr-turn-identity and the CLYFFY specs.
- RROFLOW mechanism spec v0; the RRFlow learning contract (`controller-training.md`).

title: Installing the rroflow SDK and linking subscriptions
description: Product scope, integration design and setup instructions. Check the documented implementation status.
text:
# Installing the rroflow SDK and linking subscriptions

Date: 2026-10-26. Status: plan. Goal (Jesse, 2026-10-26): install the rroflow SDK once; it finds the coding agents and subscriptions already on the machine and offers to link them to rroflow.ai for review. Devagotchi (devagotchi.com) later makes this effortless and grows into a "layer 2" for users on a free tier.

## The path (Jesse, 2026-10-26)

Implementation update (2026-10-27): the SDK capture branch now contains
[continuous source collection](source-collection.md), with account binding and a
durable retry journal across Claude/Codex project directories. It still needs
startup installation and the guided setup experience; it is not a hosted release.

rroflow.ai is built in the open: the repository is public, so every build, test and release runs on GitHub Actions at no cost, and the repository is the record.

1. rroflow.ai running: ingest, Nomen sign-in, public TLS (identity-and-devspaces.md).
2. Devagotchi enables it: it offers the rroflow.ai free tier and installs the SDK.
3. The SDK offers to link the agents and subscriptions it finds, so each AI's turns are captured and its behaviour signals tracked from then on.
4. Over time, datasets for training are generated from those turns automatically.

Rule carried from the learning contract (`claude/rroflow-canon-alignment-notes.md`, RRFlow `controller-training.md`): consent for training is separate from consent for telemetry; no dataset exists merely because turns were recorded. "Automatically" therefore means: the user opts in once (at setup, per devspace), and from then on labelled evidence sets are assembled on a schedule, each with its consent identity, retention and an immutable train/held-out split.

## What the machine already tells us (facts, checked 2026-10-26)

| Agent | Installed? | Signed in, and how | Plan | Turns to capture | Per-turn trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude` on PATH; `~/.claude/` | `~/.claude.json` → `oauthAccount {accountUuid, emailAddress, organizationUuid}` (no tokens in that file) | **Not recorded locally** in the install checked; known only from the user or from rate-limit events in transcripts | `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (parser built) | `Stop` hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` |
| Codex | `codex` on PATH; `~/.codex/` | `codex login status` prints the mode (ChatGPT, API key, access token, Bedrock …) without exposing a token (`codex-rs/cli/src/login.rs`, openai/codex `970111f`, 2026-10-23) | `plan_type` in the `rate_limits` snapshot of rollout `token_count` events (`RateLimitSnapshot`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/protocol.rs`), with primary/secondary windows and credits | `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl[.zst]` (parser built) | `notify` program (`agent-turn-complete` payload with thread and turn id) or the hooks engine (`Stop`, `SessionEnd`) |

Rules that bind detection:
- **Never read, copy or send credentials.** Anthropic's terms forbid collecting or intermediating Claude.ai credentials (see the DevPulse ledger, R279); token files (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, the OS keychain, `~/.codex/auth.json`) are never opened. Sign-in state comes from the agents' own status commands and from account metadata files that hold no secrets.
- **Consent per agent, before anything leaves the machine.** Detection is local and prints what it found; linking sends only what the person approves.
- **Personal data minimised.** The devspace stores the agent, its version, the plan when known, and a SHA-256 of the provider account id (so two machines on one account are recognised) — not the email.

## Increments (one PR each)

1. **Release binaries and installers (decided first, 2026-10-26: Windows, Linux, ARM). Built.** `dist` 0.33.0, configured as Devagotchi's: `rroflow` for Windows and Linux on x86_64 and ARM64 (native ARM runners), shell and PowerShell installers, SHA-256 sums and GitHub attestations, built on every pull request. Publishing is automatic: when `main` carries a `rroflow` version without a release, `release-on-version` starts the release and it creates the tag. CI tests every target natively. macOS follows. Later the installers are also served from rroflow.ai.
2. **`rroflow setup`: detect, then offer.** Prints each agent found: version, signed-in mode, plan when known, how many past sessions exist. Then, per agent: link it? backfill past sessions? capture every turn from now on? Runs `rroflow login` when not signed in. Re-running is safe and shows what is linked.
3. **Per-turn capture.** `rroflow capture --agent claude|codex` reads the hook payload, sends only the turns not yet sent (a local cursor per session; ids are deterministic, so a repeat replaces). `setup` installs it as the Claude Code `Stop` hook and the Codex hook, and `rroflow setup --remove` takes it out. This also fixes compaction loss: turns are captured before the transcript is rewritten.
4. **Linked agents in the devspace.** Ingest gains `PUT /v1/agents/{agent}` (agent, version, sign-in mode, plan, account hash, last seen) and the dashboard an "Agents and subscriptions" panel: plan, rate-limit windows and usage-limit hits per agent.
5. **Plan windows as data.** Codex `rate_limits` snapshots (used %, window, resets at, plan) stored per turn, so limits and wasted spend are charted, not guessed. Claude Code's rate-limit events the same way when present.
6. **Training datasets over time.** With the devspace's training consent on, a scheduled job assembles labelled evidence sets from captured turns and verdicts (mechanism spec R8): consent identity, retention, immutable split manifest with digests; held-out splits are spent once used to accept a change (R7c). Export as Parquet.

## Devagotchi and the free tier

Decided (Jesse, 2026-10-26): **Devagotchi offers to install the rroflow.ai free tier**, and from there leads the user to devscif and Vaultix and tells them the add-ons available for Devagotchi. So Devagotchi is the front door; rroflow is the first thing it installs.

Still open:
- What the free tier includes: a devspace limit (turns, retention, agents) or a feature limit (signals on, learning off).
- How Devagotchi installs rroflow: running the published installer, or `devagotchi start` managing `rroflow` as a component (version, hooks, upgrades).
- devscif: what it is and where it is recorded (no record of it exists in these docs yet).

title: Continuous session collection
description: Product scope, integration design and setup instructions. Check the documented implementation status.
text:
# Continuous session collection

Status: collection and per-user startup commands implemented on development branches;
not activated on the user's machine or deployed to Texas. This is a step toward the setup flow in
[sdk-install-and-linking.md](sdk-install-and-linking.md), not completed turnkey setup.

The one-off preview selected twelve files per agent and a date cutoff. It could
not establish capture coverage. `rroflow sources` instead binds the current user's
Claude Code and Codex session roots to a verified RROFLOW devspace and visits all
session files under those roots, across working directories, with no date cutoff.
Custom roots support alternate agent homes. It does not capture other OS users,
browser-only chats, or activity that a provider never writes to these files.

After signing in to a configured service:

```sh
rroflow login
rroflow sources link
rroflow sources run
```

`sources link --content` opts into scrubbed text at link time; otherwise only metrics
and signal results are retained. `--claude-root`, `--codex-root` and `--store` select
explicit absolute roots and the journal location. An existing binding cannot be
silently changed. `sources status` reports disk state, not process liveness.
`sources run --once --offline` is a network-free capture pass after initial linking.
`sources flush` retries up to sixteen pending batches without reparsing transcripts.

The default store is `sources/` under the existing RROFLOW account configuration
directory. Its binding contains a source UUID, endpoint, devspace, roots, content
choice and a snapshot of signal settings. It contains no provider credentials or
RROFLOW access token. Delivery obtains credentials through the existing account
mechanism, verifies the endpoint and devspace, and refuses account switching.

Each changed turn revision is scrubbed and written to an immutable, numbered batch
using the same fsync/atomic-create helper as the SDK outbox. Only after that write
can upload begin. The collector checks the server's devspace and accepted count
before recording a durable acknowledgement. An uncertain receipt is replayed;
stable event IDs let the server replace the same turn rather than duplicate it.
Later batches cannot pass a failed batch. One process lock protects each journal.
Restart reconstructs the revision index from retained batches, including acknowledged
ones. No acknowledged revision is automatically deleted.

The process scans changes every five seconds by default and rechecks every file
every sixty passes. Failed delivery uses a saved, jittered backoff of up to five
minutes; a server Retry-After can require longer. New passes continue capturing
locally, and restart/manual flush respects the saved wait. Health requests share
the same gate. See [delivery recovery](../ux/delivery-recovery.md).
A pass uploads at most sixteen batches. Requests have
connection/global timeouts and redirects are disabled. The first backfill and a
large changed file can delay a pass; this is not yet a latency guarantee.

Parsers stream JSON records, including compressed Codex rollouts, instead of
loading the entire transcript into one string. Source collection bounds retained
strings before constructing turns. Existing per-turn text limits still apply.
A partial final JSON line is revisited on a later pass; a malformed complete line
fails visibly. A JSON record over 64 MiB or a turn larger than the 4 MiB upload bound
also fails visibly. Symlinks are reported and not followed. No error is a claim
that the source was completely captured.

Project labels default to working-directory grouping when unspecified. The server
also groups older unassigned records by their recorded directory. Project and
session filters apply before the result limit in both JSONL and Postgres stores.
The dashboard groups sessions and plots UTC daily activity from the returned view;
these are explicitly not complete-history totals or source heartbeat indicators.

Still required before turnkey acceptance: per-agent setup choices; released and
activated startup installation;
compaction-safe hooks; incremental cursor performance under sustained load; disk
quotas and retention; ordered revisions across
multiple collectors; large individual turn handling; hosted Texas deployment.
The follow-ups below implement settings refresh and latest source reports. Grok SDK event capture is
a separate path; subscription ownership alone does not make every Grok surface
observable. Dataset generation and training remain unimplemented.

Tests cover more than twelve files across multiple projects, offline recording,
restart without duplicate revisions, changed turns, lock exclusion, malformed and
partial writes, unavailable delivery, uncertain receipts, account refusal, API
tenant isolation, server-side filters, escaped UI content and logout cleanup.


## Signal settings refresh (2026-10-27 follow-up)

The signal-workspace increment refreshes built-in settings after successful delivery,
at most once per minute. It verifies the bound endpoint and devspace, validates the
configuration and writes an immutable local settings revision before using it. On
restart the newest cached revision is used, including offline runs. Older/conflicting
revisions are refused and reported separately from delivery; acknowledged uploads
remain acknowledged. Changed built-in choices invalidate the scan cache so local
rules are recomputed on the next pass. Custom definitions remain cloud-only rules
on uploaded projections; a custom-setting change alone does not clear the scan cache.
The revision cache currently retains all settings revisions. Older collector builds
retain link-time settings and need an upgrade. See [signal workspace](../ux/signal-workspace.md).


## Source health reports

The source-health increment sends bounded latest-only reports with a durable sequence, pending queue counts, retained bytes, scan-error count and last upload result. The Sources page distinguishes recent reports from stale or unavailable status; old activity is never a heartbeat. See [source reporting and recovery](../ux/source-health.md). See [collector startup](../ux/collector-startup.md) for native per-user installation, lifecycle and logout limitations. Hosted activation remains unfinished.

title: Subscription support and capture matrix

text:
# Subscription support and capture matrix

Status: implementation matrix, checked 2026-10-26. Provider features change;
pin the client version and repeat a real end-to-end capture before marking support.

| Provider / surface | Supported path established by source | RROFLOW status / next proof |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic / Claude Code | Official signed-in Claude Code; local sessions and documented hooks | Parser exists. Prove idempotent setup, per-turn capture and upload from a real subscription session. |
| OpenAI / Codex | Official client sign-in; local rollout capture | Parser exists. Prove complete capture including forks, compaction and plan windows. |
| OpenAI / ChatGPT plan usage in RROFLOW | Official OAuth integration for eligible local open-source apps; hosted/paid availability requires access approval | Design option, not shipped. Register the correct client, keep credentials in the owning runtime, and verify eligibility. OAuth sign-in does not grant chat history. |
| Google / Gemini CLI | Sign in with the Google account associated with Pro/Ultra; documented hooks | Adapter needed. Validate events, tools, partial turns and missing usage against pinned fixtures. |
| xAI / Grok and Grok Bot | Official xAI sign-in; eligible subscription access is documented | Capture adapter/history-export route not yet verified. Do not equate product subscription access with a generic inference API or telemetry feed. |
| Cursor | Official client; xAI documentation describes eligible shared subscription usage | Capture adapter needed. Distinguish first-party included usage from separately billed third-party models. |
| Other major subscriptions, including Copilot | Per-provider official client/integration | Inventory and verify before claiming support; do not infer from a brand name. |
| Claude/ChatGPT/Grok browser conversations | Explicit user export or documented connector, when available | Separate adapters. No assumption that CLI parsers cover chat apps or that sign-in grants historical conversations. |

The initial product scope includes coding tools and chat-app integration paths.
Until the owner answers the surface question, this is a planning assumption,
not permission to scrape private browser state or read provider token stores.

## Connection record

Persist provider and surface separately, adapter/version, capability version,
connection status, source locations selected by the user, capture consent,
dataset/training consent references, last successful capture, and known plan
metadata with observation time. States distinguish unavailable, discovered,
awaiting sign-in, consented, capturing, stale and failed. Unknown plan/usage
remains unknown. Discovery alone sends nothing.

A connection to Nomen identifies the RROFLOW devspace. A provider account
authenticates with that provider's supported client. If an approved direct OAuth
integration is later added, it uses its own requested scopes and credential store;
the collector never repurposes another application's cached credentials.

## Meaning of works immediately

Install a supported binary, sign in, see locally discovered sources, consent per
surface, and observe a real turn with tools/evidence/usage where reported. Replay
the same turn without duplication; disconnect without data loss; revoke capture.
Provide a clear unavailable state for unsupported paths. No synthetic activity or
assumed subscription entitlements may satisfy onboarding.

## Primary sources

- [Claude Code overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview):
  supported product surfaces and account requirements.
- [OpenAI sign-in overview](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart) and
  [local open-source plan usage](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source):
  optional scoped plan usage; local versus hosted availability; no conversation access.
- [Gemini CLI authentication](https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/) and
  [hooks](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/): Google sign-in and hook integration.
- [xAI subscription overview](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/overview),
  [Grok Bot inclusion](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/grok-bot) and
  [sign-in](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/grok-bot-sign-in):
  provider-managed access, not proof of a third-party capture interface.

These sources establish available integration paths, not RROFLOW compatibility.
No subscription changes, paid API requests or provider sign-in were performed.

title: Texas application VM readiness
