text:
# Texas application VM readiness

Status: in progress, 2026-10-26. This is the operational continuation of
[rroflow-ai-plan.md](rroflow-ai-plan.md), not a replacement product authority.

## Intended outcome

RROFLOW develops Reason Ready Objects and flow from captured activity: events,
evidence, corrections, dataset revisions, experiments and reversible improvements.
Users should connect the subscriptions they already have. Capture support,
subscription-powered execution, chat-history import and model training are
distinct capabilities and each gets a verified status.

The immediate deployment is the collector-facing API and dashboard in an
identified application VM. Postgres is the answered hosted-store choice (D-4);
Nomen account ownership is the answered identity choice (D-6). The local store
remains open. The older reconciliation's JSONL-only observations are historical.

## Placement and operational gates

1. Establish the trusted SSH route and confirm VM identity against the management
   inventory. A public address and a hostname in a script do not prove placement.
   Keep addresses, SSH credentials and runtime configuration out of this record.
2. Inventory OS, architecture, vCPU, available memory, disk/inodes, clock sync,
   existing listeners, service ownership and firewall. Observe load before sizing.
   Do not run the application installer on a Proxmox hypervisor.
3. Run the read-only guard from the same pinned source checkout as deploy.sh:
   `EXPECTED_HOST=<verified-host> REV=<full-commit> bash deploy/tx-infra-prod/preflight.sh`.
   The guard is a necessary check, not a production-readiness certificate.
4. Qualify the release with fmt, clippy, Rust tests and real Postgres tests.
   Build outside the serving workload, retain the previous executable and config,
   and pin an artifact checksum. The existing source-build installer is a bootstrap
   tool; upgrades still need a transactional release/rollback implementation.
5. Install loopback-only first. Inspect role ownership, migrations and filesystem
   permissions. Keep Postgres private. Test bad-token rejection and two different
   devspaces: reads, writes, settings and generated datasets must remain isolated.
6. Exercise Nomen login/refresh/logout and account-to-devspace mapping. Complete
   dashboard PKCE and collector onboarding before claiming user-ready sign-in.
   Never use provider account credentials as RROFLOW credentials.
7. Take a database backup and restore it into an isolated target; verify data and
   owner mapping. Document retention, deletion, encryption and recovery ownership.
   Rehearse rollback across the actual migration set before the next release.
8. Configure DNS/TLS only after service checks pass. PUBLIC_HOSTS is deliberately
   empty by default. Integrate with an existing proxy instead of overwriting it.
   Prove public health, authentication and rate limiting; liveness alone is not
   database readiness. Protect abuse-sensitive endpoints before opening intake.
9. Add health/readiness and backup-failure alerts, request/worker limits and disk
   alerts. Keep dataset and training workers out of the request process. No GPU
   purchase or model placement is implied; use measured work and bound workers.
10. Prove one real, consented Claude Code session and one Codex session through
    capture, replay, dashboard and deletion. Extend adapters against the same
    contract. Record a support claim only after its complete flow passes.

## Known work before public release

The [hosted release increment](hosted-releases.md) adds a CI-built server artifact,
embedded build identity, store readiness and managed activation/rollback. It is
review-stage work; its fixture tests do not confirm a Texas deployment. Use that
path for reviewed upgrades after provisioning, rather than the source-build
bootstrap described below.

- Original installer could mutate a host before checking proxy conflicts, allowed
  public exposure by default, and had no application-VM identity guard. The new
  preflight runs before package/service/config changes and defaults to loopback.
- Source extraction replaces /opt/rroflow/src, builds run on the serving host,
  and binary/config replacement is not transactional. Replace this path with
  versioned releases and verified rollback before using it for production upgrades.
- /healthz is liveness; database readiness and public request rate limiting need
  verification/implementation.
- Browser PKCE, release installers, setup/capture hooks, per-provider linking and
  automatic dataset jobs are not established by the existing ingest deployment.
- Postgres storage and Nomen code are present; their successful operation on the
  Texas VM remains unverified.

## Evidence from this session

The independent source baseline is
`ea66dbadb077111b3ca49f35be20db3a4179ee24`.
Work is isolated on branch `codex/texas-readiness`.

The configured management route timed out. Direct SSH to the documented target
stopped at missing trusted host identity; it was not bypassed. Public checks
observed apex DNS, no HTTPS response and missing API/app DNS. Those observations
are point-in-time probes, not a complete host inventory. No remote mutation has
been performed. The verified VM SSH route is the current deployment dependency.

See [subscription support](subscription-support.md) and
[automatic dataset contract](../spec/automatic-datasets-v0.md).

title: Compute and data workload classification
description: Deployment and workload planning inputs; these notes do not confirm a live deployment.
text:
# Compute and data workload classification

Date: 2026-10-15. Purpose: classify every part of the AI stack (models, vector store, databases, project brain, learning loops) by what it consumes, and reach each part only through a configurable endpoint.

## Decided
- The eight workload classes below are locked (2026-10-15).
- Fact (2026-10-15): 3 DGX Sparks are live, in the original switchless ring.
- Endpoints, not hosts (2026-10-15, correction from Jesse): every class is a service reached through a named endpoint binding. Which machine, provider or model serves it is configuration, never code. Local, subscription, API and self-hosted are interchangeable bindings and must not change functionality.
- First binding profile `ring-3` (2026-10-15): two Sparks bound to large-model serving, one Spark bound to the brain (classes 2–5 plus the eval runner), weight training in scheduled windows on the serving Sparks, control plane on Proxmox, 550B deferred until a 4-node fabric. This is one profile, not the architecture.
- UI-driven and managed (2026-10-15, requirement from Jesse): bindings, profiles and hardware inventory must be designed so they can evolve into being created, edited and managed through a UI, not only by editing files.
- Config home (2026-10-15): the master copy of managed config lives inside each RRFlow instance's own store as UI-edited, versioned revisions. The repository ships only the schema and default templates; TOML is the import/export and backup form. Jesse's own setup is one instance like any other; a hosted shippin.cloud instance and its local-first copy sync config like any other data.
- Canonical instance store (2026-10-16): rrflowKV, RRFlow's own store, holds the project brain and the config revisions. HydraDB, SurrealDB, Postgres and DuckDB become optional bound adapters or import sources. The rrflow-hydradb prototype's UI and Raindrop wiring are to be pointed at RRFlow's API, and its HydraDB data imported.
- RRFlow build order (2026-10-16): recoverability first, then managed config revisions, ingestion on today's indexes, answer generation through bound endpoints, and the prototype UI pointed at RRFlow; C-07, E and F after. Detail and step 1 findings: `claude/rrflow-build-order.md`.

## What the store decision requires of RRFlow (mapped to its roadmap)
| Need | Roadmap item today | State |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical data is recoverable | D-11 backup verification, restore into an absent target; C-07 durability qualification | Open. The failing kill-matrix test is a missed fixture update (fix verified locally); installed-estate backup resolution is still unbuilt |
| UI-managed config revisions | Extends the existing revisioned `EstateConfiguration` (`rrd-contract/src/deployment.rs`), sealed at install by D-01 | Revisions exist only at install time; no edit/activate/rollback after install |
| Getting data in | D-02 persisted jobs, D-03 project-tree inventory, D-04 parsing, D-05 normalize → embed → index → graph | All open. D-05 is written to wait until Gates E and F pass |
| Generating answers through bound model endpoints | Gates G (LFG) and H (context flow, live delivery) | Open; waves 9–10 of 12 |
| UI | H-06/H-07 Connectome; the prototype's TypeScript UI could call RRFlow's HTTP API | Open |

Fact relevant to reordering: RRFlow's engine data-flow record states that Gates E, F and H replace the current whole-snapshot BM25, exact-vector and graph costs with native incremental paths "without changing the public operation". Ingestion built on today's paths would not need rework when E and F land.

## Why classification comes first
A DGX Spark has no separate VRAM. CPU and GPU share one 128 GB LPDDR5x pool per node. A database's page cache, a vector index held in RAM, and a model's weights and KV cache all draw from the same memory. Unclassified, the largest model takes the whole pool and everything else either starves or moves off the box.

## Endpoint model
| Concept | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Class contract | What a class does and its request/response shape. Code depends only on this. |
| Endpoint binding | One entry: class, binding kind (`local`, `self_hosted`, `subscription`, `api`), endpoint URL, model or service identifier, credential reference (an Infisical secret name, never a value), declared footprint (memory, GPU required), and limits. |
| Profile | A named set of bindings, one or more per class (ordered fallbacks allowed). `ring-3` is the first. |
| Hardware inventory | Declared capacity per machine (memory, GPU, disk). A profile is validated against it: declared footprints on one machine must fit. |
| Eval arm | May swap a profile or a single binding (e.g. local 9B vs an API model for class 2) and is measured with the decided metrics. |

Format and schema follow the decisions in `claude/skills-and-routines-inventory.md`: TOML validated by JSON Schema generated from Rust types with `schemars`. The types belong in `rrd-contract` beside `EstateConfiguration`.

Existing RRFlow vocabulary to reuse rather than reinvent: deployment profiles already treat deployment form, storage profile and endpoint presentation as independent coordinates (`docs/reference/deployment/modes.md`), and `rrd-contract/src/model_manifest.rs` has `RouterRuntimeBinding` and `RouterModelManifest`.

## What "UI-managed" requires of the design
1. Schema-driven forms. The UI renders from the same JSON Schema that validates files. Rust doc comments on the types become field descriptions in the generated schema, so labels and help text have one source.
2. Secrets as references only. The UI picks an Infisical secret name; values never enter config, the UI, or logs.
3. Versioned revisions with explicit activation. Every save creates a new revision; a revision is validated (schema, hardware fit, endpoint reachable) before it can be activated; rollback means activating an earlier revision. Mirrors RRFlow's governed-effects rule: exploration is free, durable changes are explicit.
4. Runtime resolution. Services look up the active profile at request time or on change notification, never at compile time, so an activation takes effect without a rebuild.
5. Observed state beside declared state. The UI shows each binding's health (reachable, latency, memory in use) next to its declared footprint, so the hardware inventory becomes measured, not guessed.
6. TOML stays the file form: shipped templates, import/export, backup. Files and UI share one schema.

### Precedents already in the ecosystem
- Warden (warden.rrflow.ai) has a live service catalog page and docker-compose templates with an `x-warden` extension schema covering SurrealDB, Qdrant, the Harrier embedder via TEI, Infisical and Authentik; its state store is SurrealDB (ADR 0005).
- The rrflow-hydradb prototype's dashboard creates databases and saves their Personal/Shippin assignment in HydraDB through the UI.
- Jesse's ADR rule: an ADR is edited and saved through an interactive component, then written to the repo; it is not canon until saved that way.

## Class 5 candidate facts (basis for the store decision)
| Candidate | What it gives today | Limits found | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| rrflowKV (RRFlow Rust engine) — chosen | All-or-none transactions across records, graph, vector and index deltas; bi-temporal versions with read stamps; deterministic, budgeted context assembly with per-item evidence; 832 of 833 tests pass (833 with the verified fixture fix); single binary target | No ingestion path; no answer synthesis; no UI; heavy per-change process | MIT OR Apache-2.0 (yours) |
| HydraDB managed cloud (`api.hydradb.com`) | What the working prototype uses: knowledge/memory ingestion, context graphs, hybrid retrieval, SaaS connectors | Hosted service; per the team's own research its SDK methods and connectors "should not be assumed to exist on a local graph node", so a local-first copy would not have the same surface | Proprietary service |
| HydraDB OSS engine | Rust; SlateDB plus object storage; snapshot-pinned reads; OpenCypher subset | Auto-commit only, so a sequence of requests is not one rollback unit; bare ID reads can return rows for nonexistent nodes; plain relationship creation can duplicate edges | AGPL-3.0 (modifying it and offering it over a network requires offering the modified source to those users) |
| SurrealDB v3 | Multi-model (document, graph, vector); already Warden's state store; DevPulse persistence plan | Vector store planned to be replaced by the Qdrant fork | BSL 1.1: may not be used "as a Database Service", meaning letting third parties "create, manage, or control schemas or tables"; converts to Apache 2.0 on 2030-01-01 |
| Postgres + DuckDB (three-tier plan) | Mature, permissive | No native temporal graph or context semantics; RRFlow-style logic would sit on top | PostgreSQL License; MIT |

## Hardware facts
| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Memory | 128 GB LPDDR5x unified (not DDR7), 256-bit, 273 GB/s | NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware overview |
| CPU | 20 Arm cores: 10 Cortex-X925 + 10 Cortex-A725 | same |
| GPU | Blackwell, 6,144 CUDA cores, up to 1 PFLOP FP4 with sparsity | same |
| Storage | 1 TB or 4 TB NVMe | same |
| Network | ConnectX-7, two QSFP ports; 10 GbE | same |
| Power | 240 W supply; GB10 SoC 140 W TDP | same |
| NVIDIA model guidance | Up to 200B parameters on one Spark, 405B on two | same |
| Live now (stated by Jesse) | 3 Sparks in the switchless ring; ~119 GB usable per node ≈ 357 GB total | Jesse |
| Planned (stated) | 4-node fabric, then 7–8 nodes on MikroTik CRS804 at 200G | Jesse |
| Large-model target (stated) | Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B via SGLang, TP=4/EP=4, ~42–43 tok/s aggregate at concurrency 8 | Jesse |

### What the 550B target consumes (arithmetic)
- At 4-bit weights, 550B parameters ≈ 275 GB. At 8-bit ≈ 550 GB.
- On 4 nodes (~476 GB): ≈ 69 GB of weights per node, ≈ 50 GB per node left, which the inference server takes for KV cache. 8-bit does not fit.
- On the 3 live nodes (~357 GB): the planned TP=4/EP=4 layout needs four nodes, so it cannot run as configured. Even re-laid-out, 4-bit weights leave ≈ 27 GB per node.
- Conclusion: the 550B target, as stated, consumes every Spark it runs on.

## Classification dimensions
1. Role: what the part does.
2. Bottleneck resource: memory bandwidth, memory capacity, GPU compute, CPU, or NVMe I/O.
3. Latency class: interactive (a person waits), always-warm (must answer in milliseconds, so it stays loaded), or batch (can wait, can be scheduled).
4. State: canonical (source of truth; must be backed up), derived (rebuildable from canonical), or ephemeral (lost on restart, fine).
5. Binding: the endpoint(s) a profile assigns to the class. Configuration only.

## Workload classes (locked)
Components listed are current candidate bindings, not fixed choices.

| # | Class | Current candidate bindings | Bottleneck | Latency | State | Needs GPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Large-model serving | 550B cluster target; 14B primary reasoning model | Memory bandwidth (decode) and capacity (weights + KV cache) | Interactive | Ephemeral | Yes |
| 2 | Always-warm small models | LFG intent model (150–250M, INT8, CPU); LFG boundary model (9B, yes/no logits); 0.6B minions | Latency; small footprint (LFG is CPU) | Always-warm | Ephemeral | Partly (9B and minions yes; LFG intent no) |
| 3 | Embedding and reranking | Harrier 0.6B via TEI (1024-dim) | GPU compute; batches well | Batch at ingest, interactive at query | Ephemeral | Yes |
| 4 | Vector store | RRFlow native vector indexes; `cortex/qdrant` fork (RRO); Qdrant Cloud (used by the rrflow-hydradb prototype) | Memory capacity (vectors + HNSW graph) and CPU; NVMe when on-disk | Interactive query, batch index build | Derived (rebuildable from canonical records) | No |
| 5 | Canonical store / project brain | rrflowKV (chosen); adapters or import sources: HydraDB, SurrealDB v3, Postgres, DuckDB | NVMe I/O, CPU, page-cache memory; durability | Interactive and batch | Canonical | No |
| 6 | Learning: weight updates | LoRA of minions; DPO; Unsloth/Axolotl; distillations (2B → 150–250M, ~27B → 9B) | GPU compute; bursty | Batch, scheduled | Produces versioned model artifacts | Yes |
| 7 | Learning: behaviour updates | Traces → signals → issues → experiments → changes to prompts, skills, routines, configs; Raindrop (already wired into the rrflow-hydradb prototype) | CPU, storage, small classifiers, embeddings for clustering | Continuous / batch | Evidence is canonical; classifiers derived | Little |
| 8 | Control plane and ops | Warden, Proxmox, Authentik, Infisical, Caddy | CPU, small | Always-on | Canonical config | No |

### Rough footprint of classes 2–5 when bound locally (estimate; assumptions stated)
| Part | Assumption | Memory |
|---|---|---|
| LFG intent model | 150–250M parameters, INT8 | 0.15–0.25 GB |
| Harrier embedder | 0.6B, BF16 | ~1.2 GB |
| 0.6B minion | BF16, per model | ~1.2 GB |
| 7B voice model | 8-bit | ~7 GB |
| 9B boundary model | 8-bit | ~9 GB |
| 14B reasoning model | 8-bit | ~14 GB |
| KV cache for the above | modest context and concurrency | ~10–20 GB |
| Vectors (Harrier, 1024-dim) | float32 = 4 KB per vector; 1M vectors ≈ 4.1 GB; int8 scalar quantization ≈ 1 KB per vector | 4–20 GB for 1–5M vectors |
| Database page cache | working sets of the bound stores | 16–32 GB budget |
| Total | | ≈ 70–100 GB |

Roughly one Spark's ~119 GB holds classes 2–5 at single-developer scale. These become declared footprints in bindings and are replaced by measured values once data exists.

### Reliability fact for profiles
On unified memory, an inference server that runs out of memory can take co-located processes down with it. Profiles should bind the canonical store (class 5) to a different machine from large-model serving (class 1).

## Raindrop (reference for class 7)
- What it is: hosted observability and debugging for AI agents. Self-hosting in beta. Pro is $299/mo plus $0.003 per event up to 1M.
- Loop: trace every run and tool call → explicit signals (thumbs, regenerate, copy) and implicit signals (narrow yes/no classifiers for refusals, task failure, laziness, memory failures, user frustration, wins) → cluster into issues and user intents → Deep Search (semantic search for candidates, LLM classifies each) → lightweight classifiers trained on user labels → experiments comparing a variant to a baseline → simulations on pull requests → MCP auto-fix loops that patch, replay the failed trace and verify.
- It does not train model weights. It is class 7, not class 6.
- Already integrated: the rrflow-hydradb prototype records real Raindrop events and feedback with read-back verified (per its TEAM.md, 2026-10-12).
- Mapping to decisions already made: signals ≈ configurable metrics; experiments ≈ eval arms; traces ≈ evidence graph; issue definitions ≈ lexicon and reasoning graph content.

## Open (one decision at a time)
1. How changes land in `rrflow-development` (see `claude/rrflow-build-order.md`).
2. Binding schema details (fields above are a draft).
3. Deep study of Raindrop's loop for class 7 design.

## Sources
- https://docs.nvidia.com/dgx/dgx-spark/hardware.html
- https://www.raindrop.ai/
- https://www.zenml.io/llmops-database/production-monitoring-and-issue-discovery-for-ai-agents
- https://github.com/EonsofStupid/rrflow-hydradb (README.md, TEAM.md, research/HYDRADB.md at 2026-10-12)
- https://github.com/surrealdb/surrealdb/blob/main/LICENSE

# Skills and routines inventory (build workflow)

Date: 2026-10-15. Scope chosen by Jesse: the skills and routines we use to build RRFlow and DevPulse (not the RRFlow engine's Gate I runtime).

## Decided
- Scope: our build workflow (2026-10-15).
- Clyffy loader / `taxonomy.go` compatibility is not a constraint; pre-release, design it correctly (2026-10-15).
- Primary grouping: by primary graph (2026-10-15). Each skill lives under the one graph it is authoritative for and declares any other graphs it reads. Skills whose result is an effect on an outside system are `activities/`. Routines are their own `routines/` tree. Evals are their own `evals/` tree. Build stage is a property of a routine step, not a folder.
- Graph families (2026-10-15): source, knowledge, reasoning, lexicon, routine, evidence. The family set is configuration, not hardcoded, so test runs can show which families overload context and which improve results.
- Test configuration settings per graph (2026-10-15): on/off; fold into another graph; load cap (items or tokens the graph may add to context). A configuration is run as one eval arm.
- Eval measurements (2026-10-15): every arm records outcome (success, attempts, retries), cost (input/output tokens, tool calls, latency), trigger accuracy (right skill fired, wrong skill did not), and tokens added per graph. The metric set is configurable: we ship a schema and a template so metrics can be customised and new ones added.
- Config format (2026-10-15): every config file is TOML, validated by JSON Schema. Covers graph families, test configurations, metrics, skill manifests and routines. The 9 YAML files in agent-skills are to be converted.
- Schema source (2026-10-15): Rust types are the single source; `schemars` generates the JSON Schema files, which are committed so Node, Python and editors validate without a Rust toolchain. Same direction RRFlow's contracts already use.
- Eval harness (2026-10-15): extend `rrflow-eval` as the one canonical runner. Add configurable arms (replacing the hardcoded `baseline`/`runtime` pairing), trigger accuracy (reusing skill-creator's temporary-skill technique), and tokens added per graph. skill-creator remains only for tuning skill descriptions.
- Repository for config types and harness (2026-10-16, follows from decisions in `claude/compute-and-data-workload-classification.md`): config is UI-managed instance data stored in rrflowKV, so its Rust types belong in `rrflow-development/crates/transport/rrd-contract` beside the existing revisioned `EstateConfiguration`, and `rrflow-eval` stays in `rrflow-development`. agent-skills keeps skill content and consumes the generated schema. Jesse can override.

### Design principle observed across decisions
Graph families, test configurations and metrics are all configuration with a shipped schema and template, not hardcoded. Applied by default to the rest of this design (e.g. verdict thresholds) unless Jesse says otherwise.

### Placement of existing skills under the decided grouping
```
graphs/
  source/       (none yet)
  knowledge/    rust-conventions, styling-resolver
  reasoning/    structured-discussion, ai-orchestration, fork-deliberate-collapse
  lexicon/      (none yet)
  routine/      (none yet)
  evidence/     (none yet)
activities/     proxmox, cloudflare, server-administration, figma, preflight-scripts
routines/       change-authoring (from RRFlow AGENTS.md)
evals/          proxmox-workspace
unplaced:       server-ops-orchestrator (a dispatcher, not a skill)
```

### Graph family meanings
| Family | Holds |
|---|---|
| source | Files, symbols, dependencies, build targets, tests |
| knowledge | Docs, ADRs, claims, entities, conventions |
| reasoning | Decisions, plans, hypotheses, verdicts, reasoning trees |
| lexicon | LFG canonical labels and boundary questions |
| routine | Routine steps and their dependencies |
| evidence | Commits, test and CI runs, operation captures, change journals, linked by cause |

## Existing measurement tools
| Tool | Records | Limits found |
|---|---|---|
| `rrflow-development/crates/evaluation/rrflow-eval` (Rust, 318 lines) | Drives the `claude`, `codex` and `gemini` CLIs; per trial: success, attempts, retries, tool calls, input/output tokens, latency | `summarize` pairs only arms named `baseline` and `runtime` (hardcoded); no trigger accuracy; no tokens per graph |
| skill-creator benchmark (`agent-skills/hubs/infrastructure/proxmox-workspace/iteration-*/benchmark.md`) | With vs. without skill: pass rate, time, tokens. Proxmox iteration 2: pass rate 100% vs 26%, +39.8 s, +13,332 tokens | Two configurations only (with/without) |
| skill-creator trigger eval (`proxmox-workspace/trigger-eval/*/results.json`) | Description optimisation: train and held-out test trigger scores | Anthropic plugin's Python scripts; Jesse maintains 9 Windows patches in `agent-skills/tools/skill-creator-windows-patches/` because plugin updates overwrite them |

## Config and schema facts
- agent-skills today mixes 14 TOML files (per-skill `manifest.toml`, two policy files), 9 YAML files (`connectome.registry.yaml`, `domains/*/manifest.yaml`, `server-admin-policy.yaml`, `preflight-scripts.yaml`, CI) and JSON for evals/npm.
- RRFlow takes estate configuration as TOML and derives JSON Schema from Rust types with `schemars` in `rrd-contract`, `rrd-engine` and `rrd-kubernetes`. `rrd-contract/src/deployment.rs` already has `EstateConfigurationInput` and a revisioned `EstateConfiguration`.
- KnowQL's `shape` is JSON Schema.
- agent-skills tooling today is Node (`build/validate-all.mjs`, `build/compose.mjs`) plus Python helpers (`hubs/_shared/*.py`) and skill-creator's Python eval scripts.
- `rrflow-development`'s AGENTS.md requires engine "verification ... tooling" to live in that repository and every change there to carry a planning commit and journal. `rrflow-eval` and 36 result files already live there. The repo is listed as public on GitHub although AGENTS.md calls it private.

## Sources inspected
| Source | State |
|---|---|
| `EonsofStupid/agent-skills` @ `6265c88` (2026-05-18) | 11 skill folders in the 7-hub Clyffy taxonomy; last push 5 months ago |
| claude.ai account skills | One custom skill: `fork-deliberate-collapse`; the rest are Anthropic built-ins |
| `rrflow/rrflow-development` @ `cfa0e80` | Build routine lives in `AGENTS.md` (codebase-grounded change-authoring routine); engine-side skill/routine/trigger design is Gate I and unbuilt; `rrd-core/src/reasoning_tree.rs` contract exists; attunement phases `Connect → Inventory → Parse → Normalize → EntityLink → LexicalIndex → Embed → VectorIndex → Graph → Ground → Verify` are declared |

## agent-skills today
| Hub | Skills |
|---|---|
| infrastructure | proxmox, proxmox-workspace (`kind = "macro"`, eval workspace), server-administration, server-ops-orchestrator, cloudflare |
| coding | rust-conventions (183 words) |
| content | figma, styling-resolver |
| intelligence | ai-orchestration |
| meta | preflight-scripts, structured-discussion |
| platform, personal | empty |

Shared machinery that already exists: `manifest.toml` schema (`kind` = skill/macro/preset, `category`, `capabilities`, `modalities`, `dependencies`, `permission_tier`), `connectome.registry.yaml` router, `_shared/` capture, namespace and preflight helpers, three-tier policy gating.

## Gaps found
1. No skill touches a knowledge graph, source graph or reasoning graph. Coding has one 183-word conventions file.
2. No routine layer. `kind = "macro"` is used once, for an eval workspace, not for an ordered multi-skill routine.
3. `domains/devpulse/manifest.yaml` references 11 skills that do not exist: tauri2-patterns, svelte5-runes, error-handling, state-management, data-fetching, proxmox-management (renamed to `proxmox`), devpulse-cortex, devpulse-pipeline-editor, devpulse-teaching-layer, devpulse-rro, devpulse-state.
4. The 800-word skill cap is not enforced by `ci/skills-ci.yml` or `build/validate-all.mjs`. Three skills exceed it: structured-discussion 1,805, proxmox 1,333, figma 1,204.
5. `hubs/_PATTERN.md` has 12 references to pre-reshape paths (`claude-code-skills/`, `categories/`).
6. The RRFlow build routine (AGENTS.md) is not a skill anywhere; it is repository prose.
7. `hubs/_shared/` uses a folder name banned by the Pre-Release Operating Mode (DDD) rule (`core`, `shared`, `utils`, `helpers`, `common`, `lib`).

## Grouping facts (basis for the decided grouping)
- RRFlow canon already separates skill packages (content), routine definitions (ordered steps), external activities (effects on outside systems), and typed graph relation families. Using the same split here lets the build workflow later import into RRFlow unchanged.
- RRFlow's single-owner rule: each subject has exactly one owning record. A grouping axis should give each skill exactly one home.
- Build stage gives shared skills several homes (e.g. inventory is used in discover and verify), so stage belongs on routine steps, not folders.
- Domain categories were ambiguous: structured-discussion sat in `meta` and ai-orchestration in `intelligence`, yet both produce decisions/verdicts.

## Status
Paused 2026-10-15 at Jesse's direction to classify the compute and data workloads first; see `claude/compute-and-data-workload-classification.md`.

## Parked
- Verdict thresholds (configurable per the design principle above).
- First increment format (taxonomy map vs. skill review cards vs. code).
- Placement of server-ops-orchestrator (dispatcher).
- Rename of `_shared/` and the other gap fixes above.
- RRFlow dependency-spine reorder: now the open decision in `claude/compute-and-data-workload-classification.md`.

text:
# DevPulse research ledger — facts bearing on rroflow.ai

Compiled 2026-10-25. Read-only scan of six GitHub repos plus Google Drive. One line per fact; source as `repo:path (date)` or `Drive: "title" (date)`. Repo dates are the file's last commit (first commit in brackets where it matters), taken from the GitHub REST commits API, because the clones are shallow. Where a doc carries its own date in its header, that date is given. Newer beats older; see the "Conflicts and superseded" section.

Repo abbreviations: **PD** = EonsofStupid/platform_devpulse (HEAD 2026-10-24), **LABS** = EonsofStupid/devpulselabs (HEAD 2026-10-25), **TEL** = EonsofStupid/devpulse-telemetry (HEAD 2026-06-28), **ALPHA** = EonsofStupid/devpulse_alpha (HEAD 2026-05-08), **TPL** = EonsofStupid/devpulse-template (HEAD 2026-08-17). LABS-H = devpulselabs at tag `docs-history-2026-10-12` (fetched read-only via the API).

---

## (a) Signal and telemetry definitions, event schemas, taxonomies

### Agent-run and AI-call events (most directly reusable)
- `AiEvent` is a stamped fabric domain with 4 variants, `CallStarted{call, provider, model, origin, observation}`, `FirstToken{call, ttft_ms}`, `CallFinished{call, tokens_in, cache_read, cache_write, tokens_out, total_tokens, context_used, context_size, cost_micros, duration_ms, outcome}` and `Disposition{call, kept, target}`, all keyed by `CallId`. — LABS:crates/fabric/src/lib.rs (2026-10-25)
- Every token count is `Option`. `None` means "provider did not say", which is not zero, "and must never be priced as zero". — LABS:crates/fabric/src/lib.rs (2026-10-25)
- Message content is deliberately absent from `AiEvent`. Prompts and responses go to a separate opt-in, credential-scrubbed store, joined by hash. — LABS:crates/fabric/src/lib.rs (2026-10-25); LABS-H:docs/plans/phase3-analytics-program.md §3.6 (2026-07-29)
- `AiOutcome = Ok | Refused | Cancelled | Error(AiFailureClass)`. A refusal is a valid answer, not a failure. — LABS:crates/fabric/src/lib.rs (2026-10-25)
- `AiFailureClass = Auth | RateLimit | Timeout | Transport | Protocol | Runtime | Server | Unknown`. — LABS:crates/fabric/src/lib.rs (2026-10-25)
- `Observation = Live | Backfilled`. Backfilled facts never carry `FirstToken` and must be excluded from latency and ordering queries ("a latency percentile over backfilled rows is refused, not approximated"). — LABS:crates/fabric/src/lib.rs (2026-10-25); LABS-H:phase3-analytics-program.md §3.2c (2026-07-29)

## (b) Learning-loop designs (supervised, unsupervised, recursive, evals, promotion)

- Self-generating training loop (locked Dec 25, 2025): log PSYCH/SCRIBE/TEACHER outputs, then capture the user reaction (ACCEPTED/EDITED/REJECTED/ABANDONED), write training pairs to DuckDB, train LoRA nightly, and promote weekly "if metrics improve". — PD:docs/claude.kb/training/NORMALIZER_TRAINING_SPEC.md (2026-04-06)
- "EDITED interactions are the BEST training data": the user's edit delta is the ground-truth correction. Quality scores: ACCEPTED 1.0, EDITED 0.7, REJECTED 0.0, ABANDONED −0.5. — PD:NORMALIZER_TRAINING_SPEC.md (2026-04-06)
- Translation-memory promotion: after 3 accepted uses at >0.8 confidence, a mapping becomes "auto-apply". — PD:NORMALIZER_TRAINING_SPEC.md (2026-04-06)
- learn-loop: log each error to `.claude/mistakes.md`, dedupe, count frequency, and promote to a rule at 3 occurrences. — PD:docs/claude.kb/build-queue/BUILDABLE_TOOLS.md (2026-03-31)
- "The slow path mints fast paths": tier 1 rules (regex, µs), then tier 2 similarity (encoder plus per-node classifiers), then tier 3 reasoning, which answers and mints a candidate tier-1 rule. — Drive: "RRFlow — Classification Compiler" (2026-09-24); "LFG_NOTES_v3" §4 (2026-09-26, LOCKED)
- Promotion posture: tier-3-minted rules land as `source: learned, is_active: false`, promoted in the Lab or by a hit-count threshold. User corrections (`memory.corrections`) also mint rules. "Nothing goes live on the model's say-so." — Drive: "RRFlow — Classification Compiler" §7 (2026-09-24, PROPOSED)
- Category lifecycle: narrated or minted → candidate → validated (grammar, sibling collision, exemplar count) → promoted (Lab or hit-count) → compiled into the next snapshot. Overrides of LFG answers are journaled as corrections, "which is the tuning signal". — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §2, §5 (2026-09-26)
- Supervised tier 2: classical ML (LR or GBM over TF-IDF, or a small encoder), trained per Choice node, with the journal as the labeled corpus. Disposable and rebuildable; low-probability answers still escalate. — Drive: "RRFlow + LFG — Notes v2.1 Addendum" A8 (2026-09-25, PROPOSED)
- Embeddings, not a single trained label classifier, "so new categories are new exemplars and not a retrain". — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §4 (2026-09-26)
- Research framing: "RAG isn't dead, it split". The open gap is "promoting into rules — cheap, inspectable, reversible, CPU-fast — is largely unbuilt". — Drive: "RRFlow — Classification Compiler" §12 (2026-09-24)
- Governance verification evaluators run in tier order (deterministic, then pattern, then similarity, then model for fuzzy checks only). Unevaluatable counts as fail; next step is `done | retry{attempt,max} | escalate`; "fail-then-pass pairs are promotion evidence". — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §8 (2026-09-26)
- Proof pattern (LOCKED): name the seam, freeze it with a golden file, prove it with an artifact CI keeps. "Anything not expressible this way is a guideline, not governance." — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §8 (2026-09-26)
- No fine-tune "until the journal holds thousands of real translations… Training first freezes guesses". Unsloth/LoRA "teaches format and vocabulary, not categorically different behavior". — Drive: "v2.1 Addendum" A11 (2026-09-25); "LFG_NOTES_v3" §15
- Closed-loop product shape (ratified 2026-07-28): observe (signals → ledger), understand (queries), then "recommend an action that can trigger the guided workflow itself… 'you really should do X' arrives with a button". Analytics "is a lens over the ledger files, never a store of record". — LABS-H:docs/plans/signal-ledger-and-lesson-foundation.md §9.1
- Determinism modes: Behavioral (default; the measurement mode, where A/B of lesson arms runs) and Strict (byte-identical evidence mode). Escalation is dynamic. — LABS-H:signal-ledger-and-lesson-foundation.md §9.2 (2026-07-28)
- Operator-intent gate: privileged transitions are authorized by keystroke provenance. "Model output is never re-parsed for commands", and `OperatorIntent` has no Clone, Default or serde. — LABS-H:signal-ledger-and-lesson-foundation.md §9.3 (2026-07-28)
- Experiment lifecycle: research note → feature-gated spike → journal PASS|KILL|AMEND → ADR only if law changes. Each manifest declares hypothesis, kill criteria, stamped signals and promotion target. — LABS-H:docs/plans/coach-lab-experiment-program.md (2026-07-31)
- Eval framework hypotheses: H1 context preservation (specialists vs generalist: success × token cost × latency); H2 handoff fidelity (typed A2A vs free-text); H3 KV-cache reuse (A/B LMCache on vs off). Tools named: VeriLA and promptfoo. — PD:scripts/docs/consolidation/LOCKED_DECISIONS.md §G (2026-05-13)
- Multi-LLM evidence gathered: majority voting accounts for most gains credited to debate; judge selection beat MoA synthesis; Self-MoA beat mixed MoA; multi-agent setups lose on sequential tasks; routers cut cost by 2× or more. Council output is "one selected answer, never a blend", with runner-up and dissent recorded. — LABS:docs/requirements.md R279 (2026-10-18); LABS:docs/plans/product-vision.md §2.3 (2026-10-20)
- Reversible hot-swap mechanism: encoder or adapter swapped atomically via ArcSwap, with pause → drain → load → validate → swap. If validation fails, it restores the old version. — PD:scripts/docs/specs/cortex/rro/RRD.md (v1.0.0, 2026-05-01); snapshot swap in Drive: "LFG_ENGINE_PLAN" §5 (2026-09-26)

## (e) Architecture decisions (Rust-first, local-first, storage, sync)

- Rust is the default; Python is allowed and is "the obvious choice for ML training, fine-tuning, and data pipelines" (owner 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-24). — PD:CLAUDE.md (2026-10-24)
- "AI = providers over endpoints": local runtimes are prebuilt, supervised subprocesses; subscriptions run the vendor's own CLI over ACP; "no new compiled-in inference". — PD:CLAUDE.md (2026-10-24)
- Local-first redefined as "a trust and latency property, not geography". Earlier code wrongly treated local-first as "no network" and cut the brain contract at token level. — Drive: "RRFlow — Classification Compiler" §9 (2026-09-24)
- PD storage today: Turso is SSOT; SurrealDB runs as a supervised subprocess "until RRFlow replaces it"; DuckDB handles analytics. — PD:CLAUDE.md (2026-10-24); PD:LOCKED_DECISIONS.md A-5 (superseded 2026-10-24)
- LABS storage: three rings (STATE `.userdata`, WORKING `assets`, CONFIRMED `content`). Turso holds metadata; analytics is Parquet, queried in-process by Arrow/DataFusion, and DuckDB is removed (owner 2026-08-03). — LABS:docs/design/adr-014-three-ring-root.md (amended 2026-08-03)
- DataFusion is not yet built; only the Parquet writer exists. Turso runs in-process with three DB files. — LABS:docs/requirements.md R276 (2026-10-13)
- Analytics port: `AnalyticsAdapter{name, health, query(Query)}` with a typed `Query` enum (`AiCost`, `EditorFriction`, `Timeline`…), not SQL strings; `RawSql` is an adapter-optional escape hatch. — LABS-H:phase3 §3.7 (2026-07-29)
- Redaction law: analytics consume redacted, versioned projections; credentials never reach any store. Scrub before hashing. Classification stores "the class, never the value"; HMAC handles identity without recovery. — LABS-H:phase3 §2.1a; LABS-H:signal-ledger-and-lesson-foundation §9.4–9.5
- Wide events over metrics for AI workloads; "for a local desktop app where the user IS the deployment, cardinality is free"; OTel is a view, not the write path. — PD:ADR-002 D8 (2026-04-15); Drive: "adr-turn-identity.md" D8
- Journal store per era: SQLite WAL in the Node era, fjall in the daemon era, with migration gated by a differential replay test. — Drive: "adr-turn-identity.md" D7 (2026-08-13)
- RRFlow (control plane) is dedicated AI persistence (Postgres behind a store trait) holding tree and revisions, rules, exemplars, journal, verdicts and model outcomes per address. It is bitemporal. Promotion runs against RRFlow, not inside it. — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §11 (2026-09-26, LOCKED role)
- LFG kernel is deterministic (same input plus same snapshot gives byte-identical output). Snapshot is heap-loaded with an atomic ArcSwap; tier-1 p99 target is < 1 ms. — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §2, §6; "LFG_ENGINE_PLAN" (2026-09-26)
- Schema source of truth is Rust-first: serde plus schemars produce JSON Schema, from which ArkType/Pydantic are generated. Shared fixtures must pass in all three. — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §7 (2026-09-26, PROPOSED)
- Agent-agnostic seam: thin provider hook stubs (Codex, Claude) normalize to a canonical `PromptSubmitted` event, then an agnostic seam, then a shared `EvaluationModalSpec` rendered conversationally and as a UI modal, then a pure reducer folds the validated event stream. — Drive: "Shippin — Agent-Agnostic Seam…" (2026-09-18)
- Older sync design: local-first memory with sync intake plus async heavy writes; enterprise sync via an outbox with checkpoints and idempotent apply to team Postgres/ClickHouse. — ALPHA:docs/architecture/adr-005, adr-010 (2026-05-08)
- RRO/RRD: in-process daemon, not a sidecar; "Cortex calls RRO. RRO does not call Cortex." — PD:scripts/docs/specs/cortex/rro/RRO.md (v2.0.1, 2026-05-20), RRD.md (2026-05-01)
- Shared telemetry crate is consumed by both the DevPulse desktop and `clyffyos` (headless daemon) via a git dep. — TEL:README.md (2026-06-28)

## (f) Product naming and positioning

- RRO is "also the standalone product sold via rroflow.ai to enterprise". The standalone test: "if you can sell a piece of functionality to enterprise (rroflow.ai) without the buyer also wanting Council/Fox/COSTAR+IC/minion personas — it belongs in RRO". Crates `kernel/rro-*` would be publishable to crates.io "for rroflow.ai customers". — PD:scripts/docs/specs/cortex/rro/RRO.md (v2.0.1, header 2026-05-20, last commit 2026-06-17)
- RRO vocabulary lock: RRO = "Reason Ready Object(s)"; "RRO = Orchestrator" is retired. — PD:RRO.md (2026-05-20)
- RRO reframed from "deep reasoning system / retrieval core" into a classification compiler, with first market "vibecoders — an environment where they grow into real developers". — Drive: "RRFlow — Classification Compiler" §1 (2026-09-24)
- Component names in prose: LFG, RRFlow, Dalal, Chatmaton, DevForge, Clyffy, Fox; never "the broker" or "the router". "Broker" became Dalal and "Judge" became Governance. — Drive: "LFG_NOTES_v3" §0, §12 (2026-09-26)
- Competitive notes: "Jev proves the market… Jev is one tier". Its gaps (hand-authored categories, no chaining, hosted, no teaching, no promotion loop) are described as RRFlow's moat. — Drive: "RRFlow — Classification Compiler" §4 (2026-09-24)
- Clyffy is "translator, not generator"; DevPulse "competes on success rate, cost protection, and architectural depth", not speed. — PD:scripts/docs/PHILOSOPHY.md (2026-04-19)
- Free-to-paid funnel: open-source `angryviber/claude-survival-kit` (verify-gate, psych-hook, learn-loop, hook-gen, claude-audit, context-pulse…) up-sells to DevPulse ("want them to talk to each other, remember your project, and get smarter over time?"). AngryViber blog angles include "Claude Code has a 30% lie rate". — PD:docs/claude.kb/build-queue/BUILDABLE_TOOLS.md (2026-03-31)
- Competitive gap on frustration: Claude Code makes it worse (apologetic mode); Cursor, Copilot, Bolt and Lovable don't detect it. — PD:EMOTIONAL_TRANSLATION_LAYER.md (2026-03-31)
- Naming laws: MAESTRO/Meistro/Gus are dead; Scribe was renamed Translator; the Council has 9 seats; "Minion" is the process term. — PD:LOCKED_DECISIONS.md §D (2026-05-13); PD:PHILOSOPHY.md
- Hosts in config: `rrflow.ai` is listed as a project site (PD:project.manifest.yml); `clyffy.rrflow.ai` and `api.rrflow.ai` sit behind Traefik/Authentik (ALPHA:docs/hosting/host-ownership-map.md, 2026-05); `oauth.rrflow.ai/mcp` is live (TPL:docs/ledger/poam.md, ~2026-07-29).
- No repo or Drive doc found describes rroflow.ai as "Sentry for your AI", or mentions Raindrop. The only rroflow.ai positioning in the sources is RRO-as-enterprise-substrate.

## (g) Superseded, outdated, and dated items

- DuckDB as the LABS analytics engine (R219, R239 of 2026-07-29) was superseded by R241 on 2026-08-03 (Arrow/DataFusion over Parquet). — LABS:docs/requirements.md; LABS:adr-014 amendment
- The "C libraries are subprocesses" claim was a prior-agent error and is not law; only ffmpeg *bindings* are denied. — LABS-H:phase3 §2.2 (2026-07-29)
- `ProviderEvent` was auth lifecycle only and chat crates had zero fabric calls, so "you cannot aggregate a sentence" (state as of 2026-07-29). `AiEvent` and usage adapters then landed 2026-08-03. — LABS-H:phase3 §1; LABS:crates/app/src/ai_usage.rs
- PD storage history: libSQL → Turso (owner 2026-07-01, "actually turso not libsql"). SurrealDB was "composed in, not forked" (05-13), then fork-and-own approved as RRFlow (2026-10-01), then upstream binary in a subprocess until RRFlow replaces it (2026-10-24). — PD:LOCKED_DECISIONS.md A-5, §I
- ALPHA ADR-009 (2026-05-08) named Postgres for transactional state, now superseded by Turso in PD and LABS.
- Normalizer spec storage (DuckDB training pairs, Turso `translation_memory`, 2026-04-06) has dead tables: plan 0004 C1 drops `attunement_*`, `translation_memory` and `expertise_level` in favour of a profile store (skill, lexicon, FSRS mastery). — PD:.plan/0004 (2026-10-12)
- PHILOSOPHY pillar 3, "Owning the forward pass is the moat" via Candle embedded (2026-04-19), conflicts with the current CLAUDE.md "no new compiled-in inference; local runtimes are supervised subprocesses" (2026-10-24, plan 0007).
- PD claude-integration API lanes with `cost_cap_daily_usd` and reqwest API keys (2026-04-06) predate the LABS subscription-only/no-API-key law (2026-07-23).
- LFG v1/v2/v2.1 superseded by v3 (2026-09-26): Judge moved into Governance, there are 5 operations not 3 answer types, Null became Gate, Broker became Dalal, the key excludes `@rev`, the snapshot is heap-loaded not memory-mapped, and version pins gave way to a latest-stable policy. The 177 rrd-core/rrd-lsm tests are "unit-only… not evidence that anything works end to end".
- Gemini CLI on consumer subscriptions ended 2026-06-18. The R280 "not yet: Antigravity" note was superseded the same day by R281. — LABS:docs/requirements.md
- Codex depot version gate `>=0.145.0,<0.146.0` caused a 400 error against the operator's 0.163.0 config (2026-10-19). An in-place, SHA-verified tool-update path is still missing. — LABS:docs/requirements.md R278, R283
- The 'baseline optimizing' goal in R213 (2026-07-25) "was never defined". — LABS:docs/requirements.md
- Claude Code countermeasure data comes from the v2.1.88 leak (2026-03-31). The current operator CLI is 2.1.296 (R283), so CC-001…CC-014 numbers may be stale.

---

## Conflicts and superseded (summary)

1. **What rroflow.ai is.** PD:RRO.md (2026-05-20) positions rroflow.ai as the enterprise channel for RRO, the reasoning/retrieval substrate. Drive notes (2026-09-24/26) reframe RRO/RRFlow as a classification compiler plus AI persistence (LFG, Governance, journal, promotion). Neither matches the current "Sentry for your AI" (capture, signals, spend, learning) framing; the closest pieces are the LABS AI ledger and usage adapters, and the Governance/journal/promotion design. The newest positioning needs its own canonical statement.
2. **Analytics engine.** PD keeps DuckDB (CLAUDE.md, 2026-10-24); LABS removed it for DataFusion over Parquet (2026-08-03), and DataFusion is still unbuilt. Two live repos disagree.
3. **Durable store for learning data.** Turso (PD/LABS) vs Postgres behind a trait (RRFlow, Drive 2026-09-26) vs SurrealDB (PD graph) vs fjall (journal daemon era, ADR-0001). Drive's open item "RRFlow vs Connectome / Qortex / Turso" is still unresolved.
4. **Learning mechanism.** April 2026: nightly LoRA adapters on 0.6B encoders from DuckDB pairs. September 2026: no fine-tune until thousands of journaled examples, with learning promoted into rules first and per-node classical classifiers second. The newer notes win.
5. **Inference location.** Candle in-process ("own the forward pass", April) vs endpoints and subprocesses (October). October wins.
6. **API keys.** Older PD lanes assumed API keys and daily USD caps. LABS law is subscription-only, and DevPulse never holds a key (Gemini on a paid API key is the one sanctioned exception). The Dalal doc also flags subscription routing through a third party as a terms risk.
7. **Persona and component names.** PSYCH/SCRIBE/TEACHER/ENFORCER/GUARDIAN/MAESTRO (March–April) vs Council seats Fox/Translator/Diary/Warden/Quincy (May) vs LFG/Fox/Dalal/Governance/RRFlow (September). Warden is "never a model", and Judge became Governance.
8. **Frustration-only vs bidirectional mood.** Early specs are negative-only (RAGE…NONE plus a `pos` flag). The owner's correction calls for a full positive-to-negative weight scale.

## Sources scanned

**Repos** (cloned shallow, read-only, into /home/claude/devpulse-research/):
- platform_devpulse — OK (HEAD 008546f, 2026-10-24). Read: docs/claude.kb/* (index, consolidated reference, emotional translation, tiers, buildable tools, normalizer spec, countermeasures, diff, prompt-extraction headings), scripts/docs/adr/ADR-002, scripts/docs/consolidation/LOCKED_DECISIONS.md, scripts/docs/specs/cortex/rro/RRO.md + RRD.md, scripts/docs/PHILOSOPHY.md, sprint docs (signals golden pattern, claude-integration S1/S2/POAM, dogfood day one), systems/devpulse-engine/ip/signals.registry.yaml, .plan/0001 and 0004, CLAUDE.md.
- devpulselabs — OK (HEAD 530dd17, 2026-10-25). Read: docs/requirements.md (§6 and §8 sections), docs/plans/product-vision.md, chat-provider-runtime-adr.md, docs/design/signal-doctrine.md, adr-014, docs/ops/references/signals-schema.md, crates/fabric, ledger, chat/store, chat/core, app/ai_usage, app/ai_backfill. Also, from tag `docs-history-2026-10-12` via the API: phase3-analytics-program.md, signal-ledger-and-lesson-foundation.md, coach-lab-experiment-program.md (fetched to /home/claude/devpulse-research/_history/devpulselabs/; providers-presence-and-the-brain, unified-ai-kernel-automaton-merge and workbench-experiments were fetched but not read).
- devpulse-telemetry — OK (HEAD 1f4c7d3, 2026-06-28). README plus crate layout.
- devpulse-labs — **empty repository** (no commits); nothing to scan.
- devpulse_alpha — OK (HEAD e57432f, 2026-05-08). docs/architecture ADR-004/005/009/010, hosting map.
- devpulse-template — OK (HEAD 89392de, 2026-08-17). docs/ledger/00-vision.md and rroflow grep. Mostly a Lovable/ColdLight template with little bearing on rroflow.

**Access notes:** `gh repo clone` failed (HTTP 403, GraphQL is blocked in this environment) and plain `git clone` failed (no credentials). All six repos were then attached with add_repo (read) and cloned with `git clone --depth 1`. Per-file dates came from the REST commits API. Nothing was modified or pushed. Secrets, .env files and node_modules were not read.

**Google Drive** (owner digi@angrygaming.org). Title searches for devpulse/telemetry/signals/rroflow/raindrop/vibecoder/learning matched only the folders DevPULSE_App and DevPULSE_News; the docs were found by full-text search. Read:

title: What we learned from Raindrop — findings for validation
description: Captured observations and lessons from Raindrop. Historical research, not a live feature claim.
text:
# What we learned from Raindrop — findings for validation

Prepared by Jesse (hades), RRFlow, 2026-10-24. Written to be read by Raindrop's team. Purpose: you tell us where we read your product right and where we read it wrong, so the learning layer we are designing (RROFLOW) borrows the right lessons and credits them correctly.

**Labels used on every claim.** `[public]` — read from raindrop.ai docs, blog, Query API OpenAPI, or the `raindrop-ai` GitHub org on 2026-10-24. `[observed]` — seen in our own workspace (project `rrflow-hydradb`). `[inferred]` — our reading, not stated by Raindrop. Nothing here was obtained by probing anything beyond public pages and our own account.

## 1. What we think Raindrop is

- Production observability for AI agents: events (one turn: input, tool calls, output), OTLP traces linked to events, signals that label events, issues and stumbles discovered automatically, experiments over logged cohorts, a Triage agent, Workshop for local debugging, an MCP server, a Query API. `[public]`
- The mechanism that matters most to us is Signals 2.0 (rd-signal-2, 2026-08-11): for each described behaviour an agent writes numbered policy rules and compiles a classifier as `run(event)` code that gathers evidence deterministically, early-returns non-matches without a model call, and sends only ambiguous candidates with compact context to a task-specific classification head plus an in-house reasoning model; isolated per-customer sandbox without credentials or egress; context fetched once and cached near workers; 100 ms median per trace; more than 20 billion traces a month; daily frontier-model audits of a sample with retune on regression; customers can read and edit the code and prompt. `[public: blog "Signals 2.0 — frontier-grade classification"]`
- Your published benchmark: precision 71 % and recall 87 % at 1× relative per-trace cost, against 78 % / 91 % at 260× for the best frontier judge. `[public: same post]`
- Phrasing sensitivity you published: four one-sentence phrasings of one behaviour over 2,000 traces matched 0.9–4.6 %, and 67 % of traces matched by one phrasing were rejected by another. `[public: same post]`
- Issue Detection v2 (2026-06-03): stumbles (one failed run, tagged, scan cadence) → issues (recurrence across runs and users, severity, overrepresented tools/models/signals, timeline) → signals. The two catalogs are disjoint. `[public: blog "Introducing Raindrop 2", MCP tool reference]`
- Experiments compare cohorts of already-logged events and never run the agent; "likely better/worse" needs a 95 % CI excluding zero and a sample check. `[public: docs/platform/experiments]`
- Change Reports scope traffic by `raindrop.app.commit_sha` and report ~24 h after a merge; Simulations (early access) replay production traffic against a harness change on every PR. `[public: docs/platform/change-reports; Series A post]`
- Storage: Tinybird and ClickHouse appear in your subprocessor list, RQL is a ClickHouse dialect, and the Rust SDK comments mention Tinybird's strict typing. `[public]` That events and traces are served from ClickHouse-family storage behind Tinybird is `[inferred]`.
- Our own integration: real events and feedback signals from our prototype arrived and read back in the UI on 2026-10-12 (project `rrflow-hydradb`). `[observed]`

## 2. Where we may have you wrong — please correct

1. `signals[].score` on an event: we read it as classifier probability; range and threshold are not public. `[inferred]`
2. The `event` object API inside generated signal code (`event.trace`, `findToolCalls`, `haveIdenticalInputs`, `formatForReview`, `classify(..., {spanIds})`): we have one blog example only. `[public, one example]`
3. How stumbles cluster into issues and what "Similar" uses. `[not public]`
4. How `topics[]` are generated and whether the taxonomy is per project and editable. `[not public]`
5. Whether the Signals 2.0 API / ZDR Signals / Signal Builder exposes a callable classifier outside the ingest path. `[public mention only; docs page 404]`
6. `track_partial` server-side merge semantics for conflicting fields. `[not public]`
7. Whether Rust/Go SDKs will carry `feature_flags` and `ai_data.tool_calls` on the wire (TypeScript and HTTP do today). `[public: absent from both repos]`

## 3. What RRFlow is, stated plainly

RRFlow is a local-first Rust engine (`github.com/rrflow/rrflow-development`, public, MIT OR Apache-2.0) that keeps one project's memory, graph, vectors and reasoning evidence in one bi-temporal store (rrflowDB on rrflowKV), with a System One controller (SWAG) deciding which model endpoint handles a prompt, and a learning configuration (RROFLOW) that is specified but unimplemented. Status today, in our own repo's words: storage gates A–C are the only checked gates; prompt flights and task records exist; no production generations are recorded yet; no benchmark against anything exists; our acceptance standard calls the product "0.0" until the UI drives a frontier model through rrflowDB memory end to end. We are not claiming to be faster, more accurate or cheaper than Raindrop; we have no numbers.

**Different, not better.** Raindrop observes agents running anywhere, at scale, as a hosted service. RRFlow is the engine an agent's memory and reasoning run *inside*, on the developer's own machine or in a shippin.cloud devspace, on the developer's own model subscriptions. The learning loop we want sits on evidence the engine already owns (every flight is a graph with edges to the records it used, at a read stamp). What we borrow from you is the mechanism discipline; what we add is that the classifier's evidence step is a declarative query over a temporal graph, replayable at any historical stamp.

## 4. What we intend to borrow, with credit

| Raindrop mechanism | RRFlow record | What changes in our design |
|---|---|---|
| Compile once, run deterministically, model only on ambiguous cases | behaviour signal = rrflowQL evidence program + LFG tier-2 judge escalating through SWAG | the evidence program is a query at a read stamp, not generated JS |
| Label a sample, not a checklist; ≤25 seeds, ≤500 refinement examples | Governance-family verdict records with those bounds as configuration | labels never inferred from aggregates |
| Daily frontier audit, retune as a revision | scheduled routine proposing a new definition revision | never auto-promotes |
| Stumbles ≠ issues; scan cadence with "as of" | two disjoint finding kinds; routine checkpoint stamp | cluster = hypothesis until a person acts |
| Ignore reasons as data | finding status with reason feeding refinement | |
| Cohort experiments, CI-excluding-zero verdict | cohort experiment + verdict record naming its method | method is declared configuration |
| Change Reports by commit | flight carries project-snapshot digest/commit; before/after routine | |
| Replay-server contract (`/health`, `/replay`, stitched ids) | outward adapter for agents running outside the engine | |
| Datasets as labelled snapshots | labelled evidence set pinned to a read stamp with consent and split manifest | |
| Per-project model isolation | per-estate definitions and judges | |

## 5. The proposition

Raindrop as a **class-7 endpoint binding** in RRFlow's profile: an `rrflow-raindrop` adapter exports flights as `events/track_partial` plus OTLP spans and reads your labels and findings back through the Query API or MCP. Developers on shippin.cloud bring their own Raindrop subscription the way they bring their own model subscriptions; your classifiers label our flights before ours exist, and when ours exist they are measured against yours on the same flights. We want that comparison to be possible, public and fair.

## 6. Three questions for the meeting

1. Is the `run(event)` helper API something you would publish or stabilise, or is it intentionally managed?
2. For an engine that already stores every turn as a graph, would you rather receive OTLP spans or a richer event with `tool_calls[]` and attachments?
3. Would a documented export path (events, traces, signals, verdicts) for a customer's own project be acceptable to you — it is what makes the two-way comparison honest.

## Sources

Public: https://raindrop.ai/docs (68 pages via `/docs/llms.txt`), https://raindrop.ai/blog/signals-2-frontier-classification/, https://raindrop.ai/blog/introducing-raindrop-2/, https://raindrop.ai/blog/series-a/, https://query.raindrop.ai/v1/openapi.json, https://github.com/raindrop-ai (workshop, raindrop-rust, go, raindrop-swift, skills, pi-agent, claude-code-plugin), https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/raindrop. Observed: our workspace, project `rrflow-hydradb`, 2026-10-12 read-back. Full sourced ledger available on request.

title: Raindrop live-capture checklist (logged-in workspace)
description: Captured observations and lessons from Raindrop. Historical research, not a live feature claim.
text:
# Raindrop live-capture checklist (logged-in workspace)

Purpose: the public material in `raindrop-source-ledger.md` covers wire formats, MCP tool surfaces, and the published architecture of rd-signal-2. What follows is NOT visible publicly and has to be captured from inside a logged-in app.raindrop.ai workspace (Pro trial is 14 days; Hobby exposes Signals but locks Issues/Stumbles/Experiments). Priority: P0 = blocks the learning-layer spec; P1 = shapes the spec materially; P2 = nice to have. Each item says why it matters for a layer that mints classifiers from traces.

Capture method per item: screenshot the UI state, copy any JSON/code shown, and where an MCP/Query API call exists, save the raw response (`get_signal`, `get_event`, `get_trace`, `list_signals`, `get_signal_creation_status`, `GET /v1/signals/{id}`). Record the project slug and timestamp with every capture.

## P0 — Signal definition & classifier minting

- [ ] **Signal creation card, every step** (New Signal → agent drafting → review → rules → create). Capture the full text of the numbered policy rules the agent writes, the chat transcript, and the step list the card tracks. *Why:* this is the human-readable "definition" artifact a learning layer must produce before compiling code; its structure (how many rules, scope statements, turn-vs-conversation framing) is the target schema for our definition object.
- [ ] **"Preview classifier code" contents for ≥3 signals** (one tool-pattern signal, one pure-language signal, one preset turned on). Copy the JS verbatim. *Why:* the only public example (`run(event)` → `findToolCalls` → `classify(...)`) is from a blog post; we need the real helper API (`event.trace`, `event.finalResponse`, `findToolCalls`, `haveIdenticalInputs`, `formatForReview`, `classify` signature incl. `spanIds`) to design an equivalent evidence-gathering DSL.
- [ ] **Review panel mechanics**: how many matched events are surfaced per scan, the "why it matched" explanation text, whether labels are per-event or per-span, and what "Run Again" changes in the rules. Count how many Match/Not-Match labels you give before "Create signal" enables. *Why:* fixes the few-shot budget and the label granularity our active-learning loop should mirror.
- [ ] **`get_signal_creation_status` responses over time** for one creation (`phase`, `scan.scanned_total`, `scan.matched_total`, `progress.*`). Save each poll. *Why:* reveals batch sizes, sample size scanned per revision, and the preparing→scanning→reviewing→installing state machine we would reproduce.
- [ ] **Signal detail page for a live `code` signal**: definition, description, sentiment, group, occurrence count, user count, trend chart buckets, events table columns, and the "Refine Signal" dialog (what is pre-seeded: current definition + all prior verdicts). *Why:* the refinement loop is where human labels accumulate; we need to know what state is carried between revisions.
- [ ] **Signal object from Query API `GET /v1/signals/{id}` and MCP `get_signal`** for one signal of each `type` (`topic`, `regex`, `instrumented`, `metric`, `code`). *Why:* confirms field set per type and whether classifier code/prompt/version is exposed via API (public schema shows only id/type/name/description/created_at/group/sentiment).
- [ ] **`signals[].score` on `GET /v1/events/{id}`** for several events matched by one signal; note range (0–1? logits?), whether deterministic-branch matches have a fixed score, and whether non-matches ever appear. *Why:* determines whether we can threshold/rank matches or only treat them as boolean labels.
- [ ] **Backfill behaviour**: after creating a signal, record how many of the last 90 days got labelled and the sampling ratio visible in the trend (events labelled vs total). *Why:* sets expectations for cold-start rate estimation in our layer.
- [ ] **Edit-code / edit-prompt affordance** mentioned in the Signals 2.0 post ("customers can inspect and edit the code and prompt"). Find it in the UI; capture what is editable and whether edits trigger re-scan. *Why:* tells us whether the classifier is a user-owned artifact or a managed one.

## P0 — Issue grouping & intent taxonomy

- [ ] **Issue detail page** (Pro): severity, status, affected event/user counts, affected dimensions (overrepresented tools/models/signals), timeline, report text, related events, and the Slack prompt block. Save `get_issue`, `get_issue_events`, `get_issue_timeseries` JSON. *Why:* the issue report is the "distribution-shift" grouping output; its dimensions tell us which features (tool, model, signal, flag) the grouper keys on.
- [ ] **Stumble detail + Similar panel**: tag vocabulary (collect every tag seen: Logic Error, Hallucination, …), timeline-of-key-moments format, and `search_stumbles` raw JSON incl. `cadence_minutes`/`last_run_at`. *Why:* the tag set is the implicit failure taxonomy; the cadence tells us the detection latency budget to match.
- [ ] **Topics**: find where `topics[]` surface in the UI (event sidebar? filters?), list the full topic vocabulary for the project, and check whether topics are editable/mergeable. *Why:* this is the closest thing to an intent taxonomy; we must know whether it is open-vocabulary or a fixed per-project set.
- [ ] **Conversation summaries** (Pro): format, length, and whether they are queryable. *Why:* a summary is a candidate compact context for cheap classification.
- [ ] **"Turn issue into a Signal"** path (blog claims any detected issue can become a Signal). Capture the pre-filled intent and seed examples. *Why:* the issue→signal handoff is exactly "mint a classifier from a cluster of traces".

## P1 — Experiments, replay, verification

- [ ] **Experiment builder**: cohort condition types (model, flag, property, tool, date), outcome signal picker, Events %/Users % toggle, verdict, 95 % CI / p-value tooltip text, Event Stats rows (cost per event median, tools, duration, errors). Save `get_experiment` JSON. *Why:* defines the minimum statistical verification our layer must offer to prove a minted classifier's rate moved after a fix.
- [ ] **Change Report** sample (connect a GitHub repo to a test project): early-check and full-report text, which agent-harness changes were detected. *Why:* shows how they attribute behaviour change to code change via `raindrop.app.commit_sha`.
- [ ] **Workshop replay UI**: the replay form fields (user message, model, system prompt, context prefill), the stitched original-vs-replay view, and `/api/replay` SSE events. *Why:* replay is how a minted classifier gets validated against a candidate fix locally.
- [ ] **Dataset workspace**: label set, custom-row upload format (CSV columns), CSV export columns, "find more like these" via Triage. *Why:* datasets are the labelled-example store; export columns tell us what a training row contains.

## P1 — Settings & plan limits

- [ ] **Settings → API Keys**: key types (write key, personal query key, org-wide key), scopes shown, "Limit to owners and admins" toggle. *Why:* defines the auth model we need to interoperate with (ingest vs query vs MCP).
- [ ] **Settings → Billing**: event counters, signal-slot usage, Triage message usage, overage display. *Why:* confirms metering units (one event = one turn incl. tool calls and sub-agents).
- [ ] **Settings → PII Playground**: redaction categories and toggles. *Why:* redaction categories constrain what text a classifier can see.
- [ ] **Settings → Filters → User Exclusions** and internal-traffic flag (`is_internal`, `is_excluded_user` columns). *Why:* our layer needs the same exclusion semantics so rates match.
- [ ] **Settings → Notifications**: Daily Digest, Signal Alerts thresholds (users/events/every match), Change Reports max-per-day. *Why:* alert thresholds are the operational contract for a signal.
- [ ] **Settings → Triage Agent → Use all projects**, and project switcher behaviour for All projects. *Why:* scoping rules for cross-project learning.
- [ ] **Projects page**: "Projects with data, not yet created" list and per-org slug limit (number). *Why:* we rely on ingest-first project creation; the limit is undocumented.

## P1 — Event & trace views

- [ ] **Event sidebar**: every field shown (input/output, attachments tabs, matched signals with scores, properties, feature flags, user traits, system prompt snapshot, tools map, cost). *Why:* the per-event feature vector available to classifiers.
- [ ] **Trace view**: span tree, span types present (incl. synthetic SYSTEM_PROMPT), payload truncation behaviour, sub-agent nesting. Save `get_trace` with and without `include_context`. *Why:* defines the evidence a code classifier can walk.
- [ ] **Events filter chips**: full list of filterable fields (user, conversation, date, property, model, tool, signal, flag, trait). *Why:* candidate cohort keys.

## P2 — Export, retention, misc

- [ ] **Data export** (Pro feature named in plans): locate it, capture format (CSV/JSON/Parquet?) and scope (events? traces? signals?). *Why:* bulk export is how we would bootstrap a learning layer from existing Raindrop data.
- [ ] **Users CSV export columns**. *Why:* user-level features (plan, traits, signals).
- [ ] **Retention enforcement**: on Hobby, confirm events older than 14 days disappear from Events/Query API. *Why:* training-window constraint.
- [ ] **Memory UI** (Pro): what memories look like, how Triage cites them. *Why:* customer-specific context injected into classification/triage.
- [ ] **Tool Errors tab** on Signals: how auto-derived tool-error signals are named and grouped. *Why:* a free, label-free signal family worth mirroring.
- [ ] **Self Diagnostics tab**: how `agent` signals render, category breakdown. *Why:* agent self-reports are high-precision seeds for classifiers.
- [ ] **Dashboards**: built-in Usage board panels and a saved dashboard's `get_dashboard` JSON (panel kinds, visualizations, filter kinds). *Why:* reveals the RQL queries Raindrop itself uses for rates.
- [ ] **Signals 2.0 API / ZDR Signals**: ask support or sales for docs; capture any endpoint for calling a trained classifier on arbitrary input. *Why:* would show whether classifiers are callable outside the ingest path.

title: Raindrop live capture — Jesse's workspace, read through the Query API
description: Captured observations and lessons from Raindrop. Historical research, not a live feature claim.
text:
# Raindrop live capture — Jesse's workspace, read through the Query API

Date 2026-10-24. Key type: Query API key (read). Write probe → 401; `GET /v1/projects` → 200. Projects: `default` (Production), `rrflow-hydradb`. Raw JSON in this folder. Nothing was written to the workspace.

## Workspace contents
- **default**: 12 signals, 26 events (2026-10-11 → 10-13). Signal types `instrumented` (7) and `code` (5). The code signals are Attempted Prompt Injection, User Frustration, Churn Intent, Capability Gaps and Repeated Tool Call Failures, each with a one-line description and Negative sentiment. No event in the window matched a code signal. [observed: default-signals.json]
- **rrflow-hydradb**: 2 instrumented signals (Brain ui helpful, Answer helpful), 207 events (10-12 → 10-24). Event names: workspace_sync 96, brain_ui_generated 53, brain_recall 28, github_repository_sync 14, verification_evidence_captured 12. `model` is null on every event, `topics[]` is empty on every event, and `tool_calls` lists `hydradb.query`. [observed]
- Signal groups are per project and seeded as Negative, Other, Positive. [observed]

## Facts answered by observation (closing ledger open questions)
1. `signals[].score` is **absent/null on instrumented signals**. A score exists only where a classifier produced the match. Closes part of open question 3. [observed: events]
2. `GET /v1/signals/{id}` for a `code` signal returns only id, type, name, description, created_at, group and sentiment. **Classifier code is not exposed through the Query API.** [observed: sig-code-prompt-injection.json]
3. Trace rows from `/v1/traces` carry: attributes, duration_ns, start/end_time_ns, input, output, input/output_tokens, model, provider, parent_span_id, span_id, span_name, span_type, status, trace_id. A brain_recall event shows 2 spans: an `LLM_GENERATION` root with no model, and a `TOOL_CALL` child. [observed: trace-brain_recall.json]
4. Events sent without OTLP spans (harness_run, vibeguard chat) return 0 trace rows; their `tool_calls` come from the SDK interaction instead. [observed]
5. **Evals are gated per organization**: `/v1/evals*` and `/v1/eval-datasets/*` return 403 "Evals is not enabled for this organization." `/v1/replays/manifest?dataset=` returns 400 "No dataset named …" (the route exists). [observed]

## The SDK eval surface (read from `raindrop-ai@1.0.2` type definitions and dist; not executed)
- Exports include: `publishEvalDataset`, `readEvalDataset`, `defineDataset`, `defineLocalEvaluator` (output boolean | score | number | preference), `defineEvaluatorProgram` (`executionMode: deterministic | judge`, `intent`, `rules[]`, `source`), `defineEvalSuite` (dataset + evaluators with thresholds + `run` or `agent`, concurrency), `runEvalSuite`, `createEvalSuiteRun`, `readEvalRun`, `evaluateEvalRun` ("regrade captured traces with hosted evaluators; does not call the agent again"), `compareEvalRuns` (returns `sameEvaluatorVersion`), `pullEval` and `loadEvalSnapshot` (pin dataset + evaluator artifacts to JSON, reload offline), `importPortableEvaluator`, `evaluatePortableEvaluator`, `verifyPortableEvalArtifact`, `replay` / `runReplay` / `claimReplay` / `createEvalHandler` / `defineAgent`, `traceTools.getOutput/getToolCalls` ("never execute tools").
- **Portable evaluator artifact**: `{format: "raindrop.eval-program", formatVersion: 1, runtimeAbi: "raindrop-eval-v3", evaluator: {id, slug, programVersion, executionMode, outputType, scope: "trace"}, traceProjectionVersion: 1, traceProjectionSha256, source, sha256}`. The SDK pins its trace projection (`TRACE_PROJECTION_SHA256 = 243e3954…721c`) and refuses an artifact built against another projection.
- **Guest ABI**: the source runs in QuickJS (quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0). It must define global `__raindrop_eval_run(inputJson)` and return `{type:"result", result}`. It can call host `__raindrop_eval_judge(requestJson)` with `{type:"judge_request", requestId, traceId, rubric (≤40,000 chars), text (≤4 MiB), outputType: boolean|score|preference}`. **The judge is a host callback the caller binds**: `PortableJudge(request) → {pass} | {score 1–5} | {value} | {preference A|B|tie}`.
- Sandbox defaults: memory 32 MiB, stack 64 KiB, program timeout 1 s, judge timeout 60 s, judge request timeout 30 s, judge concurrency 4, max input and output 4 MiB each.
- Eval run results carry `tracesExpireAt` / `tracesExpired`, so captured traces for eval runs expire.
- Endpoints called by the SDK: `/v1/evals/{slug}`, `/v1/evals/{slug}/runs`, `/v1/evals/{slug}/local`, `/v1/evals/{slug}/runs/local`, `/v1/eval-datasets/{slug}[/versions/{id}]`, `/v1/eval-runs/{id}?include=traces`, `/v1/eval-runs/{a}/compare/{b}`, `/v1/replays[/{id}][/claim|/report|/trace]`, `/v1/replays/manifest?dataset=`, `/v1/traces`.

## vibeguard: Jesse's own recursive-improvement experiment on Raindrop (`EonsofStupid/vibeguard`, harness in `web/src/server/harness/`)
- Loop: run 16 frozen tasks (10 train / 6 held-out) → a guard blocks candidate code that matches approved rules → a deterministic judge grades the result → failures on **train only** propose a rule → a human approves or reverts (gate: agents may only tighten; only humans approve, loosen or revert; every transition writes the rule plus an audit receipt). Raindrop receives `harness.run` interactions, `rule_proposed` events, feedback signals `rule_approved` / `rule_reverted`, an edit signal `rule_narrowed`, self-diagnostics per training failure, and agent self-grades `heldout_improved / flat / regressed`. [source + observed]
- Observed history:

| Runs | Rules active | Held-out | Train |
|---|---|---|---|
| run_001–003 | none | 1/6 (CI 0.03–0.56) | 1/10 |
| run_004–006 | VG-0001, VG-0002, VG-0003 | 6/6 (CI 0.61–1) | 9/10 |
| run_007 | VG-0002, VG-0003 (VG-0001 reverted by a human) | 4/6 (CI 0.30–0.90), signal heldout_regressed | 6/10 |
| run_008–018 | VG-0002, VG-0003, VG-0004 (narrowed from VG-0001, `warn`) | 4/6 for 11 straight runs | 7/10 |

- **Why it plateaued (from `loop.ts`)**: proposals are made only for categories with no non-reverted rule. VG-0004 covers `cost.unbounded_api_calls` with a literal pattern of the one failing snippet and action `warn`, so the category counts as covered, the proposer goes silent, and held-out never recovers. Two reverts in a category silence it permanently.
- Other defects visible in the trace:
  - The same 6 held-out tasks were evaluated across 18 runs, so the holdout is contaminated.
  - n = 6 gives a 95 % interval of 0.30–0.90, too wide to tell 4/6 from 6/6.
  - "heldout_flat" is filed in the Positive group, so a stalled loop reads as good news.
  - The eval-replay path (`raindrop-evals.ts`) could never have run, because Evals is disabled for the org.

## Lessons for RROFLOW (each added to the spec)
1. Coverage is not effectiveness. A category with an active rule must reopen for proposals when held-out stays below its best observed level for N runs. Effectiveness is measured, not assumed from coverage.
2. A human revert is a negative verdict on that rule's revision, not a permanent block on the category. Silencing needs its own explicit, revocable decision.
3. A held-out set used to accept a revision is spent. Rotate or version it (the learning contract already requires this; vibeguard shows the cost of skipping it).
4. Minimum sample per decision: state the interval and refuse "improved/regressed" verdicts the interval cannot support.
5. Sentiment of a self-grade must follow its meaning: flat is neutral, not positive.
6. Raindrop's portable evaluator (program + bound judge + pinned trace projection + content hash + sandbox limits) is the closest existing artifact to the spec's R3. RRFlow's equivalent is a behaviour-signal revision whose evidence program is rrflowQL, whose judge is an endpoint binding, and whose identity is a digest.
