text:
# RRFlow merge train, 2026-10-19/20

Status record for the merges Jesse approved on 2026-10-19 ("i gave you my approval … done right no exceptions no shortcuts", then "merge it"). Supersedes the matching open-PR lines in `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` (Status section, 2026-10-18).

## Landed on `rrflow/rrflow-development` main

Every PR was brought up to date with main by a merge commit (no force push), passed candidate CI 17/17 on that exact head, and was merged pinned to it. Since 2026-10-19 a `main` ruleset enforces this. It requires a PR, the `pipeline / ci-gate` check, a branch that is up to date with main, and resolved threads.

| PR | Merge commit | What |
|---|---|---|
| #17 | `9bcc6154` | H-06a: prompt flights governed inside `RrdEngine`; POAM-032 |
| #18 | `13ce3386` | H-06b: every prompt flight a graph rrflowQL traverses. Its commit-time constraint gap is **POAM-034**: it was first numbered POAM-033, but #26 landed a different POAM-033 first. |
| #19 | `553f6754` | H-06c: named task records that flights join. The catalogue has 41 HTTP operations after #26's `data-schema-read`. |
| #21 | `36e3bc78` | E-01a: rrflowQL traversal through native temporal adjacency. OpenAPI `97156c7cbc21414e918825ea3e777795ed007552e2c091d6a38f18911b951b11`. |
| #22 | `f948abb1` | rrflowDB capability plan, reconciled: prompt graph families are **H-09** and project links are **H-10**; SQL access is deferred to H-08 |
| #28 | `ccad7869` | B-04a: the real-server WebSocket test accepts the in-flight delivery that can precede `unsubscribed` |

Merged in parallel by other work on Jesse's account, not by this session: #20 (Connectome UI submodule at `connectome/`), #26 (rrflowDB local integration, native schema discovery, and the PostgreSQL compatibility contract as H-08), and #27 (Connectome turnkey workbench).

## Decisions and corrections this changed

- **PostgreSQL is H-08, owned by `docs/reference/protocol/postgresql.md` (from #26).** Its packages are H-08a to H-08h, and it puts the wire adapter inside `rrd-server`.
  - Decision 12 still stands: rrflowDB has a Postgres-wire face.
  - The build-order doc's wording, "an adapter crate (pgwire + DataFusion over rrflowDB)", is superseded.
  - #22's own SQL-face plan was removed when it merged. It had proposed a separate `rrflow-postgres` crate, `SET rrflow.valid_at` session settings, and repeatable-read-only transactions. The landed contract contradicts all three: it forbids an adapter-owned ambient snapshot and requires READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ.
- **POA&M numbers on main.**
  - POAM-032 is prompt flights (#17).
  - POAM-033 is rejected native commits retaining an unabortable intent (#26).
  - POAM-034 is commit-time schema constraints loading the whole scope (#18).
  - Open PR #16 also claims POAM-032 (external knowledge providers), so its record must renumber to POAM-035 when it is updated.
- **A test race on main is fixed (#28).**
  - The race lived in `rust_client_negotiates_authenticates_queries_and_reads_audit`, in `rrd-client/tests/real_server.rs`.
  - It failed 27 of 60 runs under CPU contention on main's tree, and once in candidate CI on #19.
  - The server's socket loop can send a delivery poll before it reads an `unsubscribe`. Nothing can follow `unsubscribed`, because the subscription is removed before the reply.
  - With the fix it failed 0 of 150 contention runs. `docs/reference/protocol/subscriptions.md` now states the ordering.

## Still open after this train

- E-01 is still open: context graph expansion and memory-estate seat planning still materialize a snapshot (POAM-005).
- The rrflowDB record's open decisions block M2 and L1:
  - who may accept a link when one owner holds both projects;
  - whether prompt graph families can be defined at runtime or only bundled;
  - default retention per family.
- PR #16 conflicts with main: POAM renumbering, the endpoint catalogue, and the OpenAPI digest.
- PR #23 records the ruleset (POAM-027e).
- Devagotchi PR #2 was not part of this approval.

## Lessons for later sessions

- **Generated files versus hand-written files.** A generated file (SDK projections, the file plan, indexes) may take one side and then be regenerated. A hand-written file must never be resolved by taking one side whole, because that silently drops the other side's edits. Resolve it hunk by hunk.
  - This happened once with `rrd-contract/src/lib.rs`. Strict clippy caught it before the push.
- **Shared Cargo target directory across git worktrees.** Cargo's metadata hash for path dependencies does not include the path, so builds from another checkout can be reused stale. Touch `crates/**/*.rs` whenever builds switch checkouts.
- **Count conflicts.** When both sides add operations, set the endpoint and typed-method counts from the merged contract export, not from either side.
- **Rehearse and re-root.** Rehearse an integration against the head the next merge will produce, then create the real merge commit with that exact tested tree and the real main as its parent. Confirm the main tree equals the rehearsed tree first.

title: rrflow.ai public site — spec and build order
description: Engine and Connectome context. RRFlow is a separate product from the RROFLOW monitoring dashboard.
text:
# rrflow.ai public site — spec and build order

Date: 2026-10-19. Asked by Jesse: a true public web app that captures the eye and explains RRFlow (reasoning engine, RROFLOW, rrflowQL, rrflowDB, rrflowKV) with stimulating visuals, available through DevPulse and shippin.cloud. Visual concept: the Design canvas "RRFlow public site concept" (dark instrument look, six scenes). This record is the architecture, the data flow from a public demo estate, the ops item that serves it, and the build order. No visuals here.

Code basis: `rrflow/rrflow-development` `main` at `13ce338` (PR #18 merged 2026-10-19; PR #19 tasks not yet merged), read-only shallow clone. Every engine fact below names its file.

## Decided (2026-10-19)
- Surface: a public web app at rrflow.ai, separate from Connectome; Connectome remains the client, the site remains the story.
- Fidelity rule carried over from the design pass: every live panel reads a real estate; anything the engine does not serve yet is a labeled planned state, never sample data. The published concept marks its own sample panels "SAMPLE"; the built site has none.
- The site never exposes RRFlow to the browser. A gateway on the same host as the engine calls the loopback endpoint with a read-only principal; the browser talks only to the gateway.
- **Decision 1 — repository and names (Jesse, 2026-10-19):** `github.com/rrflow/site-development`, sibling of `rrflow-development` and `connectome-development`, bound to one engine revision by a pin, no submodule. Folders and naming as in "Names" below.
- **Decision 2 — stack (Jesse, 2026-10-19):** Rust gateway (axum + `rrd-client`) and an Astro static site with islands. Rejected: Next.js route handlers with `@rrflow/rrd-client` (credential in a Node process; one language) — revisit only if the Rust gateway slows the site down in practice.
- **Decision 3 — demo-estate host (Jesse, 2026-10-19):** a small VPS running `rrflow serve` + the gateway, static assets on an edge/CDN. Rejected: Gold behind a tunnel (home-network exposure, uptime dependence); Devstation (LAN only).

## Open
- Step 0 bootstrap is the next increment (see Build order). Repository creation under the `rrflow` org is Jesse's action or an explicitly authorized one from his workstation; local scaffolding lands at `D:\localdev\site-development` on Gus (separate folder under `D:\localdev`, like `rrflow` and `connectome`).
- VPS provider, region and size; the edge/CDN; the DNS cut-over for rrflow.ai — chosen when step 1 starts.

## Facts the architecture rests on

| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| `rrflow serve` binds loopback only: `RrdHttpServer::bind` returns `RemoteBindDenied` for any non-loopback address; the network path is `bind_mtls` (mutual TLS) | `crates/transport/rrd-server/src/http/server.rs:73-95` |
| Endpoint presentations are `in_process`, `loopback_http_websocket`, `network_http_websocket`; a network endpoint "requires the accepted authenticated encrypted transport" and is "an explicit configuration addition" | `docs/reference/deployment/modes.md:34-60` |
| Principals (user, service, node) carry credential-verifier digests, validity windows, direct grants and roles; a grant binds an action to a resource prefix; most-specific grants apply; the installer generates one high-entropy API key; initial principals come from the install plan | `docs/reference/security/authority.md:62-72, 176-187, 221-263` |
| Security actions include `ServiceInspect`, `SessionCreate/Renew/Close`, `DiagnosticsRead`, `FlightRead`, `MemoryContextRead`, `QueryExecute`, `ChangefeedRead`, `ChangefeedFollow`, `VectorSearch`, `VectorCollectionList`, `VectorPointRetrieve`, `VectorPointScroll`, `EstateRead` — a read-only grant set exists | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/lib.rs` (`SecurityAction`) |
| 37 public operations at `13ce338`, including `capabilities-read`, `endpoint-catalogue`, `diagnostics-read`, `flight-launch/list/read`, `context-assemble`, `query-execute`, `changefeed-read`, `changefeed-follow`, `subscription-open/close`, `vector-search` | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/lib.rs` (operation catalogue) |
| `ProductCapabilityCatalogue`: per capability, one `SurfaceBinding` per surface with disposition `Available | Planned | Denied | Unavailable`, entrypoints and a reason; built from the endpoint catalogue plus six named capabilities; Connectome surface `Planned` everywhere ("scheduled by H-06"); no LFG, SWAG or RROFLOW row | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/capability_surface.rs:10-79`; `crates/authority/rrd-engine/src/capabilities.rs:6-99` |
| `AssembleContext {scope, query, valid_at, seeds, max_graph_depth, max_items, max_output_bytes, max_storage_keys}`; bounds: 256 seeds, 512 items, 768 KiB output, 1,000,000 keys, depth 32; the engine captures the read stamp per request (no caller-supplied known cursor) | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/memory_context.rs:6-30` |
| `ContextPacket {scope, valid_at, query_sha256, read: ContextReadStamp, plan (five stages: Seed, Lexical, Semantic, Graph, Fusion), selected_versions, read_evidence, items, output_bytes, truncated, packet_sha256}`; each item: `identity, score, values, evidence[]` with per-avenue `kind, source, source_rank, source_score, contribution, plan_sha256, evidence_sha256` | same file, lines 69-117, 252-313 |
| Flights: `LaunchPromptFlight {scope, prompt, provider (Observe only), context_mode (Fresh|Pruned), context, acceptance_marker}`; record stores `read: ContextReadStamp`, `context: {request_sha256, plan_sha256, packet_sha256, items, output_bytes, truncated, selected_versions}`, append-only events `{stage: Prompt|Context|Outcome, kind, label, detail, data}`; a pruned flight writes one `rrflow-prompt-flight-used` edge per record (rank, fused score, avenues) | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/flight.rs:48-329`; `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` (PR #18) |
| rrflowQL: `FROM <family>:<kind> AT VALID <n|$p> KNOWN <n|HEAD|$p> [WHERE …] [PROJECT …] [LIMIT n] [EXPLAIN CONTRACT|ANALYZE]`; `FROM traverse:<relation> START <kind>:<id> DIRECTION … DEPTH n`; live queries require `KNOWN HEAD`; traversal is a linear scan until E-01 | `crates/compute/rrd-query/src/syntax.rs:112-150, 700-760, 879-896`; `live.rs:60` |
| Changefeed: `changefeed-read {scope, after_cursor, limit ≤ 4096}` → page with `cursor, commit_sha256, commit_ordinal, at_unix_ms, actor, mutation (Claim | Data), change_sha256`; `changefeed-follow` long-polls ≤ 5,000 ms; `subscription-open` pushes `Changefeed` or `LiveQuery` streams over the multiplexed WebSocket | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/lib.rs:2527-2750` |
| `diagnostics-read` → `DiagnosticSnapshot {product_capabilities, graph, graph_difference, retention, vector catalogues, storage, changes, audit, sections}`; `storage.rrflow_kv` = memtable, write_ahead_log, maintenance, segment_set, page_cache, segment_io; counters are process observations, not bound to the read stamp, reset on reopen | `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/diagnostic.rs:412-503` |
| `diagnostics-read` answers 409 `StorageConflict` (retryable) under concurrent audited traffic — POAM-029, open | `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` (step 0) |
| Vector search replays the change log per search — POAM-028, open; the demo estate's similarity map took 46.9 s for 270 searches | `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` |
| No embedding backend is installed (semantic stage always skipped); no ingestion (D-02..D-05); provider arms planned (Decision 15); RROFLOW and SWAG have no record | `claude/rrflow-capability-study.md`; `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` |
| Demo estate today: RRFlow's own docs loaded by a dev harness — 270 documents, 986 `links_to` relations, 270 lexical 256-d vectors | `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` (Development environment) |
| Connectome's contract-pin discipline: `Cargo.lock` pins one RRFlow revision; `vite.config.ts` reads it; the dependency-authority gate fails if the npm and Cargo pins differ; the TypeScript SDK is a pnpm git dependency `github:rrflow/rrflow-development#<rev>&path:sdks/typescript` | `claude/rrflow-build-order.md` (Connectome PRs #2, #4) |
| Config format decided for the platform: TOML validated by JSON Schema generated from Rust types with `schemars` | `claude/skills-and-routines-inventory.md` |

## Architecture

```
browser ──HTTPS──▶ edge (TLS, cache, rate limit)
                     ├─ static site (Astro build: HTML, CSS, islands)
                     └─ /api/*  ──▶ site gateway (Rust, axum, rrd-client pinned to one revision)
                                        │  loopback HTTP, read-only principal `site-reader`
                                        ▼
                                  rrflow serve (single_node_server · rrflow_kv · loopback_http_websocket)
                                        │
                                  demo estate (instance = rrflow.ai demo project)
```

Why this shape and not another:
- The engine stays on its loopback presentation, which is the shipped, qualified one; no `network_http_websocket` configuration, no mutual-TLS client in a browser, no public RRFlow port. The gateway is the only RRFlow client and holds the only credential.
- The gateway is where abuse is absorbed: an allowlist of operations, per-IP and global rate limits, single-flight caches, a small engine concurrency pool (POAM-029 makes concurrent audited reads conflict — the pool turns that into queueing, not 409s on screen).
- The site is static-first. Scenes render with real numbers from the gateway's cached JSON; the GPU field is an island that loads after first paint and degrades to an SVG frame under `prefers-reduced-motion` or without WebGL2.

### Names (Decision 1, decided)
- Repository: `github.com/rrflow/site-development`. Local checkout: `D:\localdev\site-development` on Gus.
- Folders: `site/` (Astro app), `gateway/` (Rust crate `site-gateway`, binary `rrflow-site-gateway`), `estate/` (install plan, principal declarations, canonical prompts, rebuild script), `config/` (TOML + generated JSON Schema), `scripts/` (pin check, estate rebuild).
- Everything a human may want to change is configuration, not code: engine base URL and scope, credential reference (secret name, never a value), cache TTLs, rate limits, budgets for `context-assemble`, the canned rrflowQL set, the canonical prompt set, scene order and copy keys. Defaults ship as TOML; the gateway's Rust types are the schema source (`schemars`), and the site's TypeScript types for `/api/*` are generated from that schema.

### Stack (Decision 2, decided)
**Rust gateway (axum + `rrd-client`) and an Astro static site with islands** — three.js WebGPURenderer/TSL with WebGL2 fallback, or cosmos.gl, for the field; GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis for the scroll flight. Reasons: the credential and the engine calls live in Rust beside the engine, the browser needs no RRFlow SDK, the API surface is small and typed from one Rust source, and it matches the platform's Rust-first rule. The field library (three.js vs cosmos.gl) is chosen at step 4 by a spike on the real graph snapshot, not now.

### Hosting the demo estate (Decision 3, decided)
A small VPS runs `rrflow serve` (loopback) and the gateway; static assets ship to an edge/CDN; only the gateway port is reachable from the edge; the `site-reader` credential comes from Infisical as a reference; backups run on the D-11 lane (functional for installed estates). The estate is disposable and rebuilt from the docs, so the VPS carries no irreplaceable state.

## Data flow per scene (what each panel reads)

| Scene | Panel | Gateway route | Engine operation(s) | Cache / limits | Labeled planned until |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| global | live / planned badges | `GET /api/capabilities` | `capabilities-read` → `ProductCapabilityCatalogue` dispositions | 1 h | LFG, SWAG, RROFLOW rows: the catalogue has none, so a `config/capabilities-overlay.toml` supplies them with `disposition = "planned"` and a reason; upstream ask: add the rows to the engine's catalogue |
| hero | estate field | `GET /api/estate/graph` | `diagnostics-read` (`graph` section) + `vector-point-scroll`; clusters computed in the gateway (Louvain, as Connectome does today) | 10 min; precomputed at estate rebuild | million-record scale (ingestion, E-01) |
| hero | flight trail + packet seal | `GET /api/flights/{id}` | `flight-read` (record, `rrflow-prompt-flight-used` edges, events) | immutable → cache by id | — |
| 01 engine | stage rail, Flight Ledger | `GET /api/flights`, `GET /api/flights/{id}` | `flight-list`, `flight-read` | list 60 s; detail immutable | answer column (no provider arms); semantic avenue "skipped: no embedding model bound" |
| 01 engine | "type a prompt" | `POST /api/context` | `context-assemble` (`MemoryContextRead`), no persistence | per-IP 6/min, global pool 2, budgets from config (defaults: items ≤ 24, depth ≤ 2, storage keys ≤ 100,000, output ≤ 128 KiB); result cached by `(query_sha256, read.runtime_cursor)` 60 s | semantic stage |
| 02 rrflowQL | query + scrubber | `POST /api/query/{name}` | `query-execute` with canned, parameterized statements only (`$valid_at`, `$known`); `EXPLAIN CONTRACT` for the plan panel | 30 s; free-form statements refused | — |
| 03 rrflowDB | commit anatomy | static (from the contract) | — | — | — |
| 03 rrflowDB | neighbourhood | `GET /api/graph/neighbourhood?start=&depth=` | `query-execute` `FROM traverse:links_to START … DEPTH n`; depth ≤ 2 | 60 s | fast traversal (E-01) |
| 04 rrflowKV | counters, pipeline | `GET /api/storage` | `diagnostics-read` (`storage.rrflow_kv`) | 5 s single-flight; on 409 serve the last good value with `stale: true` and age | — |
| pulse | commit ticker | `GET /api/pulse` (SSE) | one `changefeed-follow` loop in the gateway, fanned out to browsers | one follower per gateway; browsers ≤ 1 event/s | — |
| 05 RROFLOW | loop, tiers, promotion | static (contract enums) | — | — | the whole scene: IN DESIGN |
| get it | DevPulse / shippin.cloud / Connectome | static; waitlist `POST /api/waitlist` | — | per-IP 3/h; store in the gateway's own store, not the estate | shippin.cloud: COMING |

Every live panel carries a source chip (operation + read stamp or observed_at) rendered by one component; a panel without a source renders the planned state from the catalogue or overlay. This is the one rule that keeps the site honest as the engine grows.

What a visitor can and cannot do: read everything above; assemble context for a prompt they type (a read, not a flight); never write — flights, tasks, claims and vectors on the demo estate are owner-launched during estate rebuild.

## The demo estate
- Content: RRFlow's own documentation tree, as today (270 documents, 986 `links_to`, lexical vectors) loaded by the harness, until D-02..D-05 ingestion replaces the harness. Rebuild is a script in `estate/`, idempotent, run on each engine pin bump.
- Flights: a canonical prompt set in `estate/prompts.toml` (12 prompts about RRFlow, each answerable from the docs) launched with the `Observe` provider in `Pruned` mode after each rebuild, so the ledger always has real flights with real edges. When provider arms land (Decision 15), the same set is re-flown with a provider and the answer column goes live.
- Principals in the install plan: `operator` (existing), `site-reader` (service principal; grants: `ServiceInspect`, `SessionCreate`, `SessionRenew`, `SessionClose`, `EstateRead`, `DiagnosticsRead`, `FlightRead`, `MemoryContextRead`, `QueryExecute`, `ChangefeedRead`, `ChangefeedFollow`, `VectorCollectionList`, `VectorPointRetrieve`, `VectorPointScroll`, `VectorSearch`; no transaction, flight-launch, backup or admin actions), `estate-builder` (used only by the rebuild script; flight-launch and transactions).
- Semantic lane: off until the estate binds an embedding model (Decision 17: embedded `fastembed` or an endpoint); the gateway reads the capability catalogue to flip the label, not a config flag.

## Non-functional requirements
- Performance: static HTML first paint; the GPU island loads after; scroll work budgeted (target < 4 ms/frame on a mid-range phone); adaptive quality by device tier; Lighthouse ≥ 90 on mobile before launch.
- Accessibility: `prefers-reduced-motion` → static scenes; real links and buttons; contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (the concept's palette passes); every SVG labeled.
- Privacy: no third-party trackers; the waitlist stores an email and a timestamp, nothing else.
- Truth: no speed or superiority claim against SurrealDB, Qdrant or HydraDB until J-04 passes (OBJ-10 not established).
- Resilience: the site renders with the gateway down (last-good JSON baked at build time, marked stale); the gateway renders with the engine busy (409 → stale with age).

## Build order (each step one PR in `site-development`, CI green before merge)
0. Bootstrap (next): repository, folders, Astro shell, Biome, Playwright smoke, gateway crate skeleton, the contract pin (one engine revision in `gateway/Cargo.lock`, a check script that fails the build when any other file names a different revision), design tokens exported from the concept canvas.
1. Demo estate on the VPS: `rrflow install plan|apply` with the three principals, `serve` on loopback, rebuild script (docs load + canonical flights), backup schedule on the D-11 lane, Infisical reference for the `site-reader` key.
2. Gateway v1: `/api/capabilities`, `/api/storage`, `/api/flights`, `/api/flights/{id}`, `/api/estate/graph`, `/api/pulse`; caches, single-flight, rate limits, engine pool; `/healthz`; JSON Schema from the Rust types and the generated TypeScript types for the site.
3. Site v1, no GPU yet: all six scenes with live panels and planned badges; hero field drawn as SVG from `/api/estate/graph`; source chips everywhere; deploy to rrflow.ai behind the edge. This is the first public release: honest and complete, not yet spectacular.
4. Hero field island: cosmos.gl or three.js WebGPURenderer with WebGL2 fallback (spike decides); flight trail from `/api/flights/{id}`; reduced-motion and no-WebGL fallbacks keep step 3's SVG.
5. Scroll choreography: GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis; stage lighting on scene 01; mobile frame budget verified on a real phone.
6. "Type a prompt" (`/api/context`) with budgets and rate limits; the packet renders through the same Flight Ledger component.
7. rrflowQL scene: canned parameterized queries, VALID/KNOWN controls, `EXPLAIN CONTRACT` plan panel.
8. Launch polish: OG images, sitemap, Lighthouse and accessibility passes, uptime check on `/healthz`.
Then, as the engine grows (no site rework needed — the catalogue and the gateway absorb the change): embedding bound → semantic lane live; provider arms → answer column live; tasks (PR #19) → task threads in the ledger; ingestion → "point it at your repo" demo; LFG/SWAG/RROFLOW catalogue rows upstream → badges flip from overlay to engine truth.

## Upstream asks (engine repo, not site work)
- Capability rows for LFG, SWAG and RROFLOW in `product_capability_catalogue()` with `Planned` dispositions and reasons, so the site stops carrying an overlay.
- POAM-029 fix (diagnostics under audited traffic) — the gateway's cache and pool are the mitigation, not the fix.
- A caller-supplied known cursor for `context-assemble` (or an engine replay operation at a flight's recorded stamp), the capability the design's "replay seal" wants; today only `valid_at` is caller-supplied.

## Sources
- `rrflow/rrflow-development` at `13ce338`: `crates/transport/rrd-server/src/http/server.rs`, `crates/transport/rrd-contract/src/{lib.rs, memory_context.rs, flight.rs, diagnostic.rs, capability_surface.rs}`, `crates/authority/rrd-engine/src/capabilities.rs`, `crates/compute/rrd-query/src/{syntax.rs, live.rs}`, `docs/reference/deployment/modes.md`, `docs/reference/security/authority.md`
- Project records: `claude/rrflow-build-order.md`, `claude/rrflow-capability-study.md`, `claude/skills-and-routines-inventory.md`, `claude/compute-and-data-workload-classification.md`
- Rendering and platform facts: https://web.dev/blog/webgpu-supported-major-browsers (WebGPU in Chrome 113+/Edge, Firefox 141+, Safari 26; Linux in progress), https://github.com/cosmograph-org/cosmos (MIT, WebGL2 GPU force layout), https://tympanus.net/codrops/2024/10/30/interactive-3d-with-three-js-batchedmesh-and-webgpurenderer/ (three.js WebGPURenderer + TSL, WebGPU-only post-processing caveat)

title: rrflow.ai — generated video for a gripping, layman-friendly experience
description: Engine and Connectome context. RRFlow is a separate product from the RROFLOW monitoring dashboard.
text:
# rrflow.ai — generated video for a gripping, layman-friendly experience

Date: 2026-10-24. Extends `claude/rrflow-public-site-build-order.md` (Decisions 1–3 stand: `rrflow/site-development`, Rust gateway + Astro islands, VPS demo estate). This record: how Higgsfield and Runway video fits the site without breaking its fidelity rule, the metaphor world, the shot list, the consistency recipe, the web delivery techniques, and a pilot. Nothing has been generated; no credits spent.

## The rule that makes video possible here
AI video cannot show real data, and the site may never fake data. So the experience has **two layers that never trade places**:
- **Metaphor layer** — generated video: the world a layman understands (a city, strata, a trail). Labeled "illustration" once per scene. Never renders words, numbers, UI, logos or charts (generators get those wrong anyway).
- **Truth layer** — HTML/WebGL rendered from the gateway: the Flight Ledger, read stamps, digests, counters, badges. Always overlaid on or beside the video, always from `/api/*`.
The video makes people *feel* what the engine does; the overlay *proves* it. Interaction binds the two: the same scroll, hover or scrub drives both.

## Candidate worlds (one decision)
| World | Records / relations | A flight | VALID vs KNOWN | One commit | rrflowKV | RROFLOW | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Night city on strata** (recommended) | lit buildings / streets; clusters = districts | one violet→cyan light trail gathering five lights, then sealing | the same corner at two times: sun (valid) and how much is built (known) | a whole block appears in one breath, or reverts together | geological layers under the streets: snow (WAL), soil (memtable), rock (segments), pressure (compaction), light veins (cache) | footprints → worn path → paved road → highway | matches the dark-instrument look; everyone reads a city |
| The Archive | books/cards in an infinite library-observatory | a probe sweeping the stacks, returning five sealed items | the same shelf photographed twice; date on the back vs date received | shelves rotate together | strata under the floor | a reading path worn into the carpet | warm, literate; slower to read at a glance |
| Instrument (abstract light) | points and filaments | a filament lighting | two dials | a chord struck once | sediment of light | a groove deepening | closest to current visuals; weakest for laymen |

## Tool split (verified 2026-10-24)
**Higgsfield** — account on Ultra, 5,042.81 credits; costs are quoted per job before generation.
- `seedance_2_5` (workhorse): text-to-video, `omni_reference` (image + video + audio references), `video_edit`, `video_extension`; 4–30 s; 1080p; start and end image. Base shots and extensions.
- `kling3_0`: start + end image (seamless loops: start = end), multi-shot, `4k` mode; `sound off` to save credits. Loops and before/after shots.
- `gemini_omni_flash_1_1`: 4K, `edit` mode. Hero master upscale path.
- `hf_mult_motion_control` (Genjutsu): motion from a reference video onto subjects in reference images. A consistent guide character's movement.
- `scene_builder_3d_*`: build one 3D location, generate camera angles — the consistency anchor: every shot starts from a still of the same city.
- Explainer presets (22 style references: Editorial Motion Graphics, Studio 3D, Low Poly, Paper Diorama, Isometric Flat Vector, …) resolve to a style `media_id` reusable across generations.
- `remove_background` (stills), `upscale_video`, `generate_audio`.
**Runway** (changelog, 2026): Aleph 2.0 + Edit Studio (21 May) — edit one frame, the change carries through the rest of the video → the *state-variant* tool (then/now, planned/live, day/night) without regenerating; Runway Characters (9 Mar, API) — real-time conversational avatars; Seedance 2.5 (Aug, up to 30 s, 1080p) — same base generator as Higgsfield, so masters move between the two; Runway Ruby — SDR→HDR grade; Gen-4.5 image-to-video (Jan). Model Routers and Task Cost API on Runway Dev.
Division of labour: **generate in Higgsfield** (credits in hand, 3D scene builder, presets); **vary and finish in Runway** (Aleph variants, HDR grade, a conversational guide later).

## Consistency recipe (the number-one risk of AI video)
1. World bible: palette (obsidian ground `#0B0D12`, violet `#7C5CFF` → cyan `#22D3EE` for trails, amber `#FBBF24` only for "planned"), lens (35 mm, slow pushes, top-down for maps), materials (wet asphalt, glass, basalt strata), time (always night; VALID changes the sky, KNOWN changes what exists).
2. Build the city block and its strata once in `scene_builder_3d`; export angles as stills; every shot is image-to-video from one of those stills.
3. One approved hero still becomes the style reference passed on every Seedance `omni_reference` call.
4. Variants by Aleph edits of a master, never by re-prompting.
5. Loops by start = end frame; extensions by `video_extension`, not new seeds.
6. Three takes per shot, pick one, log the seed/prompt/refs in `estate/../video/shots.toml` in the site repo so a shot can be re-made when the pin bumps.

## Shot list — night city on strata (v1)
| # | Scene | Shot (6–12 s unless noted) | Generation route | Interaction on the site |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H | Hero | Aerial slow push over the city at night; visible strata beneath; one trail runs five blocks and freezes into a sealed line; loop | 3D still → Seedance omni-ref → Kling start=end loop; 4K via Gemini Omni | Video texture under the live field; the *real* flight trail from `/api/flights/{id}` drawn over it in alpha |
| 1.0 | Engine | One continuous 20–25 s flight in five beats: lantern lit at an address (seed) → street signs flare (lexical) → windows glow by colour (semantic) → light spreads along streets (graph) → five brightest converge and seal (fusion) | Seedance 30 s t2v + `video_extension`; beats timed to a shot sheet | Scroll-scrubbed (WebCodecs); the Flight Ledger counts rungs in as each beat passes; semantic beat dims with "when an embedding model is bound" |
| 2.0 | rrflowQL | The same corner, two times: sky moves (VALID), buildings appear (KNOWN) | Master + two Aleph variants (dusk/night; block absent/present) | Bi-temporal scrubber crossfades variants; live claim bars beside |
| 3.0 | rrflowDB | A block appears in one breath: building, streets, lights, sign together; reverse = abort | Kling start/end images before/after | Hover "abort" plays backwards; commit anatomy list pins to each element |
| 4.0 | rrflowKV | Camera descends below the street through snow → soil → rock layers compacting; veins of light where reads run; 12 s | Seedance t2v with style refs; vertical move | Scroll-scrubbed descent; live `diagnostics-read` counters pin to each layer |
| 5.0 | RROFLOW | Footprints across grass → worn path → paved road → highway the trail flies straight down | Seedance 15 s or four Aleph states of one field | Hover each stage plays its segment; whole scene badged IN DESIGN |
| 6.0 | Get it | The same city twice: on a desk under a lamp (DevPulse) and under a cloud (shippin.cloud); a thin light between (sync, planned) | Two stills → Kling start/end | Static with a slow loop; badges from the capability overlay |
| G | Guide (optional) | A lamplighter who walks the trail; later a conversational guide | Genjutsu motion transfer (consistent movement); later Runway Characters grounded by `/api/context` so answers come only from the estate, with the ledger as receipts | Hover/click; later ask-the-estate |

## Web delivery (sourced)
- **Scroll-scrubbed video**: demux in-browser, decode with WebCodecs `VideoDecoder`, keep a ±1 s frame window, draw to canvas; backward seeks restart from the previous keyframe, so encode with dense keyframes (every 12–24 frames); close every `VideoFrame`. Chromium complete; Safari unconfirmed → fallback to a poster or `currentTime` stepping. [Lion Keng, WebCodecs scroll sync](https://lionkeng.medium.com/a-tutorial-webcodecs-video-scroll-synchronization-8b251e1a1708)
- **Transparent overlays**: stacked luma/alpha video (colour on top, alpha below) drawn through a WebGL shader; AV1 ≈ 460 kB vs native VP9 alpha ≈ 1.1 MB vs native HEVC alpha ≈ 3.4 MB for the same clip; HEVC for older Apple hardware; avoid animated AVIF. [Jake Archibald, video with transparency](https://jakearchibald.com/2024/video-with-transparency/)
- **Textures**: looping video as a three.js/cosmos.gl texture for the field's ground; cheap on the GPU, loads after first paint.
- **Loops**: start = end frame at generation; no crossfade hacks.
- **Motion safety**: `prefers-reduced-motion` → poster frames; autoplay muted; sound only on an explicit control.
- **Budget**: video island loads after first paint; per-scene clips ≤ 2–3 MB; hero 4K only for desktop, 1080p for mobile; scroll work under ~4 ms/frame.

## Where it lands in the build order
Steps 0–3 unchanged (bootstrap, estate, gateway, site v1 with SVG/HTML scenes). Video enters at step 4 as part of the hero island and step 5 (scroll choreography); each scene's clip replaces nothing in the truth layer, it sits under it. Shots, prompts, references and encodes live in the site repo under `site/public/media/` (encodes) and `media-src/shots.toml` (recipes), never in the estate.

## Pilot (before the full list)
Three shots prove the world or kill it in one sitting: **H (hero loop)**, **4.0 (strata descent)**, **5.0 (desire paths)**. Each: one 3D-scene still, three Seedance takes, one Kling loop; Aleph variant on one of them to test the state-switch. Pass: all three read as one place, no text artefacts, loop seamless, the trail colour matches the UI. Fail: switch world or register before spending further. Credits are quoted per job at generation; nothing is generated without an explicit go.

## Sources
- Higgsfield MCP: `balance` (Ultra, 5,042.81 credits), `models_explore` (Seedance 2.5, Kling 3.0, Gemini Omni Flash 1.1, Genjutsu), `get_explainer_presets` (22 presets), workflow list.
- [Runway changelog](https://runway.com/changelog) — Aleph 2.0 & Edit Studio (2026-05-21), Runway Characters (2026-03-09, API), Seedance 2.5 (2026-08-11), Ruby (2026-08-20), Gen-4.5 image-to-video (2026-01-21).
- [WebCodecs scroll sync](https://lionkeng.medium.com/a-tutorial-webcodecs-video-scroll-synchronization-8b251e1a1708) · [Video with transparency](https://jakearchibald.com/2024/video-with-transparency/)

title: Signal inbox and review journal
description: Product scope, integration design and setup instructions. Check the documented implementation status.
text:
# Signal inbox and review journal

Status: implemented in the SDK capture work branch; local verification, not a Texas deployment.

The dashboard reads actual turn records and shows a signal inbox, evidence tool
references, rule revisions and capture identity. A rule match is a finding to
review, not a proven failure. Selecting a signal count filters the recent turns.
Historical activity does not establish that a collector is connected now.

`GET /v1/turns` includes a `revisions` map from event ID to the SHA-256 of the
server's serialized turn record. `POST /v1/reviews` accepts:

```json
{
  "review_id": "a9c3d761-299f-4677-b9fd-8b197823f660",
  "event_id": "the captured turn ID",
  "turn_digest": "the revision returned with that turn",
  "signal": "blocked_handoff",
  "rule_version": 1,
  "verdict": "not_match"
}
```

The authenticated devspace is authoritative. The server verifies the turn and
signal revision, then retains the exact snapshot with the verdict, receipt time
and reviewer identity. A devspace key is attributed as `devspace-key`, not falsely
as a named human. An identical request ID is replayable; a changed request under
the same ID conflicts. New reviews of stale evidence are rejected. A later
correction creates another review; it never overwrites the prior verdict.
The UI displays the latest verdict for the exact revision among the newest
1,000 reviews. The local store is single-process; hosted persistence is Postgres.

Reviews do not authorize dataset creation, training, rule activation or promotion.
Those remain governed by the existing learning plan and mechanism spec. Outcome
labels, review sampling and reviewer roles remain future increments.

## Delivery gaps that this increment does not close

- `setup` must discover and link existing agents, install capture safely and show
  real source health. SDK wrappers are a separate developer integration path.
- Native transcript ingest still requires network settings before sending.
  Its automatic durable offline replay is not implemented by the SDK outbox.
- Source identity, dispatch correlation, queue age/bytes, backpressure and
  automatic reconnect must be observable at both the collector and cloud.
- Shippin owns account and subscription truth. Free/paid allowances, retention
  and rate limits need a versioned entitlement seam and enforcement; no pricing
  or allowances have been invented here.
- Raw transcript token normalization needs validation. The dashboard withholds
  spend totals and labels raw usage unverified.
- Texas management identity, deployment, DNS/TLS and real account onboarding
  remain required hosted acceptance checks.

See `plan/sdk-install-and-linking.md`, `plan/rroflow-ai-plan.md` and
`spec/mechanism-spec-v0.md` for the product flow and governed learning roadmap.

title: Automatic datasets v0
description: Dataset and learning requirements. Implementation status is described in the note.
text:
# Automatic datasets v0

Status: proposed implementation contract, 2026-10-26.
Owner: RROFLOW dataset product; engine promotion continues to follow RRFlow's
learning contract. Extends R8 and R3-consent in
[mechanism-spec-v0.md](mechanism-spec-v0.md).

## Product behavior

A user enables a dataset policy once for a devspace and selected sources.
Subsequent capture can schedule dataset builds automatically within that grant.
Dataset creation does not silently authorize training or activation. A separate
bounded training policy may authorize recurring experiments. Successful experiments
produce candidates; promotion follows held-out evaluation and reversible admission.

Objects carry stable identity and immutable revision: source event, evidence,
human correction, label, dataset manifest, experiment and candidate. Repeated
capture must not mutate the meaning of an already published dataset revision.

## Build input and output

A build accepts an authenticated devspace, policy revision, consent revision,
source cutoff/read stamp, projection/redaction version and split policy.
Its idempotency key derives from those inputs. Client-supplied devspace claims
cannot override the authenticated owner. No cross-tenant pooling by default.

Every output manifest contains:

- schema and dataset ID/revision; owner and allowed sharing scope;
- exact source event IDs plus immutable source digests/revisions;
- content eligibility, purpose-specific consent and redaction/projection version;
- immutable labels with author/evaluator provenance; corrections reference both
  the prior and corrected artifact;
- included/excluded counts and machine-readable exclusion reasons;
- immutable train/validation/test assignments and their digests;
- row format, artifact digests, creation time and retention/deletion policy;
- builder version, code revision and input cutoff so the snapshot is reproducible.

Existing turns are upserted. A source reference alone is therefore insufficient:
the builder must materialize an immutable redacted snapshot or retain the exact
source revision before publishing a manifest.

## Job behavior

`queued -> running -> validating -> published`, with explicit failed/cancelled
states. A durable lease and idempotency key prevent duplicated jobs after restart.
Write artifacts into a private staging area; publish the manifest only after every
artifact checksum, scope, count and consent check passes. Recheck consent before
publication. A failure leaves no partly published dataset.

Keep builds off the HTTP request path. Apply per-devspace CPU/memory/storage,
concurrency and retry budgets. Persist progress and exclusion counts; record
failures without raw prompt content or credentials. Queue selection, scheduler
and artifact storage remain implementation decisions with owned interfaces.

## Dataset families

- **Supervised:** explicit MATCH/NOT MATCH and outcome labels; edited artifacts
  preserve the actual correction. Ambiguous/unlabelled rows stay out of the
  labelled training set.
- **Unsupervised:** eligible unlabelled examples for clustering and novelty
  detection. Cluster IDs are candidate groupings, never correctness labels.
- **Evaluation:** frozen, separate held-out revisions. Group related sessions,
  forks, near-duplicates and project artifacts before splitting to prevent leakage.
  Once consumed for selection, rotate the holdout according to policy.
- **Preference/correction:** pairs require a supported provenance relationship
  and human or declared evaluator preference; an aborted turn is not automatically
  a rejected example.

Provider-neutral canonical rows can have explicit exporters for a training target.
A consumer subscription does not itself establish a model fine-tuning interface.
Training a RROFLOW classifier, evaluating a prompt/rule, and fine-tuning an external
model are separate job types with distinct capability and budget checks.

## Revocation and deletion

Stopping capture, withdrawing dataset use and deleting records are separate
commands. Revocation blocks new builds and affected pending training. Deletion
invalidates affected manifests and propagates to retained artifacts/exports under
the accepted retention policy. Record downstream model provenance; do not promise
that deleting a row reverses an already trained model. Requalification, retirement
or retraining is an explicit downstream action.

## Acceptance evidence before activation

1. Two devspaces cannot read, build or export each other's records.
2. Replay/crash/retry yields one published revision with identical contents.
3. Missing consent, withdrawn consent, unredacted content and malformed sources
   are excluded or rejected with observable reasons.
4. Related sessions/forks and duplicate artifacts never cross train/test splits.
5. Unlabelled and cluster-generated rows cannot become supervised truth.
6. Row counts, labels, source revisions and artifact digests reproduce exactly.
7. Delete/revoke blocks future use and invalidates affected revisions.
8. A bounded training run references the manifest, code, parameters, budget and
   evaluation method; failed or inconclusive results cannot promote.
9. A passing candidate can be shadowed, admitted and reverted with journaled
   evidence. The existing ingest alone satisfies none of these acceptance gates.

No dataset worker or training engine is claimed built by this document.
