text:
# RROFLOW mechanism spec v0

**Status:** design-time proposal, 2026-10-24. Not canon. Each numbered record below is a candidate ADR; it becomes canon only when reviewed, edited and saved through the ADR component and then landed in `rrflow/rrflow-development` as a pull request with its journal.
**Owner it fills in under:** the learning contract `docs/reference/inference/learning/controller-training.md` (loop: Outcomes → Candidate → Eval → Shadow → Proposal → `RrdEngine` admission → Active), the LFG/SWAG contract, the rrflowDB capability record (prompt graph families, experiments), Gate I's two RROFLOW packages. This document restates none of them; it fills the mechanism level beneath them with what Raindrop and REA show works.
**Basis:** `rrflow-development` `main` `94d0567` (PR #116, 2026-10-24); `sources/raindrop/raindrop-source-ledger.md` (228 sourced claims); `sources/rea/rea-source-ledger.md`; `sources/prototype/prototype-raindrop-ledger.md`; `canon/alignment-notes.md`. Every Raindrop or REA fact below is in those ledgers with a source; nothing is quoted from a logged-in workspace yet (live capture pending).
**Reading rule:** the latest explicit statement by Jesse wins over anything here.

---

## 0. Boundary and glossary

**Who does what.** RROFLOW **mints** (proposes definitions, candidates, findings). LFG **executes** the cheap tier (per-node classifiers on CPU, Decision 3). SWAG **decides and dispatches** model calls when a judge is needed. Governance **gates** every verdict and promotion. `RrdEngine` **admits and commits**; nothing else writes. Raindrop's own split is the same shape: a classifier is built once by a model-backed agent and then executed deterministically millions of times; ambiguous cases alone reach a model.

**D0 — the term.** `signal` is taken: in RRFlow it is the H-05 telemetry catalogue (`docs/reference/protocol/signal-catalogue.md`). This spec uses **behaviour signal** for Raindrop's "signal": a versioned classifier definition that labels flights with a named behaviour. Candidates if Jesse prefers another: *lens*, *behaviour rule*, *verdict rule*. Decision pending; all other records use the placeholder.

**Term map (Raindrop → RRFlow).** Keep the right column in all records.

| Raindrop | RRFlow | Note |
|---|---|---|
| project | estate (rrflowDB) | both isolate models and data per unit; Raindrop: "a model trained in one project does not leak into another" |
| org | account | account owns many estates (Decision 1) |
| user (`user_id`, traits, plan) | seat | Raindrop silently never ships an event without `user_id`; a flight must carry its seat |
| event (one turn: input, tool calls, output) | prompt flight | Raindrop's pricing unit is also one turn incl. tool calls and sub-agents |
| conversation (`convo_id`) | session (and task, when the prompts serve one named goal) | tasks group flights by goal; a `convo_id` groups by thread — both are needed, they are not the same relation |
| trace / span (`LLM_GENERATION`, `TOOL_CALL`, `INTERNAL`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT`) | flight stage events (vocabulary to extend, R1) | one temporal graph; never a second event store |
| property, feature flag | flight properties; experiment assignment/exposure events (H-09) | |
| signal (type `code`/`topic`/`regex`/`instrumented`/`metric`) | behaviour signal (R3); explicit verdict (R6); lexicon label; H-05 metric | one Raindrop noun splits into four RRFlow kinds |
| preset signal | bundled behaviour signal revision | shipped as the initial configuration revision, overridable |
| tool-error signal | derived behaviour signal over `TOOL_CALL` error events; deterministic, no model | |
| label signal (`sentiment: OTHER`, e.g. `intent_reorder`) | classification-family Answer (LFG) | describes, does not grade |
| stumble | one-flight finding (R5) | |
| issue | distribution-shift finding (R5) | |
| topic | lexicon-family label | |
| dataset (labelled snapshot) | labelled evidence set (R8) | snapshot at add time ≈ read stamp |
| experiment (cohorts of logged events) | cohort experiment (R7); the H-09 experiment covers arm assignment | |
| replay / simulation | governed replay (fresh work, R7) | the contract already separates inspection replay from re-invocation |
| Workshop (local trace viewer + MCP) | Connectome flight lens + `rrflow-mcp` | |
| write key / query key / MCP OAuth | endpoint binding credential reference; RRD session grants | secrets are Infisical names, never values |

---

## 1. Evidence substrate — what a flight records versus what a classifier needs

**Raindrop's unit of evidence.** One event = `event_id`, `user_id`, `event` name, `timestamp`, `ai_data{input, output, model, convo_id, tool_calls[]}`, `properties` (incl. SDK `$context` and `raindrop.app.commit_sha`), `attachments[]`, `is_pending`; plus OTLP spans linked by `traceloop.association.properties.event_id`. Server-side, an event row carries `tool_calls`, `tool_names`, `error_spans`, `token_usage`, `topics[]`, `signals[{id,name,score}]`, `user_traits`, `feature_flags`, `is_internal`, `is_excluded_user`. Spans carry `span_type`, `status`, `input_payload`, `output_payload`, tokens, `provider`, `model`, `raindrop.pricing.cost_usd`.

**What RRFlow records today.** A flight = lifecycle record + append-only stage events at one read stamp + `rrflow-prompt-flight-used` edges (rank, fused score, avenues) + `rrflow-task-includes` edge + context-packet digests. Provider arms (the real model generation) are deferred as governed opt-in adapters (PR #17). There is no model-generation event, no tool-call event, no system-prompt snapshot, no token or cost on a flight.

**Consequence.** Nothing in RRFlow is classifiable yet. Every behaviour signal in this spec needs flights that carry what the model saw, did and said. That is step 4 of the build order (answers through bound endpoints) plus provider arms, not a RROFLOW task.

**R1 — flight stage-event vocabulary.** Extend flight events (through the I-01 engine-event envelope when it lands; as flight events until then) with: `generation` (model identity, request/response payload references in the object tier, tokens in/out or explicit unknown, elapsed, status), `tool-call` (name, arguments and result references, status OK/ERROR, elapsed), `system-prompt` (digest + object reference, one per flight), `cost` (provider-reported or catalog-priced, with a coverage flag). Payloads above a configurable size live in the content-addressed object tier and the event holds the digest. The SWAG `Result` row in the LFG/SWAG contract already lists model/runtime identity, usage references, elapsed and outcome; R1 is that row persisted as flight events.
Facts that set the bar: Raindrop caps an event at 1 MiB and text fields at 1,000,000 characters with an explicit truncation marker; drops a finalized event with empty input and output (phantom guard); enriches asynchronously (topics, signals, error spans may lag); drops spans lacking a GenAI/AI-operation attribute. RRFlow's equivalents are configuration, not constants: payload cap, truncation marker, "what makes a flight classifiable" declared in the family definition.

**R2 — one store.** Raindrop's `traces` table is what RRFlow's events key family plus flight edges already are. No trace store, no span table, no SQLite sidecar. Connectome reads flights through `flight-read`; cost is the flight's own size (PR #18).

**Retention.** In the only controlled study of REA (community, rea-lab), agents proactively kept Evidence in 0 of 339 runs, so retention has to be designed in. Raindrop's Hobby tier keeps 14 days, and eval-run traces carry an expiry. The rrflowDB record lists "default retention per family" as an open decision; R1 adds the generation/tool payload families to that decision with a stated default and a per-estate override.

---

## 2. Behaviour signal minting — the supervised loop

**What Raindrop does (public).** Describe the behaviour → an agent studies traces and writes numbered policy rules → compiles a classifier → scans a sample → a review panel shows matches one at a time with a reason; the person labels Match / Not Match on a *sample, not a checklist* → "Run Again" folds labels into the rules → optional "Preview classifier code" → create → runs on every new event and backfills 90 days, sampled. Over MCP: `create_signal(intent, ≤25 positive/negative ids)` and `refine_signal(signal_id, ≤500 ids, comment)`, headless. Signals 2.0 (rd-signal-2): the compiled classifier is `run(event)` code that gathers evidence deterministically (e.g. find tool calls by name, test for three identical-input failures), early-returns non-matches without any model call, and hands only ambiguous candidates with compact context to a task-specific classification head plus an in-house reasoning model. Runs in an isolated per-customer sandbox with no credentials or egress; trace context fetched once and cached near workers; median 100 ms per trace; over 20 billion traces a month. Daily audit of a random sample against a frontier model; regressions retune. Customers can read and edit the code and prompt. Match-rate sensitivity: four one-sentence phrasings of one behaviour over 2,000 traces matched 0.9–4.6 %, and 67 % of traces matched by one phrasing were rejected by another. Reported benchmark: precision 71 % / recall 87 % at 1× relative cost versus 78 % / 91 % at 260× for the best frontier judge.

**R3 — behaviour signal definition.** A schema-registry definition (same mechanism as a prompt graph family) with: name; description; scope (`turn` | `conversation` | `task`); polarity (`negative` | `positive` | `label`); the numbered policy rules as text; the **evidence program**; the **judge binding**; seed and verdict references; revision and digest; provenance (who minted, from which finding or request). Activation is per estate in the configuration revision, like families. Bundled presets (User Frustration, Task Failure, Forgetting, Refusals, User Praise are Raindrop's) ship as the initial revision.

**R3a — the evidence program is rrflowQL, not JavaScript.** Raindrop generates JS over an `event` object. RRFlow's flight is already a graph; the deterministic gathering step is an rrflowQL read at the flight's read stamp over the evidence, classification and R1 stage-event families, with a predicate. Empty result = deterministic non-match, no judge call. The sandbox is the engine's existing `QueryBudget`, read-only authorization and no egress; the cache Raindrop builds near its workers is the flight's own neighbourhood, already materialized by `flight-read`. This is the RRFlow-native form of "compile once, run cheaply" and it is replayable at any historical stamp — Raindrop's `run(event)` is not.

**R3b — the judge is an LFG tier-2 classifier, escalating through SWAG.** `classify()` maps to Decision 3: a per-node classifier on CPU (class 2 binding) bound to the behaviour signal's revision, escalating to a class-1 endpoint only when confidence is below the configured floor. Its output is an Answer (value, probability, confidence, tier, provenance) — the type v3 §3 names and the repo lacks. Raindrop's per-match numeric `score` is probably this probability (inferred; range and threshold unpublished; observed null on instrumented signals). Confidence is reported only with a declared calibration (LFG/SWAG contract), and escalation goes to the tier-3 binding SWAG selects, not a fixed endpoint.

**R3c — verdicts are Governance-family records.** `{flight, behaviour signal revision, label: match | no_match | skip, labeler seat, read stamp}`. Labels are given by a person or an explicitly bound evaluator, never inferred from aggregates (Raindrop's skill rule; RRFlow's contract). Bounds default to Raindrop's (25 seeds at creation, 500 at refinement) and are configuration.

**R3-consent — minting reads only a labelled evidence set.** Collecting flights does not authorize training on them (learning contract). R3d's scan, R3c's verdicts, the R3b judge's training and R3e's audit samples all read an R8 labelled evidence set that carries consent identity, sharing scope and a split manifest. A flight outside every consented set is never sent to a judge endpoint or used as a training row. An audit sample sent to a remote frontier endpoint also needs that set's sharing scope to allow the endpoint's locality.

**R3d — minting is an I-03 routine.** Steps: draft definition (judge-model-backed through SWAG, budgeted) → scan a bounded sample of flights at one read stamp → review (verdict records) → refine (re-draft folding verdicts in) → create as a definition revision → backfill as a separate bounded, sampled job. Every step is an engine operation with a receipt; the routine can be killed and resumed (Gate I corpus). Raindrop's phases `preparing → scanning → reviewing → installing` are the routine's checkpoints.

**R3e — drift audit is a scheduled routine.** Sample recent matches and non-matches, judge them with an eval arm bound to a frontier endpoint, write regression findings (R5 shape), propose a retune revision. Never auto-promotes (Gate I exit condition).

Depends on: Answer type; H-09 schema-registry definitions; I-01 envelope; I-03 routines; endpoint-binding runtime resolution (step 2 config revisions); R1.

---

## 3. Discovery — the unsupervised loop (stumbles and issues)

**What Raindrop does (public).** Three disjoint layers since Issue Detection v2: a **stumble** is one flagged run (what happened, why, key moments; tags such as Logic Error, Hallucination; a Similar panel groups alike stumbles), detected on a per-org scan cadence, not in real time. An **issue** is the same failure recurring across runs and users: severity critical…low, status unresolved/resolved/ignored, affected event and user counts, "affected dimensions" = tools, models and signals overrepresented in matched events, a timeline, a report, matching events. Actions: resolve, ignore with a reason (not accurate, too broad, too specific, show less like this), reopen, duplicate-merge; any issue can be turned into a signal. Built on the same classifier architecture.

**R5 — findings are Governance-family records.** Two kinds, disjoint by construction: `one-flight finding` {flight, tags, why, key-moment event refs, detector revision, status} and `distribution-shift finding` {member findings, overrepresented dimensions computed by rrflowQL facets (tool names, model identity, behaviour signals, properties), severity, status, trend window, report}. Status starts as `proposed`; a seat resolves, ignores (with reason), merges or promotes. The contract's rule holds: a cluster is a hypothesis, never a verdict.

**R5a — the detector is a scheduled I-03 routine** with a configurable cadence over flights since the last stamp: tag through a class-2 judge binding; group by exact dimension facets first, then by vector similarity of finding descriptions in the estate's own vector subsystem. Raindrop's `cadence_minutes`/`last_run_at` become the routine's checkpoint and the Connectome lens says "as of <stamp>".

**R5b — issue → behaviour signal.** Promoting a distribution-shift finding hands R3d its member flights as **candidates for review, never as labels**. Only flights a seat has given a `match` verdict become seeds (bounded by the seed limit). Cluster membership is a hypothesis (learning contract; Gate I I-07). A trigger (I-02) may *propose* this when a finding crosses a configured threshold; it cannot run it.

**Topics and intents.** Raindrop attributes `topics[]` per event server-side and uses label signals (`sentiment: OTHER`) for intents; its MCP integration injects a hidden `_intent` parameter the model fills on the first tool call of a prompt. In RRFlow these are lexicon-family labels and classification-family Answers produced by LFG — already placed by the rrflowDB record; no new kind.

---

## 4. Feedback refinement — explicit and implicit

**What Raindrop does (public).** Explicit: `signals/track` with type `feedback` (comment), `edit` (after), `default`, `agent` (self-report), `agent_internal`; sentiment POSITIVE/NEGATIVE/OTHER; optional `attachment_id`. Implicit: tool-error signals derived from `TOOL_CALL` errors; agent self-diagnostics through an SDK-generated tool (`__raindrop_report`) with categories `missing_context`, `repeatedly_broken_tool`, `capability_gap`, `complete_task_failure`; review labels and `refine_signal` negatives; issue triage verdicts; feature flags and properties for cohorts.

**R6 — explicit verdict events.** Feedback, edit and self-report arrive as engine events (I-01 envelope) through Connectome, DevPulse, or a host-event adapter (I-04: Claude/OpenAI adapters, explicitly installed, never hooks). The self-report tool is an engine-provided tool definition the agent may call; its categories are configuration with Raindrop's four as the initial revision. Each verdict is a Governance-family record on the flight.

**R6a — derived behaviour signals need no model.** Tool errors: an rrflowQL predicate over R1 `tool-call` events with `status: ERROR`, shipped as a bundled definition. Repeated identical-input failures (Raindrop's canonical example) is the same shape with a count predicate.

**R6b — refinement re-mints.** Negative and positive verdicts feed R3d as examples; the new definition is a new revision; the old one stays readable. Knowledge corrections take the claim path the kernel already has (`valid_to`, tier, `PromotionState`, supersession by digest) once `AssertClaim` can express them (the H-09 gap).

**Rule carried from the prototype (Jesse's team, 2026-10-12) and the contract:** a verdict is evidence about behaviour, not automatic authorization to change a rule, prompt or weight.

---

## 5. Experiments, replay and labelled sets — the recursive loop

**What Raindrop does (public).** An **experiment** compares a baseline cohort and an experiment cohort of already-logged events (date ranges plus conditions: model, feature flag, property, tool); outcome = all or selected signals, measured as events % or users %; verdict "likely better/worse" requires a 95 % CI excluding zero and a sample check; "Mixed" when outcomes disagree; event stats (median cost per event, tools, duration, errors). Experiments never run the agent. **Change Reports** read the agent harness on merge, scope traffic by `raindrop.app.commit_sha`, and report after ~24 h which changed tools were called, negative signals on them, related stumbles. **Simulations** (early access) replay production traffic against a proposed harness change on every PR. **Workshop** replay: a replay server with `GET /health` and `POST /replay` on a reserved port range, stitched to the original by setting the SDK event id to the replay run id; the eval loop has the coding agent write code-aware evals asserting on tool-call sequence, state and files. **Datasets** are labelled snapshots of events/traces (Good/Bad/Needs review/Interesting or custom labels), exportable as CSV.

**R7 — cohort experiment and verdict rule.** The H-09 experiment covers configuration arms with assignment/exposure/outcome events. Add a cohort experiment over logged flights with no re-run: two cohort definitions (stamp range + predicates over flight properties, model identity, tool names, task), outcome behaviour signals, unit flights % or seats %, and a **verdict record** carrying the method name, interval, sample check and result (`likely better` | `likely worse` | `mixed` | `insufficient`). The statistical method is declared configuration (Raindrop's is unpublished — D7). Promotion of anything on the strength of a verdict goes through the contract's Proposal → admission → receipt path.

**R7a — governed replay.** Re-running a flight's prompt against a candidate configuration is fresh work through SWAG with its own budget and receipt (the contract's rule), linked to the original by the cohort digest flights already share. The replay-server contract Raindrop publishes (`/health`, `/replay`, stitched ids) is the shape of an outward `rrflow-*` adapter for projects whose agent runs outside RRFlow.

**R7b — change attribution.** A flight is to carry the project-tree snapshot digest once D-03 lands (planned; flights have no such field today) and, when known, the commit; a scheduled routine compares behaviour-signal rates before and after a commit and writes a finding. Raindrop's Change Report is this routine's report.

**R8 — labelled evidence set.** A record holding flight/event references pinned to a read stamp plus labels, with the contract's required manifest: source references, estate and sharing scope, consent, retention, immutable split manifest with digests and row/exclusion counts. Export is a public operation (Parquet is already the optional exchange form). "No dataset exists merely because a prompt flight was recorded" stands: a set is created by an explicit operation with consent identity.

---

## 5b. What the live workspace showed (2026-10-24, Query API, read-only)

Source: `sources/raindrop/live/live-capture-ledger.md`.

- **Raindrop already ships the R3 artifact.** `raindrop-ai@1.0.2` defines a portable evaluator: `format raindrop.eval-program`, `runtimeAbi raindrop-eval-v3`, program source plus SHA-256, a pinned trace-projection hash, and `executionMode deterministic | judge`. It runs in QuickJS with 32 MiB memory, a 1 s program timeout, and judge calls through a host callback **the caller binds**. R3 matches that shape: the evidence program is rrflowQL instead of guest JS, the judge is an endpoint binding instead of a callback, and the identity is a digest pinned to a flight-projection version.
- **Classifier code is not readable through the Query API.** Signal detail returns metadata only. Score is null on instrumented signals.
- **Evals are disabled per organization** in Jesse's org (403), so a vibeguard-style eval replay never ran server-side.
- **vibeguard, Jesse's own loop on Raindrop, plateaued at 4/6 held-out for 11 runs.** That adds five requirements:
  - **R5c — effectiveness reopens a category.** A category with an active definition reopens for proposals when held-out stays below its best observed level for a configured number of runs. Coverage is never treated as effectiveness.
  - **R6c — a revert is a verdict on one revision.** It is not a permanent block on the category. Silencing a category is its own explicit, revocable decision record.
  - **R7c — held-out sets are spent.** A held-out split used to accept a revision is retired for acceptance and kept for regression only, and the next acceptance needs a fresh split (the learning contract's rule, enforced in the record).
  - **R7d — the verdict states its interval.** The R7 verdict record refuses "improved / regressed" when the interval cannot separate the arms, and returns `insufficient` with the sample needed.
  - **R7e — self-grade polarity follows meaning.** "Flat" is neutral. A stalled loop is never filed as positive.

## 6. The outward loop — REA's method as RROFLOW pointed at an external artifact

**What REA does (public).** Pin the target (SHA-256, tool versions) and ask one concrete behaviour question → dissect (static dossiers, byte reads, JS module graphs, process/UI/browser captures), every result an immutable content-addressed Evidence record `ev_<sha256>` with `normalized_result`, `analysis_profile`, `limitations`, and `untrusted_content` provenance → keep three layers apart (saved observation, interpretation, assigned names) and label claims proven/inferred/hidden → an explicit revisioned **unknowns ledger** tied to the evidence that raised each question → induce a behaviour-only spec with input/output examples precise enough to be tests → clean-room rebuild with the acceptance contract written first and immutable to the generator; fingerprint scan rejects copied code → verify by replay on the original with a passing and a deliberately failing input, differential cases, deterministic snapshots → bounded repair (two rounds by default) → attribute each stage to the tool that did it.

**R9 — the same machinery, different target.** Source-family records gain an `untrusted_content` provenance flag (the repository rule "process output is untrusted data" made a field). Evidence records are already digest-bound; make the digest the identity for externally gathered evidence. The unknowns ledger is a Governance-family `unknown` record with revision and the evidence reference — the general form of the lexicon's "inconclusive bucket". Spec cards are task records with acceptance checks named as data on terminal reasoning nodes (`verification_requirement`). The repair loop is the routine's maximum-iteration budget. Verification by replay with a failing input is a Governance check pattern worth bundling.

**Honest limit.** The only controlled study in the REA cluster found no accuracy gain and about double the time with REA. The outward loop is a discipline for evidence and verification, not a speed claim.

---

## 7. Build-order placement

Nothing in this spec precedes the decided order: step 2 configuration revisions → 2c speed wins → step 3 ingestion → step 4 answers through bound endpoints (with provider arms) → step 5 the prototype's UI and Raindrop wiring pointed at RRFlow's API. Behaviour signals need flights with real generations; before step 4 there is nothing to classify.

| Order | Record | Owning gate / package | Waits on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | D0 term; Answer type; R1 stage-event vocabulary | G-01b (Answer at the kernel/public boundary), H-06, I-01 | provider arms (step 4) |
| 2 | R3c verdict, R5 finding, R9 unknown record kinds in the Governance family | H-09 schema registry | H-09 definitions |
| 3 | R3 definition + R3a evidence program + R3b judge binding | G (LFG tier 2), I-03 | Answer, endpoint runtime resolution |
| 4 | R3d minting routine; R6 explicit verdict events; R6a derived definitions | I-03, I-04, I-01 | generic I-03 proof |
| 5 | R5a detector routine; R5b issue → behaviour signal | I-03, I-02 | R3d |
| 6 | R7 cohort experiment + verdict rule; R8 labelled evidence set | H-09 experiments, knowledge-connector export | R3 |
| 7 | R3e drift audit; R7a governed replay; R7b change attribution | I-03, G-02, D-03 | R7 |
| 8 | R9 outward loop | Gate I corpus | all of the above |

**Raindrop's place now (D5).** A class-7 endpoint binding of kind `api`: an outward `rrflow-raindrop` adapter exports flights as `events/track_partial` plus OTLP spans and reads Raindrop's behaviour labels and findings back through its Query API or MCP, so a production classifier labels RRFlow flights before RROFLOW's own exist and the two can be compared on the same flights later. That is build-order step 5 made concrete, and it is the honest basis for any later comparison. Reference-only is the fallback if the binding is not wanted.

---

## 8. What Raindrop and REA supply that canon lacks (absorbed, with the record it lands in)

1. Compile once, execute cheaply: deterministic evidence gathering with early return; a model only on ambiguous candidates (R3a/R3b).
2. Label a sample, not a checklist; bounds 25 at creation, 500 at refinement (R3c).
3. Phrasing sensitivity is real (0.9–4.6 % match across four phrasings; 67 % disagreement): a definition must carry its rules as text and its revision, and comparisons must pin the revision (R3).
4. Daily audit of a sample against a frontier judge; retune as a revision (R3e).
5. Issues and stumbles are disjoint catalogs; detection on a cadence with an "as of" stamp (R5, R5a).
6. Ignore reasons as data (not accurate / too broad / too specific) feed refinement (R5, R6b).
7. Per-project model isolation, matched by per-estate definitions and judges (R3).
8. A numeric score per match (probability) rather than a boolean (R3b).
9. Label signals that describe rather than grade (`OTHER`) — intents separate from quality (term map).
10. Phantom-event guard, payload caps with explicit truncation markers, asynchronous enrichment made visible (R1).
11. Cost with a coverage ratio: never quote a total over unpriced calls (R1 `cost`, R7 event stats).
12. Change attribution by commit identity (R7b).
13. A replay-server contract for agents that run outside the engine (R7a).
14. A normalization layer across SDK span shapes into `NormalizedLLMSpan` / `NormalizedToolSpan` (Workshop) — RRFlow's single flight vocabulary makes this unnecessary internally and necessary at the adapter edge (R1, D5).
15. REA: content-addressed evidence, untrusted-content provenance, an unknowns ledger, observation/interpretation/name layers, contract-first clean-room verification with a deliberately failing input (R9).

---

## 9. Decision queue (one per pass)

| # | Decision | Options | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| D0 | Term for Raindrop's "signal" in RRFlow | behaviour signal · lens · behaviour rule · verdict rule | behaviour signal — plain, scopes the H-05 collision away |
| D1 | Where generation and tool-call evidence lives | flight stage events (R1) · a new span record kind · derive from provider receipts only | flight stage events, payloads in the object tier |
| D2 | Evidence program language | rrflowQL + predicate (R3a) · sandboxed JS/Wasm like Raindrop · both | rrflowQL; Wasm functions exist if a predicate outgrows the query |
| D3 | Judge binding default | class 2 CPU classifier escalating to class 1 · class 1 only | class 2 with escalation; confidence floor is configuration |
| D4 | Who may promote a definition or finding | seat with Governance verdict · qualified policy for bounded auto-promotion · never automatic | seat now; policy later per the contract |
| D5 | Raindrop's place in the profile | class-7 `api` binding (export + read-back) · reference only · both | binding, so RRFlow is measured against production classifiers |
| D6 | Retention defaults for R1 payload families | per-family default + estate override · one estate-wide default | per family |
| D7 | Cohort verdict statistics | declared method in configuration (two-proportion interval as default) · adopt a library · leave to eval arms | declared configuration, method named in the verdict record |
| D8 | Term for REA-style outward loop | RROFLOW outward · "dissect" family · none yet | park until R1–R7 exist |

---

## 10. What this spec cannot claim

No behaviour signal can be minted today: flights carry no generations. No speed, recall or cost figure here is RRFlow's; every number is Raindrop's or REA's and is sourced in the ledgers. Live-workspace facts (classifier code shape, score semantics, issue grouping, review-panel counts) are pending capture; the P0 list is `sources/raindrop/live-capture-checklist.md`.

title: Keep your collector running
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# Keep your collector running

Implementation: development branch; native lifecycle verified in [PR #23](https://github.com/rrflow/rroflow-development/pull/23).
Public release and activation remain separate gates.
This does not confirm installation on your computer or deployment to Texas.

RROFLOW reads the Claude Code and Codex session folders linked on this computer.
It saves captured turns locally, then retries delivery to your signed-in account.
The startup option keeps this work running after you close the terminal.
It does not collect conversations from provider websites or phone apps.

## Set up once

Use a collector build containing `sources service`. The published older binary
may not include it. Sign in with `rroflow login`, then link your session folders
with `rroflow sources link`. Stop an existing foreground `sources run` first.

Run `rroflow sources service install` as your normal user. This starts collection
now and registers it for future logins. If you linked a custom store, use
`rroflow sources service --store "ABSOLUTE STORE PATH" install` instead, and pass
the same store for each command below.

Installation requires the saved login. Temporary `RROFLOW_INGEST_KEY`,
`RROFLOW_INGEST_URL`, and `RROFLOW_REDACT` overrides are refused because they would
not reliably survive a new login. Persist supported settings or use foreground
collection when those overrides are needed. Credentials are read from the saved
account file, never copied into task definitions or command lines.

## Check, pause, or remove

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `rroflow sources service status` | Shows whether startup is registered and its operating-system state. |
| `rroflow sources service stop` | Stops capture now; future login startup remains enabled. |
| `rroflow sources service start` | Starts the installed collector again. |
| `rroflow sources service remove` | Stops capture and removes automatic startup. Keeps captured data and your account. |

Open **Sources** in the dashboard to check the last report, delivery queue and
capture errors. A running task is not proof of successful delivery. Refresh the
dashboard to retrieve new reports. A missing or expired login pauses delivery;
local capture continues while the collector is running. Use `stop` to pause
capture too. Signing into a different account does not transfer the old queue.

## What survives closing a session

Windows uses a Task Scheduler task under your current user, with limited
privileges and no saved password. Closing the terminal or disconnecting RDP
leaves a logged-in user's collector running. Logging out stops this interactive
task; the next login starts it. This is not a machine-wide Windows service.

Linux uses a systemd user service. Keeping the user manager running after logout
or starting it at boot requires the host administrator's deliberate linger
configuration. Installation never enables linger or changes system services.
See [systemd user service behavior](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.service.html)
and [loginctl linger](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/loginctl.html).
Windows settings follow [Task Scheduler settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/new-scheduledtasksettingsset?view=windowsserver2025-ps).

## Upgrade and recovery

Installation pins a private copy of the current collector by SHA-256. Replacing
the original download does not silently replace the running collector. To
upgrade, remove startup, run `install` with the newer collector, then check
Sources. Retained journal data is replayed with its existing identities.

Each worker launch checks the pinned binary and linked source binding. Changed
manager definitions are refused rather than overwritten. Restore an edited
definition before removing it deliberately. A fatal worker failure has bounded
automatic retries; normal network failures stay in the delivery retry loop.
macOS startup registration is not implemented.

title: Dashboard experience: notes to implementation
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# Dashboard experience: notes to implementation

Date: 2026-10-27. Status: implemented on `codex/dashboard-experience`, based on
`codex/sdk-capture`. This records a dashboard increment, not a production launch.
The local serving process has not been replaced. Texas deployment and hosted
account activation remain unverified. No personal browser was controlled during
this increment; the checks below do not establish visual acceptance in a browser.
The follow-up `codex/dashboard-ui-verification` branch adds isolated browser tests
in CI; their reports must pass and their screenshots be reviewed before that
acceptance advances.

## What the user can do in this build

The workspace has seven focused destinations: Overview, Activity, Signals,
Sources, Learning, Settings, and Research & guides. The sidebar replaces the
previous long page of stacked sections. Small screens have a navigation drawer;
closed navigation is removed from keyboard focus. Appearance follows the device
or an explicit light/dark preference. There are no external scripts or fonts.

Activity has server-side search, agent/project/signal/session filters, a time
range and cursor pagination. The URL retains the view and filters for back/forward
navigation. Search covers captured prompt, response, model and session ID, not
uncaptured content or every tool payload. A turn opens in a native dialog with
Conversation, Tools, Signals and Details tabs. The session button opens that
session; a copied turn link still requires authorization to the same workspace.
Long tool traces initially render 50 calls, with explicit expansion.

Signal cards show the rule revision, summary and source evidence. Reviews persist
MATCH/NOT MATCH against the exact evidence digest. Settings persist through the
existing devspace API. Neither action silently activates a learned policy.

The research library includes the full text of every Markdown note under `docs/`,
including all eight Raindrop documents. It can be searched by title/path/category
and read in the dashboard without navigating away. Its generated inventory carries
SHA-256 fingerprints of canonical UTF-8/LF source text. CI detects a stale index.
The original notes are preserved; the library is a projection, not a new authority.

## Review of the existing 33 source notes

This was an inventory and targeted requirement review: product/experience notes
were read directly, while large historical ledgers were inspected by their
headings and relevant evidence sections. It is not a claim that every historical
statement was independently reverified. The complete source texts are retained
for inspection in the library.

| Existing notes | Consequence in this increment |
|---|---|
| `docs/README.md`, `plan/rroflow-ai-plan.md`, `plan/canon-alignment-notes.md`, `plan/capability-map.md` | Separate monitoring from the RRFlow engine; distinguish built capabilities from proposals; preserve source provenance. |
| `plan/browser-sign-in.md`, `plan/identity-and-devspaces.md` | Shippin sign-in is primary; devspace keys are an advanced preview path. Every data query remains account-scoped. |
| `plan/sdk-install-and-linking.md`, `plan/source-collection.md`, `plan/subscription-support.md` | Separate provider, app surface and execution machine. Received records are not proof of a live source. Grok SDK fixture coverage is not subscription-history support. |
| `plan/texas-readiness.md` | No cloud-ready or Texas-deployed badge without verified infrastructure and activation. The connection guide identifies unreleased development commands. |
| Raindrop `findings-brief.md`, `live-capture-checklist.md`, `live-capture-ledger.md`, `prototype-ledger.md` | Real captured turns and evidence are primary navigation. Empty states say what has not arrived. Counts name their scope; no invented activity or confidence. |
| Raindrop `signal-authoring-capture.md`, `source-ledger.md` | Plain-language signal summaries, inspectable evidence, revision-pinned verdicts and no automatic classifier rewrite after a label. |
| Raindrop `ux-onboarding-and-gating.md`, `ux-settings.md` | Friendly first-capture entry, visible settings and source limitations, light/dark/system themes. No fabricated quota or unlock meter. |
| `research/devpulse/devpulse-research-ledger.md` | Protect wallet/time, preserve unknown usage, distinguish content from metrics, and report observed truth. Spend remains explicitly unpriced. |
| `research/rea/rea-source-ledger.md`, `spec/mechanism-spec-v0.md`, `spec/automatic-datasets-v0.md` | Review leads toward consented datasets and evaluated learning. Clusters are candidates, not labels. Unimplemented jobs have no pretend action buttons. |
| `ux/vibe-coder-onboarding.md` | Progressive disclosure and first useful evidence. Its older payload-on proposal is superseded by the newer explicit content opt-in contract. |
| `platform/compute-and-data-workload-classification.md`, `platform/skills-and-routines-inventory.md` | Separate serving, capture and later dataset/training work. Do not imply training runs inside the dashboard process. |
| RRFlow `build-order.md`, `capability-study.md`, `definitions-and-schema-audit.md`, `development-salvage-assessment.md`, `merge-train-2026-10-19.md` | Engine research remains available but does not become RROFLOW account or monitoring UI authority. |
| RRFlow `public-site-build-order.md`, `site-video-pipeline.md` | The planned Astro public story site and Remotion explainers remain separate from this working Rust-served dashboard. |

## API and verification boundaries

`GET /v1/turns` adds literal `search`, RFC 3339 `since`, opaque `cursor`, and exact
`event` parameters. Unknown parameters and malformed navigation fail with 400.
Pages order by timestamp descending, then event ID ascending, with undated turns
last. Both stores use the same ordering and filter before limiting. Cursors are
positions, not authorization; the authenticated devspace always scopes the query.
This is not a snapshot export: concurrent edits to a turn's timestamp can change
its page position. Dataset snapshots need their own immutable contract.

The Rust tests exercise assets, authentication, account isolation, equal-time and
undated pagination, literal search, date filters and exact-event lookup. CI runs
the same scenarios against Postgres. The Node tests execute the shipped script
with an isolated DOM/fetch harness: navigation, auth state, late responses after
logout/filter changes, content escaping, exact-review writes, settings writes,
research access and bounded tool rendering. They are not screenshot or browser
layout tests. A responsive layout, focus treatment and tab semantics are present
in the implementation; visual and assistive-technology acceptance remains open.

The follow-up suite in `scripts/dashboard-ui/` exercises the actual server and
dashboard at desktop and phone widths using disposable fixture records. It checks
page reflow, keyboard interaction, persisted labels/settings, research navigation,
logout and automatically detectable WCAG A/AA issues, and retains screenshots for
review. It uses a fresh server/store in CI, never the private serving preview or
personal browser. Fixture screenshots are not evidence of real captured activity.
Manual visual/assistive-technology review and hosted sign-in remain separate gates.

The first rendered CI run passed eight of twelve scenarios. It exposed insufficient
contrast on light status badges; two pagination scenarios also failed because of
incorrectly encoded labels in the test. Corrections darken the accent, keep skip
navigation on visible content without changing the current route, and repair the
test labels. Screenshot review also moved the phone menu shadow to its open state
and arranged overview sources/signals beside recent activity instead of stretching
one short panel down the page. These changes require the follow-up CI result.

## Remaining product acceptance

- Activate a reviewed build and verify the UI against real records in the serving
  environment. The local process restart was previously rejected by automatic
  execution review with only “blocked by policy”; this is not missing user consent.
- Confirm Texas VM identity/access and implement a GitHub-built immutable hosted
  release, transactional activation, recovery, TLS and working Shippin login.
- Complete source installation/startup, live heartbeats and queue health, reliable
  hooks, retention/quotas and settings refresh. A finite capture pass is not an
  always-running service.
- Verify live provider integrations individually. Subscription ownership alone
  cannot establish observability of browser/mobile histories.
- Add server-enforced free/paid entitlements, validated pricing/plan limits,
  redaction editing and dataset consent. Then implement dataset revisions,
  supervised/unsupervised jobs and held-out reversible promotion.

These remain acceptance work. A clearer dashboard does not close them.

title: When the connection drops
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# When the connection drops

The session collector saves changed turns before uploading. SDK adapters likewise
acknowledge local storage separately from cloud delivery. An upload failure keeps
unacknowledged records queued; a retry uses their existing identities.

This development increment adds a saved delivery cooldown. Restarting the collector
or running another flush does not skip that wait. Ordinary failures use exponential
backoff with random variation: initially 5–10 seconds, increasing up to 150–300
seconds. A valid server `Retry-After` delay or HTTP date can require a longer wait.
See [HTTP Retry-After](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-retry-after).
This timing applies to uploads to RROFLOW, not calls to your AI provider.

## What you can check

Run `rroflow sources status` for session collection, or
`rroflow capture status --spool "YOUR SPOOL PATH"` for SDK recording. The `retry`
section shows `next_attempt_unix` (UTC seconds), attempts since the last success (including a reserved or in-progress attempt) and the last HTTP
status when available. Zero means no saved cooldown. A future time means delivery
is waiting; it does not mean captured work was deleted. `sources flush` and SDK
`capture.flush()` respect the same saved wait and return an error while deferred.

Session collection keeps scanning while delivery waits. Its managed worker retries
when eligible. The SDK recorder also accepts new events during the cooldown, but
an SDK flush remains an explicit attempt: the application must schedule another
flush after a deferred or failed one. Closing the application does not create a
background SDK uploader. The automatic session collector is a separate mechanism.

Source health requests share the session collector's cooldown. The dashboard may
therefore show an older report while the server asks the collector to wait. The
cloud cannot see an offline machine's newest local queue. This increment does not
add live retry-time display to the dashboard.

## Recovery rules

Only a verified receipt acknowledges records. Invalid receipts, account mismatch,
connection failures and HTTP errors retain the queue. The retry file contains
only counters, a deadline and an HTTP status, never tokens or captured text. It is
written atomically before an attempt so an interrupted process retains a cooldown.
A successful attempt clears it; malformed retry metadata fails closed rather than
silently resetting pacing. Accurate system time is required for saved deadlines.

This is not unlimited storage or proof of complete capture. Disk limits, retention,
large-backlog performance and every provider surface still need separate work.
Native fixture tests and release checks are the verification source for this
increment; they do not establish Texas deployment or personal account activation.

title: Public and member entry
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# Public and member entry

Status: implemented in development; hosted activation remains unverified.

Visitors land on `/`: a public explanation of activity, signals, evidence,
connections and the learning direction. `/app` contains the sign-in and member
workspace. Public browsing does not request private activity or identity. The
page has authored vector artwork, system fonts, no external runtime assets and
no invented usage figures. The artwork is explicitly an illustration.

`site/` is the Astro static authoring source chosen in the product plan. Run
`npm ci --ignore-scripts` then `npm run export` there to update the embedded
`public.html`, `public.css` and `public.js`. Do not edit those generated files.
CI runs `npm run verify` to reject drift. The Rust gateway serves all three from
the same immutable artifact as the API and workspace; deployment needs no Node
runtime. The existing dashboard stylesheet supplies the shared visual tokens.

## Account entry

`GET /auth/config` returns `enabled` and `member_origin` (null when disabled).
The latter is the already-validated canonical HTTPS browser origin, not a
request-supplied redirect. Public workspace links use that origin. The dashboard
sign-in link starts OAuth there so the browser binding cookie and callback share
a host. The callback finishes at `/app`, or `/app?signin=failed`. Tokens remain
server-side; this change does not alter ownership or credential acceptance.

Existing `/#activity?...` and other unambiguous workspace bookmarks move to
`/app#...`, preserving filters. `/#learning` now names the public learning
section; use `/app#learning` for the member destination. Copied turn links use
`/app`. The public page stays readable when sign-in configuration cannot load.

The member sidebar distinguishes verified account access from devspace-key
access and displays the returned name as text. The first-steps checklist uses
verified workspace access, received turn count and saved review history. Clicking
setup does not complete a step. Unavailable review history cannot count as a
completed review. The checklist opens for an empty workspace and collapses once
turns exist; the monitoring overview stays prominent. Private member context and
progress clear at logout. These milestones do not assert connection health or
complete provider coverage.

## Acceptance boundaries

The same gateway can expose public entry and member UI, but this does not make
the hosted service live. Real Nomen registration/sign-in, same-account collector
capture and two-account readback still need acceptance on the verified Texas VM.
Shippin-site's inspected MemberAccountPort/Supabase adapter is not a released
RROFLOW subscription contract. Free/paid entitlements, billing, self-service
credential management and retention controls remain separate unfinished work.
Automatic datasets, supervised training and unsupervised discovery remain
planned. Consumer subscription browser/mobile history is not automatically read.

Validation covers public and private route separation, disabled/configured auth
states, callback routing, unchanged tenant/session security, evidence-derived
onboarding, logout cleanup, desktop/phone reflow and accessibility. Browser tests
use disposable Rust-server fixture records. Canonical-origin UI tests supply
fixture configuration; identity exchange tests use a mock provider. Neither is
evidence of a live account or Texas deployment.

Astro implementation references: [static deployment](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/deploy/)
and [external scripts](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/client-side-scripts/).

title: A signal dashboard that leads to evidence
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# A signal dashboard that leads to evidence

Status: implementation in development, 2026-10-28. Hosted activation and complete
Raindrop/Sentry/PostHog parity are not established by this increment.

Open a signal from the library or choose a signal in Findings. The dashboard
shows matching turns, received turns in the same selection, and the share with
a recorded match. Agent, project, session, text and time filters apply to the
counts and evidence. A turn counts once even when it has repeated hits for the
same signal. Match share is neither classifier accuracy nor evaluation coverage:
the service cannot infer that a missing hit means a rule checked the turn.

The timeline shows up to the latest 30 UTC dates with received activity. Missing
calendar days do not establish inactivity. Earlier-date matches and undated
matches are counted separately and remain in the overall total. Selecting a day
sets inclusive start and exclusive end boundaries, clipped to the current range.
Undated records cannot satisfy a dated filter. Agent and project lists show the
top 12 groups, with omitted match counts. These limits bound presentation, not
the population used for totals. The paginated evidence list is a separate read;
ongoing ingestion can change records between the aggregate and evidence requests.

Choosing an agent, project or day preserves the other filters and resets pagination.
The URL holds the selection, so browser history and copied links keep context.
Advanced raw data remains in the turn inspector. A failed aggregate request shows
an unavailable state while retaining the evidence list; it never substitutes
first-page counts. Logout and navigation discard late responses and private totals.

The library includes captured signals without a current catalogue/definition under
Other recorded signals. Their evidence remains accessible, but they have no pause
or edit control because the service does not know their policy. Built-in and custom
signals keep their existing settings and immutable-definition behavior.

## API and storage

`GET /v1/signals/stats?signal=...` is authenticated. Optional filters are `agent`,
`project`, `session`, `search`, `since` and `until`. Unknown parameters, malformed
dates and reversed intervals are rejected. It returns `rroflow.signal-stats/v1`,
the owner, normalized scope, observation time, bounded breakdowns and complete
cohort counts. No prompt, response or tool payload is returned. `GET /v1/turns`
also accepts the exclusive `until` boundary for exact drill-down selection.

JSONL reads the owner's current in-memory index under its existing lock. Postgres
uses one statement snapshot with tenant predicates, signal existence checks and
grouping sets; ranking and truncation happen in SQL. A five-second statement
timeout bounds database work. No new schema or arbitrary query endpoint is added.
The API uses the current upserted turn revision, so replacement can change counts.
Saved review snapshots remain immutable in the separate review store.

Acceptance includes more-than-one-page histories, duplicate hits, missing dates,
bounded breakdown reconciliation, literal search, date boundaries, two owners,
replacement/restart, unavailable aggregates and late-response cleanup. Desktop
and phone tests follow signal → project → day → exact turn using the real Rust
fixture server. These tests are not a production load benchmark.

The [capability baseline](../plan/capability-map.md) tracks the remaining monitoring,
enterprise dataset and learning requirements. This screen does not publish a
dataset, measure held-out performance or activate a learned change.

title: Your monitoring workspace and signal library
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# Your monitoring workspace and signal library

Status: implementation on `codex/signal-workspace`, 2026-10-27. This is a review
build, not a claim of deployment or learning activation.

## Start with what matters

- **Overview:** activity received, signals worth looking at, and source history.
- **Findings:** the moments a rule picked out. Inspect the request, response and
  completed tools, then answer "Yes, this matches" or "No, it does not". The decision
  is tied to that exact captured revision. A match is not proof of failure.
- **Projects:** choose the project or folder you care about and open its activity.
- **Signal library:** browse built-in checks and organize your own rules in named
  groups. Filter by group, built-in/your signals, or a phrase in the description.
- **Datasets:** see the captured work and saved decisions that could support future
  datasets, and understand the permissions and evaluation steps still to build.
- **Improve:** the path from reviewing evidence to evaluated, reversible changes.

Raw IDs, provider fields and usage remain in the turn's Details tab. Research &
guides preserves the source notes, including the eight Raindrop documents.

## Create a signal without code

Choose **Signal library > Create a signal**. Give it a name and a group, then
choose one rule: a number of failed tools, a completed tool with a particular name,
a phrase in the message sent to the AI, or a phrase in its response. Limit it to
an agent or project if useful. Phrase matching is literal and ignores letter case;
no generated code, regular expression or model call runs.

**Try on recent activity** inspects up to 100 recent turns within the selected
agent/project scope. The result separates matches, checked turns, and turns whose
text was unavailable. Open a captured turn to inspect context. This is a preview,
not measured precision, and it changes no saved findings. You can save a rule even
when no recent examples match, after inspecting that result.

**Save and turn on** persists the rule and starts checking newly received turns.
Custom rules run on the server's received projection, so phrase checks require
opted-in, scrubbed uploaded text. Tool names and error counts need no prompt text.
The collector's built-in rules still evaluate locally before text is stripped.

**Pause** stops a custom rule from matching later arrivals. Existing findings stay
until their turn is re-sent; a re-sent turn is evaluated using current rules. No
history scan is silently started by saving. Saved review snapshots remain immutable
when capture changes. Definitions are immutable in this increment: create a new
signal to change a condition; pause the old one. Up to 32 definitions are supported.
Editing/version history and archiving are future usability work, not hidden buttons.

Built-in choices refresh in this collector version after successful delivery, at
most once per minute. Updated choices are cached durably for offline use and
reapplied on the next scan. Older collectors still need an upgrade/relink. Capture
continues when settings cannot refresh, using cached choices and reporting the
settings error separately. Closing a phone does not install or stop a source agent;
source startup and heartbeat acceptance remain separate work.

## Dataset and learning boundaries

The counts shown are received turns and the latest 1,000 saved decisions. They are
not counts of consented training rows. No dataset is published by this screen.
Supervised learning uses explicit corrections; unsupervised work proposes patterns
from eligible unlabelled examples. Neither starts from a click on a verdict.
Purpose-specific consent, fixed source snapshots, leakage-safe splits, durable
build jobs and held-out evaluation follow [automatic datasets v0](../spec/automatic-datasets-v0.md).
That contract remains the owner; the UI does not invent a training service.

## Contract and verification

`SignalConfig` adds defaulted `revision` and `custom` fields, using the existing
per-devspace settings stores; no new database or table is selected. Migration 0004
preserves existing built-in choices, adds default revision/custom fields and refuses
older Postgres writers that omit them. The changed migration fingerprint makes the
release activator refuse an unreviewed upgrade or downgrade across this boundary.
Take and verify a backup before migrating; restoring an older binary requires a
reviewed data restore, not bypassing that guard. JSONL deployments must obey the same
release boundary because their files have no database constraint. GET returns
the revision. PUT supplies the last-read revision, replaces the whole configuration
and returns the incremented revision. Stale writes receive 409. Old clients that
omit revision can write only the initial revision; they must GET before later writes.
JSONL serializes writes within the single service process; Postgres locks the owning
devspace row before comparing and writing. Multiple JSONL service processes over
one directory remain unsupported.

`POST /v1/signals/preview` accepts a bounded custom definition under the authenticated
account. Ingest owns the `custom_` namespace and discards submitted hits in that
namespace before computing current matches. Custom definitions keep version 1 and
are retained for interpreting evidence; only their enabled state can change.
Changing a rule needs a fresh identity. Saved reviews retain exact capture snapshots.

Acceptance covers isolated preview/ingest/restart, missing-text coverage, validation,
concurrent settings edits, collector cache identity/rollback refusal, and a real
server desktop/phone journey from creation through a new arrival, review and pause.
Fixture screenshots demonstrate UI behavior, not live provider coverage or Texas
activation. Full manual assistive-technology and real-user acceptance remain open.

title: Source reporting and queue health
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# Source reporting and queue health

The Sources page separates received agent history from reports sent by the
computer collecting sessions. A recent turn may be backfill; a quiet agent may
have no new turns. Neither is proof of connection health.

An updated `rroflow sources run` sends a small report after a scan, at most once
every 30 seconds. The page shows three states:

- **Reporting recently:** a report reached this service within two minutes.
- **Reporting with a problem:** a recent report includes capture errors or a
  failed delivery attempt. Check the collector output on that computer.
- **No recent report:** the collector may be stopped, disconnected or busy
  scanning. Displayed counts are its last report, not current queue measurements.

The report shows waiting turn revisions and bytes, last-scan error count, and the
last delivery check result. Queue details include the oldest waiting batch timestamp,
retained journal size, collector version and saved signal-settings revision.
The oldest timestamp comes from the local batch file's modification time; restored
or copied journals may change it. Retained bytes include acknowledged records.
Numbers describe this session collector, not SDK-only capture or browser chats.

Refresh fetches new reports. The visible report ages while the page remains open;
it cannot stay marked recent indefinitely. An unavailable health endpoint is shown
separately and does not hide received activity. Older collectors show no reports.
This is diagnostic visibility, not a completeness or uptime guarantee.

## Contract and recovery

Authenticated `POST /v1/sources/health` accepts `rroflow.source-health/v1`.
`GET /v1/sources/health` returns the account's latest source observations, server
time and the two-minute freshness window. Account identity comes from the
credential. The request cannot select a devspace. No prompt, response, local path,
hostname, credential or raw error message is included.

The source binding supplies a stable source ID. Under the existing process lock,
the collector atomically persists a strictly increasing report sequence in
`health.json` before sending. Restart continues that sequence. Unavailable delivery
does not delete queued turns; a failed health request cannot undo acknowledgements.
Offline runs do not access credentials or send reports. A single `--once` run
returns failure if capture, delivery or health reporting fails, with separate local
diagnostics. Continuous runs keep collecting and retrying.

Ingest keeps only the latest report per source. An identical replay preserves the
original receipt time; lower sequences and conflicting reuse receive 409. A new
sequence receives server time after the source write is serialized. Postgres locks
the devspace row; the JSONL store uses its single-process lock and an atomic file
replacement. This version supports at most 128 reporting sources per devspace as a
storage bound, not a billing tier. Source deletion/retirement UI remains future work.

Keep the binding, journal and health state together during recovery. Restoring an
older local health sequence causes refusal instead of falsely refreshing status.
Do not clone a bound source into two running collectors; link a separate source
store for a second machine. Damaged health state fails visibly and never resets
silently. This increment does not install automatic startup, enforce journal
retention/disk quotas, guarantee scan latency, or activate Texas.

Migration `0005_source_health.sql` adds the latest-observation table. Its migration
fingerprint changes the managed-release compatibility boundary. Back up and verify
the migration/restore procedure before activation; do not bypass the release guard
to run an older binary over a different migration fingerprint.

title: RROFLOW onboarding for vibe coders: plan v0
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# RROFLOW onboarding for vibe coders: plan v0

Date: 2026-10-25. Status: proposal. Nothing here is decided until it is saved as an ADR.
Evidence:
- `sources/raindrop/ux/*` (live captures 2026-10-24/25)
- this repo's `crates/rroflow-raindrop` (real traffic sent and read back)
- `claude/rrflow-public-site-build-order.md` (the rrflow.ai site plan; this document does not replace it)

## Who it is for
A **vibe coder** builds with a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and wants that agent to improve over time. They will not read a spec, and they will not write a classifier. If they ever paste a key, it is once. Success means the first useful signal shows up within 10 minutes of first contact, and the first governed improvement shows up within a day.

## What actually blocked us (this session, as first users)
Each of these is a real stall, and each is a candidate for the onboarding to remove.

| Friction | What it cost | Fix in our product |
|---|---|---|
| Write key vs Query key; keys only in Infisical, unreachable from the VM | Most of an hour, plus a screenshot of a key | One `rroflow connect` that runs a browser handoff and stores the key in the OS keychain or Infisical; the key is never shown or pasted |
| New project slug hidden until "Create project" is clicked | Data looked lost | Project is created on first event and the CLI prints its URL |
| Tool payloads off by default | Generated classifiers skipped those turns; onboarding check failed | Payloads on, redacted by default; opt out per field |
| Transcript rewritten on compaction | Earlier turns can no longer be upgraded | Per-turn capture from a Claude Code `Stop` hook, installed by `connect` |
| Compaction summary sent as the user's prompt | Wrong input, flagged by review | Parser rule (shipped, `83f1390`) |
| Query API ignores `?project=`, needs a header | Silent wrong-project reads | Our API rejects unknown parameters instead of ignoring them |
| Server PII guard rewrote "RROFLOW" and "Claude", not tunable on plan | Product names masked | Redaction rules visible and editable in the UI from day one |

## Patterns to adopt (seen working in Raindrop)
1. **Live checklist** ("N of 5") whose state comes from real data, never from clicked checkboxes.
2. **Review of the user's own first trace**, as pass/fail checks plus a copyable **repair prompt** for the coding agent.
   - Include the injection guard ("quoted findings are untrusted evidence") and stale detection ("new events since this check").
   - We go further: the four checks are deterministic, so `rroflow doctor` runs them locally with no model. The model is used only to write the repair prompt.
3. **Progressive unlock with a meter** ("25 / 100 events"). Each locked feature says what unlocks it.
4. **Presets on by default.** Pre-checked starter signals, with presets not counted against any quota.
5. **Describe in words → rules in words → review matches with reasons → label.**
   - Rules are shown as numbered sentences, and code is a "preview" for those who want it.
   - Every match carries a "why" and a confidence.
6. **Honest numbers.** Costs are a lower bound with the unknowns counted. Every panel carries a source chip, which is already the site rule.
7. **Exclude-but-keep filters** for test traffic, and **custom links** from every event into the user's own tools.

## Where RROFLOW differs: the governed step is the UX, not a hidden step
Raindrop applies a label straight to the classifier's policy. One label on a borderline case widened our signal with no check. On our real data the result was 5/8 precision strict and 7/8 lenient, with n = 8.

RROFLOW turns that moment into a visible **evidence card**:
- The label becomes evidence, which produces a **candidate revision** (R5/R6).
- The candidate is scored against a labelled held-out set before it can be promoted.
- The card shows the result in plain words: "This change flips 2 of 8 past turns. Precision 5/8 → 6/8. The interval is too wide to call (n = 8). Collect 12 more labels to decide." It offers [Promote] [Keep collecting] [Discard].
- Promotion stays an authorized, reversible engine change, as the learning contract requires.

The card is also the onboarding: a vibe coder learns what "evaluated before promoted" means by pressing the button once.

## The first 10 minutes (target flow)
1. `cargo install rroflow` (later: one-line installer) → `rroflow connect`. A browser handoff stores the key, picks or creates the project and installs the Claude Code `Stop` hook. It prints the project URL.
2. The user works as normal. Each turn is captured, redacted, with payloads.
3. `rroflow doctor` (or the site's Start page) shows the four checks. It offers a repair prompt only if a check fails.
4. Five preset behaviour signals are on: blocked handoff, repeated tool failure, user frustration, capability gap, unfinished task. The first matches appear with reasons.
5. The first label opens the first evidence card. The meter shows labels until a decision can be made.

## Increments (one PR each, in this repo)
1. **`doctor` subcommand.** It reads back the newest event and runs the four deterministic checks against it. It prints pass/fail and a repair prompt. Built and tested against our `claude-code` project.
2. **`connect` + `Stop` hook installer.** It writes the hook into `.claude/settings.json` for the chosen scope. The key reference lives in the keychain or Infisical, never a plaintext value.
3. **Preset behaviour-signal set** as data (`signals/presets.toml`). Each preset has rules in words and an evidence program, evaluated offline against our captured traffic with precision reported.
4. **Evidence-card prototype**, run against the Blocked Work Handoff labels we already have. It is a static artifact first, then a site Start-page panel.
5. **rrflow.ai Start page** in `site-development`. It is the checklist, the doctor results and the evidence card, all reading real data through the gateway. It follows the site plan's source-chip rule.

## Open decisions (one per pass)
- D-UX-1: the first increment. The recommendation is `doctor`, because it is cheap, testable now, and removes the most-hit friction class.
- D-UX-2: the hook scope default, either per project (`.claude/settings.json`) or per user (`~/.claude/settings.json`).
- D-UX-3: preset set names and the "behaviour signal" term (still D0 in the mechanism spec).

title: The visual workspace
description: Product experience requirements and their implementation boundaries.
text:
# The visual workspace

Implementation: `codex/visual-workspace`, building on the existing captured-turn,
signal and source-health APIs. This note describes the interface increment;
it is not evidence of Texas activation or a functioning hosted account flow.

## The experience the owner asked for

A person should understand what deserves a closer look without knowing what an
ingest pipeline, span or classifier is. The owner called the visual direction
"custom flat vector 2.0": fast, authored vector art, friendly navigation and
progressive detail, with contextual help and A2UI components and triggers.

The workspace now uses an evidence-derived headline and a next-action card.
The headline counts received signal matches, not failures or unique turns. The
card prefers an unreviewed finding in the newest 100 received turns, joins its
exact revision to saved reviews, and opens that turn's Signals tab. If review
history is unavailable, it does not call the finding unreviewed. Empty workspaces
offer a connection step; absence of findings never becomes an all-clear.

The signal library preserves built-ins, groups, search, preview-before-save and
pause controls. Source history remains distinct from collector reporting health.
The connection dialog first asks where the agent runs, then explains the next
step. Installation commands and development-build availability sit behind an
explicit disclosure. This guide does not silently install anything or provision
an account. SDK support is instrumented-call capture, not subscription history.

## Authored visual system

`dashboard.css` owns semantic surface, text, accent, border and illustration-area
colors, mapped separately for light and dark appearance. Components consume those
roles. `dashboard.html` owns an inline SVG symbol set and three small illustrative
scenes: capture flow, a signal lens and a source connection. Illustrations have
fixed palettes, use no external images or fonts, and are hidden from assistive
technology because the adjacent text carries their meaning. They are conceptual
art, never diagrams claiming a particular source is connected.

The interface uses warm paper, graphite, sage, lime, lilac and apricot; rounded
surfaces; restrained offset depth in vector art; and a consistent stroke icon
set. Mobile reduces the hero artwork so the next action remains visible. Motion
is limited to short nonessential transitions and respects reduced-motion settings.
The total HTML/CSS/JS shell is tested below 150 KiB raw and 40 KiB when gzip-sized.
The gzip check is a size benchmark, not a claim that the server compresses responses.
Research text is fetched only when its destination is opened.

Authored files are HTML, CSS, dashboard JavaScript, the A2UI adapter and this note.
`research.json` remains generated by `scripts/index-research.mjs`; never edit it by
hand. No token compiler, UI framework, external font or art runtime was added.

## Controlled A2UI interactions

The authority is Shippin's `contracts/a2ui/v1/` at umbrella revision `e96d6f8`,
schema `shippin.a2ui.v1`. The product owns a narrow renderer in
`dashboard-a2ui.js`, catalog `rroflow.workspace.v1`, surface `rroflow.workspace`.
There is no filesystem import from the umbrella repository.

Registered targets:

| Target | Accepted actions | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.views` | `view.select` | Select one of ten authored workspace routes |
| `workspace.guide` | `coachmark.show`, `focus.set` | Open plain-text help or focus the guide control |

Local UI triggers produce ordered envelopes. The renderer checks exact object
fields, actor, surface, IDs, action values and target allowlists. It rejects
replays and out-of-order mutations without applying them. Text is assigned with
`textContent`. No envelope can invoke JavaScript, inject markup, navigate to an
arbitrary URL, select arbitrary DOM, save a signal or submit a verdict.

This is a local-operator adapter, not a remote provider-agent transport or a
general model-generated component renderer. Provider-agent actors are rejected.
Authenticated transport, per-action permissions and a broader component catalog
need their own implementation and validation before external agents can drive UI.
Session-local adapter state is cleared at logout.

## Interaction and verification

Help is available from the workspace guide, source and library introductions,
and next-action explanations. Hover/focus tooltips also open full explanations
on click or Enter, including touch. Escape dismisses tooltips. Native modal dialogs
contain focus, close with Escape, and return focus to their opener. Existing turn
details retain keyboard tabs and advanced source/tool/revision detail.

`scripts/test-dashboard.mjs` covers account clearing, evidence identity, unavailable
reviews, empty states, bounded asset size, A2UI validation/replay/order and guidance
actions. `scripts/dashboard-ui` runs the actual compiled service with temporary
fixture data on desktop and phone, checks reflow and automatic WCAG issues, and
captures overview, library, evidence, connection, help and dark appearance images.
Screenshots are explicitly fixture evidence, never the owner's activity.

Automatic accessibility checks and developer visual review do not substitute for
the owner's judgment of this visual direction or for assistive-technology testing.
Automatic datasets, training, paid-tier enforcement and Texas activation remain
separate acceptance work.
